guide.title: AAC files and FLAC output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AAC file?

Advanced Audio Coding, or AAC, is a lossy, perceptual audio coding family standardized through MPEG. It is specified in MPEG-2 Part 7 and placed in MPEG-4 Part 3. AAC can sit in MP4, QuickTime or other wrappers, and a standalone .aac file commonly carries ADTS framing. The media type audio/aac covers ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport. LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2 are among its profiles, and it serves streaming and delivery to listeners.

### Programs that open AAC files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player reads raw AAC files and decodes MPEG-4 AAC.
- FFmpeg decodes AAC and also has its own AAC encoder.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Audition imports AAC, including HE-AAC.

### AAC and FLAC compared

FLAC squeezes integer PCM audio and throws no samples away. It supports one through eight channels, carries metadata such as seek points, pictures and Vorbis comments, and uses the audio/flac media type. RFC 9639 standardized its description in December 2024. FLAC is an open, royalty-free codec developed by Xiph.Org, and people use it for music archiving, audiophile listening and lossless backups of CDs.

This page decodes the AAC and writes FLAC with FFmpeg in your browser, without a picture stream. The FLAC is lossless only from the point of decoding. The page has no settings, and a batch yields one FLAC per AAC.

### Other ways to convert AAC to FLAC

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i speech.aac -vn -c:a flac speech-decoded.flac`. With `-vn` no video stream is written, and `-c:a flac` picks the FLAC encoder.
- **VLC:** choose Media > Convert/Save, add the AAC, click Convert, pick the Audio - FLAC profile, set a .flac destination and click Start.

### Problems with AAC files

- **The sound is not as good as hoped**: a lossy AAC already lost detail, and changing it to FLAC cannot recreate the samples that were removed.
- **A decoder rejects it**: an MPEG-2 AAC decoder may not follow the MPEG-4 variants.
- **Renaming did nothing**: giving the file an .m4a name leaves the ADTS framing as it was; no MP4 wrapper appears.
- **The decoded file is much larger**: once decoded, the audio can need far more space than the compressed original did.

guide.title: AI files and TIFF output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

AI is Adobe Illustrator's native artwork format. Inside it sit vector paths, shapes, text and effects arranged in layers and artboards, and pixel images can sit among the vector objects. Illustrator 9 changed the format in 2000, and earlier files used PostScript. This page reads the PDF rendition that the PDF-compatible saving option stores next to the Illustrator data. Logos, illustrations and print layouts are typical AI source files.

### Programs that open AI files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ImageMagick reads AI as Illustrator CS2. That is rendering, not Illustrator editing.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Illustrator opens native artwork with its editable objects.

**Linux:**

- Inkscape imports AI artwork from Illustrator 9.0 onward, and some document features may be unavailable.

### AI and TIFF compared

TIFF is a tag-based raster wrapper developed by Aldus and Microsoft. Revision 6.0 appeared in 1992, and Adobe now controls the specification. Compression methods and color representations vary between TIFFs, and one file can hold several images, as in a scanned page sequence. Its extensions are .tif and .tiff, with the media type image/tiff.

Here PDF.js draws each page of the PDF inside the AI, and the pixels are written as a TIFF on an opaque white background. Each page is drawn at up to double its size, and a very large artboard is scaled down to stay within a pixel budget of about 16.8 megapixels. Every page is a separate file with no ZIP, named name_page1, name_page2 and so on. You can choose several AI files at once, and they run one after another. The page sets no print resolution, so artwork meant for a printer's dpi spec should be exported from Illustrator. A file with no PDF inside fails with a message telling you to resave it with Create PDF Compatible File turned on.

### Other ways to convert AI to TIFF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -density 300 artwork.ai artwork.tiff`. The -density option sets the canvas resolution used when a vector format is rendered to a raster image.

### Problems with AI files

- **No PDF inside**: other software can fail on an AI that lacks its PDF-compatible representation. Resave it from Illustrator with that option on.
- **Not editable afterwards**: reading the embedded PDF gives no native Illustrator objects, so the AI stays your editable master.
- **Missing links**: a linked image stays outside the file unless Include Linked Files was ticked when saving, so the TIFF can lack it.
- **Older Illustrator versions**: opening artwork in an older version can cause compatibility problems, so match or exceed the saving version.
- **Blurry when enlarged**: the TIFF is pixels, so render again at the size you need.
- **Layers are gone**: the TIFF is flattened.

guide.title: Understanding AIFF for FLAC output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFF file?

Audio Interchange File Format came from Apple and descends from the IFF wrapper created at Electronic Arts. In its common form the file holds uncompressed linear PCM plus optional chunks naming the author, copyright and annotations, and studios often keep masters in it. A compressed variant, AIFF-C, extends the family to other encodings. Common media-type labels are audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.

### Programs that open AIFF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity brings in nearly any AIFF, PCM variants included, and FFmpeg both reads and writes the format.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Audition handles uncompressed AIFF plus the common compressed kinds.

### AIFF and FLAC compared

- **Size**: AIFF is large, since PCM is uncompressed. FLAC compresses the same samples without loss.
- **Fidelity**: both keep every sample when the AIFF holds PCM.
- **Video**: neither is meant for it, and the page discards any video stream.
- **Metadata**: AIFF uses chunks. FLAC relies on Vorbis comments and may embed cover art.
- **Openness**: FLAC's specification is open, and its reference encoder comes from Xiph.

The page runs `-acodec flac -vn` in FFmpeg, so the audio is encoded as FLAC and any video is dropped. Stream choice and tags follow FFmpeg's defaults.

### Other ways to convert AIFF to FLAC

- **flac:** run `flac session.aiff` with the Xiph reference encoder. It reads linear PCM AIFF with 4 to 32 bits per sample, not A-law or mu-law, and writes session.flac in place of the .aiff ending.
- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i take.aiff -c:a flac take.flac` on the command line.
- **Audacity:** open the AIFF, choose File > Export Audio, pick FLAC, and set 16-bit or 24-bit and a compression level from 0 to 8.

### Problems with AIFF files

- **The conversion fails**: the file may be an AIFF-C that uses a compression type FFmpeg cannot decode.
- **You expected better sound**: FLAC cannot restore detail that a lossy step removed before the recording became an AIFF.
- **The author looks misplaced**: Audition may list an AIFF's author under Dublin Core: Creator rather than Author.
- **A file over 4 GB**: AIFF stores its length in 32 bits, so very large files are malformed.

guide.title: AIFF files and M4A output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFF file?

Apple developed the Audio Interchange File Format in 1988 on top of the IFF container. It usually stores uncompressed PCM audio, so it is lossless and large, with metadata chunks. It serves for macOS audio production and professional sound editing.

### Programs that open AIFF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Audacity brings in AIFF recordings, every PCM variant included, with no extra library.
- VLC media player opens AIFF.
- FFmpeg includes both AIFF encoding and decoding.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Audition opens uncompressed AIFF and most compressed variants.

**Mac:**

- Apple Music and Logic Pro open it.

### AIFF and M4A compared

An M4A is audio only, stored in the MPEG-4 container. It usually holds AAC, or lossless Apple Lossless (ALAC), and it supports tags and cover art. It is widely supported, and is the usual form for podcasts and music from the Apple stores.

FFmpeg runs in your browser here with `-acodec aac -b:a 192k -vn`, which writes AAC at 192 kbps and drops any video stream. The result is lossy and far smaller than the AIFF. Choose several AIFF files and each is encoded in turn into a separate M4A. No sample rate or channel setting is passed, so there is no control for either. Before you delete the AIFF, play the M4A through once, because AAC discards some detail.

### Other ways to convert AIFF to M4A

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i master.aiff -c:a aac -b:a 192k listening-from-aiff.m4a`.
- **Audacity:** after installing the optional FFmpeg library, open the AIFF, then File > Export Audio and M4A (AAC) Files (FFmpeg). Its AAC export has a quality setting for the bit rate.

### Problems with AIFF files

- **A huge file**: PCM audio takes up space by design, so size alone does not mean damage.
- **Lossless is required**: AAC discards detail, so keep the AIFF as the master.
- **Tracks sound different**: AAC is lossy, so compare the M4A with the AIFF before deleting anything.
- **You need an editable file**: edit the AIFF first and convert last.
- **Metadata**: AIFF carries metadata chunks, so look at the tags in your player after converting.

faqs.question: Which AU encodings work?
faqs.answer: According to the specification, AU can hold ADPCM, floating point, A-law, mu-law or linear PCM data. In tests with this page's FFmpeg, AU files holding mu-law, A-law, 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit floating point samples all converted.

faqs.question: How good is the MP3?
faqs.answer: The page asks the encoder for 192 kbit/s, which MP3 cannot reach below a 32 kHz sample rate. At 16 to 24 kHz the encoder writes at most 160 kbit/s, and at 8 kHz about 64 kbit/s. You cannot pick a bitrate here.

faqs.question: Does converting AU to MP3 lose quality?
faqs.answer: MP3 compression is lossy, so the MP3 is not identical to the AU's samples. Keep the AU if you need them exactly.

faqs.question: Why does my AU sound thin?
faqs.answer: Eight-bit mu-law is common in AU files, and IANA's audio/basic definition describes it at 8 kHz, a narrow telephone rate. The page does not change the sample rate, so the MP3 keeps the source's rate.

faqs.question: Can I convert an Audacity project?
faqs.answer: Not as a whole. Old Audacity projects stored audio in small AU block files, and one block does not carry the arrangement stored in the project file. Open the project in Audacity and export from there.

faqs.question: Can I convert several AU files at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select several AU files together; the page processes them in order and gives one MP3 per file.

faqs.question: Is my audio uploaded?
faqs.answer: No. FFmpeg runs in the page and the AU is not uploaded.

faqs.question: What is the MP3 called?
faqs.answer: It keeps the AU's name with an .mp3 ending, so interview.au downloads as interview.mp3. The AU itself is not touched.

guide.title: About AU files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AU file?

AU is a simple audio format from Sun Microsystems, also called Sun or NeXT audio. Sun's published specification describes a fixed header, an annotation area and the audio samples. A file starts with the four-byte signature .snd. In the header you find the encoding, the sample rate and the number of channels, and multibyte numbers are big-endian.

The defined encodings include linear PCM, mu-law, A-law, floating point and ADPCM. Eight-bit mu-law is often used. People meet AU as Unix and Java system sounds and as legacy audio.

FFmpeg uses audio/basic as the media label for its Sun AU writer. IANA's audio/basic definition describes mono eight-bit mu-law at 8 kHz, which is narrower than the full set of AU encodings.

### Programs that open AU files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Audacity: imports AU audio without adding the optional FFmpeg library.
- Praat: reads supported NeXT and Sun encodings with Read from file.

### AU and MP3 compared

- **Structure**: an AU is a short header followed by samples. An MP3 is a stream of lossy compressed audio.
- **Compression**: AU data is often mu-law or PCM. MP3 is always lossy.
- **Metadata**: AU keeps notes in an annotation area, while MP3 relies on ID3 tags.
- **Reach**: nearly every device plays MP3. AU is handled by Audacity, VLC media player and QuickTime Player.

The page decodes the AU with FFmpeg and encodes the result with its LAME MP3 encoder.

### Other ways to convert AU to MP3

- **Audacity:** open the AU with File > Open or File > Import > Audio, check that it plays, then choose File > Export Audio and pick MP3 in the Format list.
- **FFmpeg:** run ffmpeg -i interview.au -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 128k interview-listen.mp3. FFmpeg lists Sun AU among the formats it reads.

### Problems with AU files

- **An old Audacity project is silent**: such a project needs its associated audio files in the places it expects them.
- **More than two channels**: the specification allows more than two interleaved channels, but some applications cannot handle them.
- **Clipping after a Praat export**: Praat's Sun export quantizes samples to 16-bit mono, so keep amplitudes below one.

infoArticle.title: About audio and video transcription
infoArticle.markdown:
Audio to Text transcribes speech from audio or video files. Uploaded files are processed in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser for transcription. YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud, and other webpage links are not supported right now. The speech model downloads on first use and runs locally.

This tool is best for interviews, meetings, lectures, and voice notes. Larger files take longer to process and may use more memory.

**Why use this tool**

- Handles uploads or direct links to audio and video files.
- Creates a plain text transcript you can edit or share.
- Works with common audio and video formats.

faqs.question: Do my files get uploaded?
faqs.answer: Uploads are processed locally in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser. The model files are downloaded when needed.

faqs.question: Which file types are supported?
faqs.answer: Common audio and video formats like MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, and M4V.

faqs.question: Can I use YouTube or SoundCloud links?
faqs.answer: Not right now. YouTube, SoundCloud, TikTok, and other webpage links are not supported. Upload the audio or video file, or paste a direct link to one.

faqs.question: Why is the first run slower?
faqs.answer: The speech model downloads the first time you run the tool. After that it is cached for faster use.

faqs.question: What does the output look like?
faqs.answer: You get a plain text transcript (.txt) that you can download or copy.

faqs.question: Does it just copy the video into an M4V?

faqs.question: Is M4V different from MP4?

guide.title: AVI files and M4V output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

AVI, Audio Video Interleave, is a RIFF-based container that Microsoft introduced in 1992. It interleaves video with audio and can carry many codecs. It turns up as older Windows video, in camera or capture output, and in archives; modern features are poorly supported.

### Programs that open AVI files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- mpv plays AVI and lets you pick the audio track.
- ffplay plays it.
- Adobe Premiere imports AVI when the decoder is available.

**Mobile:**

- The VLC apps on Android and iOS play AVI on phones.

### AVI and M4V compared

M4V is a video format developed by Apple that is very close to MP4, with H.264 video and AAC audio. HandBrake treats .m4v and .mp4 outputs as the same container. Files from the iTunes Store may carry FairPlay DRM. iTunes and the Apple TV app use it for videos, and so do phones and tablets.

This page runs FFmpeg in your browser. It re-encodes the video as H.264 at CRF 30 with the ultrafast preset and the sound as AAC at 96 kbps, with the index placed first in the file. A filter deinterlaces frames flagged as interlaced, a picture bigger than 1920 px on a side is shrunk to fit, and no more than 30 frames a second are kept. Width and height are then rounded down to even numbers, and a video inside those limits otherwise keeps its size and rate. A batch of AVI files is encoded in turn, one M4V each.

### Other ways to convert AVI to M4V

- **FFmpeg encode:** run `ffmpeg -i archive.avi -c:v libx264 -crf 19 -c:a aac -f mp4 delivery.m4v`. The `-f mp4` picks MP4 packaging for the .m4v name.
- **FFmpeg copy:** run `ffmpeg -i archive.avi -c copy -f mp4 copied.m4v`. The `-c copy` option leaves the streams unchanged instead of re-encoding them.

### Problems with AVI files

- **An old codec**: some players and decoders lack support for older AVI codecs.
- **Sound out of sync**: check the whole clip, not only the opening seconds.
- **Larger than expected**: the page sets no target size, so check the result against your needs.
- **Looks softer than the AVI**: this page trades detail for speed, so use FFmpeg with a lower CRF for archival quality.

guide.title: About AVI and MPEG
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

AVI arrived with Windows 3.1, and Microsoft's first specification is from 1992. It stores timed pictures and sound inside a RIFF file, where FOURCC codes name each stream's codec, the header notes dimensions and frame rate, and a separate chunk holds the media. The video inside may be uncompressed, lossless or lossy, which means the extension reveals nothing about quality. You find it in video production archives and older desktop workflows.

### Programs that open AVI files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay uses FFmpeg's demuxer to play AVI. mpv plays it on the desktop and lets you pick audio and subtitle streams.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports the AVI container.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is free, and the iOS version plays most movie files on iPhone and iPad.

### AVI and MPEG compared

- **What they are**: AVI is a container. The MPEG written here carries MPEG-2 video, a codec made for television that DVDs also use, together with MP2 audio.
- **Streams**: MPEG packs coded picture, sound and data into separate streams that are cut into packets.
- **Extensions and media types**: .avi is labeled video/x-msvideo. .mpeg and .mpg both name MPEG video, for which the Library of Congress records video/mpeg.

The converter decodes the AVI and encodes MPEG-2 video with a quality scale rather than a bitrate target, plus MP2 audio at 96 kbps. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced first, and because the compression is lossy, the result is a fresh encode rather than a copy of the source.

### Other ways to convert AVI to MPEG

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i capture.avi capture.mpeg`. FFmpeg reads AVI, and the .mpeg ending tells it to write an MPEG program stream.
- **Prism (Windows):** run `prism.exe -convert "C:\Media\capture.avi" -format .mpg`. Prism lists AVI as an input and MPG as an output. It offers no completion message, so check its window yourself.

### Problems with AVI files

- **Picture missing, sound present**: an editor can recognize AVI without having the decoder for its contents.
- **Very large captures**: original AVI size restrictions differ from the later OpenDML extension, so big captures need compatible software.
- **Wrong shape or striped motion**: aspect ratio and scan-type metadata are not handled consistently across AVI implementations.

guide.title: Understanding AVIF for BMP output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

AVIF stands for AV1 Image File Format. Its specification was written by the Alliance for Open Media, which was founded in 2015 for royalty-free media formats, and the format stores AV1-coded pictures inside a HEIF container. A file can use lossy or lossless compression, hold transparency or an image sequence, and reach twelve bits per channel for HDR and wide-gamut color. It can also carry Exif, XMP and an ICC profile. Most people meet AVIF as small images on websites.

### Programs that open AVIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - GIMP: imports and exports AVIF since version 2.10.22.
  - ImageMagick: reads AVIF files.
- **Web:**
  - Google Chrome: version 85 added AVIF decoding.
  - Mozilla Firefox: version 93 added AVIF image support.
- **Mobile:**
  - Android: AVIF decoding starts with version 12.
  - Safari: on iOS 16 it added still AVIF images.

### AVIF and BMP compared

- **Names and types**: .avif is image/avif and .bmp is image/bmp.
- **Compression**: AVIF is compact. A BMP commonly keeps its pixels raw, with an optional lossless run-length scheme, so the file is bulky.
- **Color**: a BMP stores between one and 32 bits for each pixel.
- **Use**: BMP turns up in Windows screen captures, system graphics and simple pipelines that want plain pixels.

Your browser handles the AVIF side, and ImageMagick encodes the BMP from the pixels. An animated AVIF gives frame one, and embedded metadata is left behind.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to BMP

- **GIMP:** GIMP 2.10.22 and later open AVIF. Open the file, choose File > Export As and save it as BMP. In the BMP export dialog, run-length encoding is available for indexed and grayscale images only, writing color space information is on by default and can be switched off for programs that can't read it, and an RGB format list sets the layout for other images.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **A browser shows nothing**: older browsers can fail to show AVIF, which is why sites keep a JPEG, PNG or WebP fallback. This converter also needs a browser that can decode AVIF.
- **GIMP refuses it**: releases older than 2.10.22 lack the AVIF importer.
- **Android depth**: handsets and tablets decode baseline 8-bit AVIF, and 10-bit decoding is optional.
- **Slow opening**: decoding an AVIF is slow, and encoding can take several seconds per image.

guide.title: Understanding AVIF to ICO
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

AVIF, short for AV1 Image File Format, was created by the Alliance for Open Media. It stores AV1-compressed pictures in the HEIF container and supports lossy and lossless compression, transparency, HDR and up to 12 bits per channel. It is royalty-free, and an Exif block, XMP or an ICC color profile can be embedded. Version 1.0.0 of the specification is dated 19 February 2019.

### Programs that open AVIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP can import and export AVIF from version 2.10.22. ImageMagick also reads AVIF.
- **Windows:** to view .avif files in the system you need the HEIF Image Extension plus Microsoft's AV1 Video Extension.
- **Web:** Chrome 85 and Firefox 93 added AVIF display.
- **Mobile:** Safari on iOS 16 gained still-image support, and Android 12 or newer decodes baseline 8-bit AVIF.

### AVIF and ICO compared

ICO is Microsoft's icon format. One file can contain bitmap images in several sizes and color depths, as PNG or bitmap entries with alpha transparency, and browsers also use it for favicons. AVIF is built for small web images and HDR, while ICO is built for icons.

Here the browser decodes the AVIF first, and then the page writes one image into the ICO. A side over 256 pixels is shrunk to fit inside 256 by 256 with its aspect ratio kept, and an image of exactly 256 pixels goes into the ICO as an embedded PNG. GIMP's own ICO export can save each icon size at its own color depth, or as compressed PNG, which not every program reads.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to ICO

- **GIMP:** use File > Open on the AVIF, then File > Export As and save it as an ICO, reviewing the icon options for each size.
- **libavif and GIMP:** `avifdec artwork.avif decoded.png` makes a PNG, which you open in GIMP and export as ICO.

### Problems with AVIF files

- A website should offer a fallback picture, since some browsers cannot display AVIF.
- GIMP gained its AVIF importer in 2.10.22, so earlier releases cannot open these files.
- Creating an AVIF can take several seconds, and opening one is slow too.

Your browser must be able to open AVIF files for this page to work.

guide.title: About AVIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

AVIF, the AV1 Image File Format, stores pictures compressed with the AV1 video codec inside a HEIF container, the same container family iPhone photos use. It comes from the Alliance for Open Media, a group founded in 2015 to build royalty-free media formats, which published AV1 in 2018. Version 1.0.0 of the AVIF specification is dated 19 February 2019.

AVIF can be lossy or lossless, keep transparency, hold image sequences and store up to 12 bits per channel for HDR and wide color gamut. The cost is speed: AVIF images are slow to decode, encoding one can take several seconds, and they don't draw progressively while loading.

An AVIF image sequence can stand in for an animated GIF at a fraction of the size. You mostly find AVIF on the web, where sites send it to browsers that can show it. Save such a picture and you get an .avif file that many editors, upload forms and older devices can't use.

### Programs that open AVIF files

**Windows**

- Photos: shows AVIF once the AV1 Video Extension and the HEIF Image Extension are installed from the Microsoft Store.
- GIMP: imports and exports AVIF from version 2.10.22, released in October 2020.

**Mac**

- GIMP: the same AVIF support as on Windows.
- ImageMagick: converts AVIF from Terminal.

**Linux**

- GIMP: the main desktop editor for AVIF.
- avifdec: the command-line decoder that ships with libavif.

**Web**

- Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16.1+ and Edge 121+ display AVIF. This page relies on that support, since your browser does the decoding.

**Mobile**

- Android: decodes AVIF from Android 12.
- Phone browsers: current Chrome on Android and Safari on iPhone show AVIF pages.

### AVIF and JPG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avif with image/avif; .jpg or .jpeg with image/jpeg.
- **Compression**: AVIF uses AV1's intra-frame coding, lossy or lossless. JPEG cuts the picture into 8x8 blocks, and its baseline mode is always lossy.
- **Color depth**: AVIF goes up to 12 bits per channel, with HDR and wide gamut. JPEG stores 8 bits per channel.
- **Transparency**: AVIF has an alpha channel. JPG has none.
- **Sequences**: AVIF can hold an animation. A JPG holds one frame.
- **Size**: in AVIF's Baseline profile one AV1 image is at most 8,192 x 4,352 pixels, and a larger picture is stored as a grid of such tiles. A JPEG can measure up to 65,535 pixels a side.
- **Loading**: a progressive JPEG shows a coarse version first and sharpens. AVIF appears only once decoded.
- **Licensing**: AVIF is royalty-free, and JPEG's US patents expired in 2006.
- **Metadata**: both carry Exif, XMP and an ICC profile; this converter keeps none of them.

The JPG gives up AVIF's small file and extra color precision in return for reach: almost every program, device and upload form takes it. This page decodes the AVIF with your browser and writes the JPG at quality 0.85.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to JPG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: open the AVIF in version 2.10.22 or later, choose File > Export As, name the file with .jpg and click Export.
- **ImageMagick (command line)**: run `magick input.avif output.jpg`.
- **avifdec from libavif (command line)**: run `avifdec input.avif output.jpg`. The `-q` option sets the JPEG quality, 90 by default. Only the first frame of a sequence is decoded unless `--index` names another frame, or all of them.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **"This browser can't open … files"**: your browser has no AVIF decoder. Update it, or switch to Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16.1+ or Edge 121+.
- **Windows Photos shows nothing**: add the AV1 Video Extension and the HEIF Image Extension.
- **A big image takes a while**: AVIF decodes slowly by design, so give a large file a moment.
- **See-through areas are lost**: JPG has no alpha channel. The [AVIF to PNG converter](/avif-to-png/) keeps transparency.
- **An animation gives one picture**: a JPG holds a single frame, so only the first is kept.
- **Changed the ending by hand**: an AVIF renamed to .jpg still holds AV1 data, and JPEG readers reject it.
- **An upload form says the file type isn't allowed**: many forms list only JPG, PNG and GIF. Upload the JPG made here instead.

guide.title: About AVIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

Most AVIF files people want to convert were saved from a web page. Image services and content delivery networks send AVIF to browsers that support it because the files are small, so a picture that looked ordinary on a site lands on disk as .avif and then won't go into a slide deck, an older editor or an upload form.

Underneath, AVIF, the AV1 Image File Format, is HEIF: a structure of boxes that holds image items and their properties. Each picture is compressed with AV1, the royalty-free video codec the Alliance for Open Media released in 2018, and version 1.0.0 of the AVIF specification followed on 19 February 2019.

Transparency gets an item of its own. The alpha plane is coded as a separate auxiliary image tied to the main picture, which is how an AVIF logo or cut-out keeps soft, partly see-through edges. A file can also hold an image sequence, Exif, XMP and an ICC profile, at up to 12 bits per channel. Decoding all of this is slow, and an AVIF appears only once it is fully decoded instead of sharpening as it loads.

### Programs that open AVIF files

**Windows**

- Edge and Chrome: open an .avif dragged into a tab, with no add-ons.
- Photos: needs two Microsoft Store add-ons, the HEIF Image Extension and the AV1 Video Extension, before it shows AVIF.
- GIMP: reads and writes AVIF from release 2.10.22.

**Mac**

- Safari, Chrome and Firefox: view AVIF files.
- ImageMagick: turns an AVIF into a PNG with one Terminal command.

**Linux**

- GIMP and ImageMagick: open and convert AVIF.
- avifdec: libavif's own decoder, which can write a 16-bit PNG.

**Web**

- Current versions of every major browser: Chrome from 85, Firefox from 93, Safari from 16.1 and Edge from 121.

**Mobile**

- Android: AVIF decoding is built in from Android 12.
- iPhone and iPad: Safari shows AVIF on current iOS versions.

### AVIF and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avif with image/avif; .png with image/png.
- **Compression**: AVIF codes each picture with AV1's still-image tools, with or without loss. PNG filters every row of pixels and packs it with DEFLATE, never losing anything.
- **Transparency**: both have a full alpha channel. AVIF keeps it as an auxiliary image beside the picture; PNG stores it with every pixel. This converter keeps it.
- **Bit depth**: AVIF reaches 12 bits per channel and PNG up to 16, but the PNG made here has 8 bits per channel, so HDR and extra depth don't survive.
- **File size**: for a photo, a PNG is often several times the size of the AVIF. For flat graphics the gap is smaller.
- **Animation**: an AVIF can be an image sequence; this page converts its first frame only.
- **Metadata**: AVIF can carry Exif, XMP and an ICC profile. None of them is copied into the PNG.
- **Support**: nearly every program opens PNG. AVIF needs a fairly recent browser, viewer or editor.

Choose PNG when you need transparency, crisp edges or a file you will edit and save again. For photos you only want to share, the [AVIF to JPG converter](/avif-to-jpg/) gives a much smaller file, and [AVIF to WebP](/avif-to-webp/) keeps transparency at a smaller size than PNG.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to PNG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: GIMP 2.10.22 or newer opens the AVIF; then choose File > Export As, end the name with .png and click Export.
- **ImageMagick (command line)**: `magick input.avif output.png` writes the PNG in one step.
- **avifdec (command line)**: run `avifdec input.avif output.png`, adding `-d 8` or `-d 16` to choose 8 or 16 bits per channel. A 16-bit PNG keeps more of an HDR picture's depth than this page does. For an image sequence it decodes frame one unless `--index` asks for a different frame or for every frame.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **Windows shows a blank thumbnail or won't open the file**: add Microsoft's HEIF Image Extension and AV1 Video Extension from the Microsoft Store, or open the AVIF in a browser.
- **"This browser can't open AVIF files"**: there is no AVIF decoder in your browser. Updating usually fixes it, and any current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari works.
- **The PNG is far bigger than expected**: a photo stored losslessly is heavy. Convert photos to JPG or WebP instead.
- **An animation became a still picture**: only the first frame is converted. Keep the AVIF, or use a tool that writes animated output.
- **Colors look duller than in the browser**: the PNG has 8 bits per channel and no color profile, so HDR and wide-color highlights are lost.
- **"Image decode failed."**: the file is damaged or isn't really an AVIF. Save it again from its source.

guide.title: About AVIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

AVIF, from the Alliance for Open Media, is the AV1 Image File Format. It places AV1-compressed pictures inside a HEIF container, with lossy or lossless compression, transparency, HDR, wide color gamut and 10-bit or 12-bit depth. Web images with small files and HDR images are its main uses. The registered media type is image/avif, and a file can carry Exif, XMP and an ICC color profile. The format is royalty-free, though decoding an AVIF is slow and an encoder can need several seconds per picture.

### Programs that open AVIF files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- GIMP: import and export arrived in GIMP 2.10.22.
- ImageMagick: reads AVIF.

**Web**

- Google Chrome: decoding arrived in Chrome 85.
- Mozilla Firefox: Firefox 93 added AVIF image support.

**Mobile**

- Chrome for Android: use a release with AVIF decoding.
- Safari: iOS 16 added still AVIF images.

### AVIF and TIFF compared

- **Compression**: AVIF uses AV1 for lossy or lossless images. TIFF offers a long list of methods, both lossless and lossy.
- **Depth**: AVIF channels can be 10 or 12 bits, and TIFF handles high bit depth and CMYK.
- **Pages**: a TIFF can hold multiple images in one file.
- **Use**: AVIF suits the web, while TIFF suits scanning, archiving and print.
- **Support**: Chrome, Firefox, Safari and GIMP open AVIF, while Photoshop, GIMP, Windows Photos and Preview open TIFF.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to TIFF

- **GIMP:** load the AVIF, go to File > Export As, give the name a .tiff ending and press Export. The TIFF dialog covers compression and metadata.
- **libheif:** run heif-dec artwork.avif artwork.tiff. The tool writes TIFF only when it was built with TIFF support.
- **ImageMagick:** run magick artwork.avif working-copy.tiff.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **A browser shows nothing**: older browsers may fail to display AVIF, so offer a JPEG, PNG or WebP fallback on a web page.
- **GIMP will not open it**: older GIMP releases lack the AVIF importer.
- **Windows shows nothing**: viewing .avif files on Windows needs Microsoft's AV1 Video Extension alongside the HEIF Image Extension.
- **A phone app rejects it**: from Android 12, devices decode baseline 8-bit AVIF, while 10-bit decoding is optional.

guide.title: Understanding BIN for JPEG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a BIN file?

The .bin ending marks raw binary data and says nothing about which image encoding, if any, is inside. The content could be a disc image, a dump of a program's memory or an email attachment, and the name gives no hint which. GNU objcopy, for one, can turn an object file into a flat memory image with the symbols and relocation records left out. The files people bring to a page like this are mostly pictures saved under that name, such as the ATT00001.bin attachments Outlook produces, or a Mac file in MacBinary, whose own extension is .bin.

### Programs that open BIN files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - GNU Emacs Hexl: shows and edits the bytes with hexl-find-file.
  - UltraEdit: gives a hex view of a .bin file.
- **Web:**
  - HexEd.it: inspects and edits the bytes in your browser.

A binary editor lays out the bytes in hexadecimal beside a text view. It does not interpret them as a photograph, so none of these programs shows the picture.

### BIN and JPEG compared

- **Names**: .bin has no fixed type, while .jpg and .jpeg are the same format.
- **Structure**: a BIN has no fixed layout. A JPEG is a lossy picture format built for photographs.
- **Transparency**: a JPEG cannot hold an alpha channel, so see-through pixels are lost, and it keeps no editable layers.

This page reads the start of the file and checks it against the signatures of known picture formats. A Mac file saved as MacBinary is recognized too, by skipping its 128-byte header. When the bytes match a picture, the file is converted as that format and you get a JPEG. Anything else is refused with a message that the file isn't an image, without the page reading all of it.

### Other ways to convert BIN to JPEG

This page works from the .bin itself. It identifies the picture from its first bytes, so you do not need to know beforehand whether the file is a PNG, a GIF or another picture format.

### Problems with BIN files

- **"This file isn't an image"**: the BIN contains data that is not a picture, so there is nothing to make a JPEG from.
- **Raw pixel data**: a BIN of bare pixel values has no picture header for the page to recognize, so it is refused as not an image.
- **The picture couldn't be read**: the file starts like an image but looks damaged or incomplete.
- **Editing in a hex editor**: work on a copy, because changing the wrong bytes alters the data.

guide.title: Understanding BMP for DDS output
guide.markdown:
### What is a BMP file?

BMP is the Windows Bitmap family, controlled by Microsoft and used originally on Windows and OS/2. Pixels are normally stored uncompressed, with lossless compression as an option, and you will run into the format in Windows screen captures and built-in system graphics. Version 5 appeared with Windows 98 in 1998 and can hold an ICC profile and an alpha channel. A BMP holds no vector shapes and no live typography.

### Programs that open BMP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - ImageMagick: reads BMP images.
- **Web:**
  - Mozilla Firefox: displays BMP pictures.
  - Google Chrome: supports BMP images.

### BMP and DDS compared

- **Names and types**: .bmp is image/bmp. .dds is Microsoft's DirectDraw Surface texture format.
- **Purpose**: BMP is a plain picture. DDS is a texture container for games and GPUs.
- **Contents**: a DDS can hold raw pixels or compressed texture data, and a chain of mipmaps may accompany the largest surface. Cube maps and volume textures fit as well, and Direct3D 10 and 11 reach texture arrays by way of an extra header.

The decoding happens in your browser, and ImageMagick turns the resulting 8-bit RGBA pixels into a DDS. Neither a compression format nor a mipmap option is set, and metadata is dropped.

### Other ways to convert BMP to DDS

- **DirectXTex texconv:** run `texconv -ft dds -f BC3_UNORM texture.bmp` to choose the pixel format yourself. Here -ft names the output file type, and -f names the DXGI format. texconv reads a BMP through Windows Imaging Component, and DDS output gets a full mipmap chain unless -m sets a different number of levels.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick surface.bmp surface.dds`. ImageMagick lists BMP and DDS as readable and writable, and its DDS notes cover DXT compression and mipmaps.

### Problems with BMP files

- **Large files**: an uncompressed BMP can be rather large, and a PNG or JPEG is more practical to share.
- **A program wants an older header**: some programs expect an older bitmap header, and ImageMagick writes those as BMP3 or BMP2.
- **No editable shapes or text**: a BMP keeps no vector shapes or live typography, so keep the project file you drew it from.

guide.title: About BMP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a BMP file?

BMP stands for Windows Bitmap. Microsoft controls this family of raster formats, which Windows and OS/2 used from the start. Windows 98 shipped in 1998 with version 5, which gained an alpha channel and ICC profile support. A BMP commonly stores uncompressed pixels, though lossless compression is available, and it can use 1 to 32 bits per pixel.

People often meet BMP through Windows screenshots and the graphics Windows itself uses. The media type image/bmp is the one registered for it.

A file opens with the two bytes BM for Windows, then a 14-byte file header and a DIB header that comes in several versions. The color table is mandatory at 8 bits per pixel or fewer, and 16 and 32 bit images are always uncompressed.

### Programs that open BMP files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- ImageMagick: reads and writes BMP.
- XnView MP: counts BMP among its supported formats, with a license needed for company use.

**Web**

- Mozilla Firefox: shows BMP pictures in web content.
- Google Chrome: handles BMP images, per Mozilla's browser compatibility table.

### BMP and GIF compared

- **Compression**: a BMP is usually uncompressed. A GIF compresses with LZW, without loss.
- **Colors**: a BMP pixel uses 1 to 32 bits, whereas each GIF frame draws on no more than 256 colors.
- **Transparency**: BMP version 5 can hold an alpha channel. GIF has 1-bit transparency.
- **Animation**: a BMP is one picture, and GIF supports simple animation.
- **Origin**: Microsoft introduced BMP with Windows. CompuServe introduced GIF in 1987.

In this converter a browser-side decode of the BMP feeds ImageMagick, which writes one GIF frame.

### Other ways to convert BMP to GIF

- **ImageMagick:** run magick diagram.bmp diagram-share.gif. ImageMagick lists GIF with up to 256 palette entries.

### Problems with BMP files

- **The file is bulky**: uncompressed pixels make a BMP heavy, and PNG or JPEG can suit distribution better.
- **An older program refuses it**: some programs expect the older bitmap header, and for them ImageMagick can write BMP3 or BMP2 instead of the default.
- **Vector shapes are gone**: a BMP does not keep editable vector shapes or live type.

### What is a BMP file?

BMP is Windows Bitmap, a raster format introduced with Microsoft Windows and later used on OS/2 too, registered as image/bmp. Microsoft controls the family. Pixels are usually stored uncompressed, from 1 to 32 bits per pixel, which makes files large and keeps them from being a good choice for sending pictures around. BMP mostly appears in screen captures and system graphics. - **Compression**: BMP is mostly raw. TIFF offers lossless and lossy schemes.
- **Structure**: TIFF is tag-based and can hold several images in one file.
- **Depth**: TIFF supports high bit depth. This page writes 8 bits per channel.
- **Use**: TIFF is common for scans and preservation masters.
- **Media types**: image/bmp for BMP and image/tiff for TIFF.
- **Origin**: Aldus and Microsoft developed TIFF, and Adobe holds the specification today.

The browser's own decoder reads the BMP into pixels, and ImageMagick compiled to WebAssembly writes the TIFF. No quality or compression value is set by the page.

guide.title: Understanding CDR for JPEG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a CDR file?

CorelDRAW saves its drawings as CDR by default. Corel calls the format primarily vector, with shapes, text and effects, though bitmap content can live in a drawing as well. Saving can compress bitmaps and graphic objects, which reduces the file size but slows opening and saving. Properties such as a title and subject can be stored, and fonts are embedded unless they are Asian fonts or lack embedding permission. For compatibility, the Save As dialog lists earlier CDR versions.

### Programs that open CDR files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - LibreOffice Draw: opens CDR by way of the libcdr library.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - CorelDRAW: opens its native drawings,.

### CDR and JPEG compared

- **Names**: .cdr is a proprietary Corel file, and JPEG goes by .jpg or .jpeg.
- **Structure**: a CDR holds shapes, text and pages that stay editable. A JPEG is a single flat picture and keeps no editable layers.
- **Transparency**: a JPEG can't store an alpha channel, so see-through areas are lost.

This converter cannot read CDR files. If you add a CDR, the page stops with "Image decode failed." Export the JPEG from a program that understands CorelDRAW drawings instead.

### Other ways to convert CDR to JPEG

- **CorelDRAW:** open the drawing and choose File > Export. Pick the folder, set Save as type to JPG and type a file name. Two optional check boxes limit what is exported: Export this page only, for the current page of a multipage file, and Selected only, for the selected objects. Neither is available for every format. Click Export.
- **Corel PHOTO-PAINT:** choose File > Import, pick CDR - CorelDRAW (*.cdr) in the list next to the File name box, click the filename, click Import, then click the image window. In the Convert to bitmap dialog, adjust the width, height, resolution or color mode. Then choose File > Export, pick a JPEG format in the Save as type list, type a file name and click Save.

### Problems with CDR files

- **A newer drawing won't open**: an earlier CorelDRAW release can refuse it, and the documented workaround is a copy saved for the older version.
- **Saving backward changes the drawing**: Corel warns that the copy can lose effects, change how items look or limit editing.
- **PHOTO-PAINT lost the vectors**: imported CDR files are rasterized, so shapes cannot be edited afterward.
- **Fonts**: embedding is limited by each font's permissions, and Asian fonts are not embedded, so check them before you share the CDR.

faqs.question: Why is my JPEG the same size after compressing?

faqs.question: Are .jpeg and .jpg files compressed the same way?

faqs.question: What happens to the camera details and color profile?

faqs.question: Should I compress a JPEG before or after editing it?

faqs.question: Can I undo the compression?

guide.title: About JPEG compression
guide.markdown:
### What is JPEG compression?

JPEG is a lossy way of storing photos, first published as ITU-T T.81 in 1992 and as ISO/IEC 10918-1 in 1994. It is built into most digital cameras and scanners, and every major browser shows it. Its trick is to keep what the eye notices and drop what it doesn't. Brightness is kept in more detail than color, small blocks of the picture are turned into frequency patterns, and the subtle patterns are stored with less precision or not at all.

The quality number controls that precision through tables of rounding steps. A high quality keeps almost everything and makes a big file. A lower one rounds harder, and the file shrinks. The scale usually runs from 0 to 100, but each program maps it to its own tables, which is why the same number gives different files in different apps.

Some arithmetic shows why the setting matters. A 12-megapixel photo is 12 million pixels with three color values each, about 36 MB before compression. At typical settings, a tenth to a twentieth of that, it lands somewhere between 1.8 and 3.6 MB, and a lower quality pushes it further down.

Compressing a JPEG that already exists means decoding it to pixels and encoding those pixels again with harder rounding. There is also a lossless kind of tidying: rewriting the file's coding tables or switching it to progressive order without touching the picture. That saves far less, but nothing is lost.

### Programs that compress JPEG files

**Windows**

- Adobe Photoshop: the Quality setting in Export As decides the JPEG's size.
- GIMP: with Show preview in image window ticked, its JPEG export dialog shows the file size each quality gives.

**Mac**

- Preview: re-exports a JPEG with a Least-to-Best Quality slider.
- Photos: can export a batch of photos as smaller JPEGs.

**Linux**

- GIMP: free on every desktop system.
- MozJPEG's cjpeg: the command-line version of the encoder this page uses.

**Web**

- Squoosh: a web app from Google Chrome Labs that shows the original and the compressed version side by side.
- This page: MozJPEG at a fixed quality of 82, with several files at once.

**Mobile**

- iPhone: Preview in iOS 26 has a Size slider when exporting a JPEG.
- Android and other phones: use this page in the browser.

### Lossy and lossless JPEG compression compared

- **Re-encoding (what this page does)**: the picture is decoded and saved again at quality 82. Savings are large on photos saved at a high quality, and a little detail is lost.
- **Lossless optimizing**: tools such as jpegtran rewrite the existing data with better coding tables or in progressive order. The pixels stay identical, and the file usually shrinks only a little.
- **Progressive and baseline**: a baseline JPEG loads top to bottom, while a progressive one appears blurry first and sharpens. This page writes progressive JPEGs.
- **Metadata**: thumbnails, EXIF, XMP and color profiles can add a noticeable amount to a small file. Re-encoding here leaves them out.
- **Pixel size**: neither kind of compression changes the width and height. Scaling down is a separate step, and the one that cuts size the most.
- **What stays the same**: the result is still image/jpeg, with 8 bits per color channel and no transparency or layers.

### Other ways to compress a JPEG

- **Preview (Mac)**: choose File > Export, set the format to JPEG, drag Quality down, then click Save.
- **Photos (Mac)**: choose File > Export > Export Photos, set Photo Kind to JPEG and lower JPEG Quality or Size.
- **Preview (iPhone, iOS 26)**: tap the actions button beside the file name, tap Export, pick JPEG and move the Size slider, which works for JPEG and HEIC.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: choose File > Export As with a .jpg or .jpeg name and lower Quality from its default of 85. Every export re-compresses.
- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: choose File > Export > Export As, select JPG and drag Quality down before clicking Export.

### Problems with JPEG compression

- **A form rejects .jpeg but takes .jpg**: the format is the same. Rename the ending, or convert with the [JPEG to JPG converter](/jpeg-to-jpg/).
- **The file is still too large after compressing**: its pixel dimensions are the main cost. Resize it, then compress again.
- **Smooth skies show bands or blocks**: gradients suffer most when a JPEG is squeezed. Start from a higher-quality original.
- **A logo lost its transparent background**: JPEG has no alpha channel. Keep such images as PNG or WebP, and shrink a WebP with the [WebP compressor](/compress-webp/).
- **The compressor returned the file unchanged**: the new encode wasn't smaller. The JPEG is already lean at this quality.

guide.title: About JPG compression
guide.markdown:
### What is JPG compression?

A JPG is compressed the moment it is saved. JPEG, named after the Joint Photographic Experts Group that started work on it in 1986, cuts a picture into 8x8 pixel blocks. Each block is turned into a set of frequencies with a discrete cosine transform, the finest frequencies are rounded off, and what is left is packed with Huffman coding. That rounding saves the space, and the quality number says how coarse it gets.

So compressing a JPG means saving it again with coarser rounding. Cameras and phones often store photos at a high quality, keeping detail that a web page, a chat message or an email never shows. Decoding such a file and encoding it at a lower quality gives a lighter file with the same width and height. Typical JPEG settings already shrink a picture to a tenth or a twentieth of its raw size, so a second pass saves most on files that were saved generously.

Three things decide how heavy a JPG is: how many pixels it has, how much fine detail and noise it holds, and how much metadata rides along. A 12-megapixel photo of grass is heavy at any quality. A small, smooth graphic stays light.

### Programs that compress JPG files

**Windows**

- Adobe Photoshop: Export As has a Quality setting for JPG.
- GIMP: free editor whose JPEG export dialog has a Quality slider.

**Mac**

- Preview: Export shows a Quality slider when JPEG is picked.
- Photos: exports photos as JPEG with a quality and a size choice.

**Linux**

- GIMP: the same JPEG export as on Windows and Mac.
- ImageMagick: `magick photo.jpg -quality 80 smaller.jpg` re-encodes from a terminal, on any system.
- jpegtran: rewrites a JPG without decoding it to pixels, for example with `-optimize` or `-progressive`, so the picture stays exactly the same and the saving is small.

**Web**

- This page: MozJPEG at quality 82, run by your browser.

**Mobile**

- iPhone: Preview in iOS 26 exports JPEG with a Size slider.
- Any phone: this page works in a mobile browser.

### Original and compressed JPG compared

- **Format**: both are JPEG files, image/jpeg, ending in .jpg. Any program that opened the original opens the copy.
- **Pixels**: the width and height are the same. Nothing is cropped or scaled.
- **Encoder and quality**: the copy is written by MozJPEG, an encoder tuned to get more out of the JPEG format, at quality 82. Quality numbers aren't a shared scale, so 82 here and 82 in another program can look different.
- **Layout**: the copy is a progressive JPEG with optimized Huffman tables. A progressive file shows a coarse picture early and fills in detail as it loads.
- **Metadata**: the copy carries no EXIF, ICC profile or XMP. Camera settings, the date taken and GPS location stay only in your original.
- **Size**: usually smaller. If it isn't, you get the original back, so a download is never larger than what you chose.

Every JPEG save is lossy, including this one. Compress from the best copy you have, once, rather than squeezing the same file again and again.

### Other ways to compress a JPG

- **Preview (Mac)**: open the image, choose File > Export, pick JPEG, drag the Quality slider down and click Save.
- **Photos (Mac)**: select the photos, choose File > Export > Export Photos, set Photo Kind to JPEG, then lower JPEG Quality or pick a smaller Size.
- **Preview (iPhone, iOS 26)**: open the file, tap the actions button next to its name, tap Export, choose JPEG and drag the Size slider. The slider applies to JPEG and HEIC exports.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: choose File > Export As, give the file a .jpg name, then lower Quality in the export dialog, which starts at 85. Each export compresses the picture again.
- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: choose File > Export > Export As, pick JPG, lower the Quality setting and click Export.

### Problems with compressing JPG files

- **The same file came back**: the quality 82 encode wasn't smaller, which happens with JPGs that were already saved light. Reduce the pixel size instead.
- **Still over an upload limit**: scale the photo down first, for example with Tools > Adjust Size in Preview or Image > Scale Image in GIMP, then compress the smaller copy.
- **Sharp text and lines turn fuzzy**: JPEG blurs hard edges. Keep screenshots, logos and diagrams as PNG and shrink them with the [PNG compressor](/compress-png/).
- **The location and camera details are gone**: the copy has no EXIF. Keep your original when you need them.
- **Colors look a little flat**: the ICC profile isn't copied, so a photo tagged with a wide-gamut profile such as Display P3 is shown as plain sRGB.
- **Blocks appear after several rounds**: each pass loses detail. Go back to the original rather than compressing a compressed copy.

guide.title: Understanding CR2 for PDF output
guide.markdown:
### What is a CR2 file?

Canon RAW version 2, or CR2, is the raw image format of many Canon EOS cameras from the mid-2000s until CR3 replaced it. Inside a TIFF-based file sit unprocessed sensor readings and an embedded JPEG preview. The Library of Congress notes that raw formats need special software to turn them into usable images. CR2 is a proprietary Canon format, so long-term access depends on software keeping up with it.

### Programs that open CR2 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - darktable: accepts CR2 on import and decodes supported raw files with RawSpeed.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Canon Digital Photo Professional: supports .CR2 among the raw extensions it opens, for images from compatible cameras.
- **Linux:**
  - LibRaw dcraw_emu: a LibRaw sample that emulates dcraw and takes its options as command-line keys.

### CR2 and PDF compared

- **Names**: .cr2 is a Canon camera format. .pdf is a document format with a fixed page layout.
- **Contents**: a CR2 holds sensor data and a preview. A PDF page holds the finished picture.
- **Use**: CR2 is for editing photos. PDF is for sharing and printing.

ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, reads the CR2 in your browser as one picture. In the PDF you get one page that matches the image, one pixel per point and no margin, so it is neither A4 nor Letter. The image is embedded losslessly as PNG data, and each file gets a PDF of its own. Anything over about 537 megapixels is refused as too large.

### Other ways to convert CR2 to PDF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick cr2:review.cr2 review.pdf`. ImageMagick lists CR2 as read-only and PDF as readable and writable, and the `cr2:` prefix tells it to read the file as a CR2.

### Problems with CR2 files

- **Your camera is not supported**: Canon's Digital Photo Professional handles .CR2 images from compatible cameras only, so check that yours is one of them.
- **The page size is odd**: the PDF page matches the pixel size, so it is large on paper. Place the picture on a standard page in a layout program.
- **Long-term access**: CR2 is a proprietary format, so reading it depends on software that keeps supporting it.

guide.title: Understanding CR2 for TIFF output
guide.markdown:
### What is a CR2 file?

CR2, or Canon RAW version 2, was the raw format of many Canon EOS cameras until CR3 took over. Inside is unprocessed sensor data in a TIFF-based layout. Those measurements need processing to become a viewable photograph, and choices such as white balance and tone can be made after the shot. That is why a CR2 and its small preview can look different. Canon's DPP names .CR2 in its list of supported raw extensions, and a CR2 differs from a finished JPEG because the interpretation is left to processing software.

### Programs that open CR2 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** darktable imports CR2 for the cameras its raw decoder supports.
- **Windows and Mac:** Canon's Digital Photo Professional reads CR2 files from supported Canon cameras, and Adobe Camera Raw opens them with its own camera support list.
- **Linux:** The dcraw_emu sample that ships with LibRaw develops raw files from the command line.

Each of these keeps its own list of supported camera models.

### CR2 and TIFF compared

- **Content**: a CR2 holds raw sensor data to be processed. A TIFF holds finished pixels.
- **Compression**: TIFF allows several methods, and the page sets none.
- **Pages**: a TIFF may hold several images. The page reads one picture.
- **Origin**: Aldus published TIFF, and Adobe now maintains it.

Everything runs locally. LibRaw, compiled into ImageMagick for WebAssembly, develops the CR2, and ImageMagick then writes the TIFF. Pictures larger than about 537 megapixels are not accepted.

### Other ways to convert CR2 to TIFF

- **Canon Digital Photo Professional:** select the CR2, choose File > Convert and save, pick TIFF as the image type, set a destination and save.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick cr2:exposure.cr2 exposure.tiff`. The `cr2:` prefix names the format explicitly.

### Problems with CR2 files

- **The TIFF differs from the preview**: raw rendering varies between programs. Compare in your editor.
- **The page can't read the file**: the camera may be too new for LibRaw, or the file is cut off. Try Canon Digital Photo Professional.
- **A CR2 suffix does not guarantee support**: check the decoder's model list for the camera that made the file.
- **Long-term access**: the proprietary camera format depends on continued software support, which is a preservation concern.
- **You want to edit the exposure later**: raw settings stay with the CR2, so keep the original.

guide.title: About CSV and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is a CSV file?

CSV exchanges rows of text fields between databases and spreadsheets. RFC 4180 documented a common representation in October 2005 rather than inventing the older format, and the registered media type is text/csv. A header record may come before the data rows, and double quotes protect fields that contain commas or line breaks. Dialects differ in delimiter and quoting, and a spreadsheet export stores one sheet's data without workbook formatting.

### Programs that open CSV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** LibreOffice Calc opens Text CSV through an import dialog with delimiter and column-format choices.
- **Windows and Mac:** Microsoft Excel imports and exports CSV; choose text handling with care for identifiers.
- **Linux:** the Python csv module reads records with configurable dialects.
- **Web:** Google provides a documented Apps Script for importing CSV into Google Sheets.

### CSV and JPG compared

- **Content**: CSV is text you can sort and calculate with. JPG holds pixels, so the numbers in the picture cannot be selected as data.
- **Compression**: JPEG is lossy and has no alpha.
- **Types**: text/csv against image/jpeg; .jpg and .jpeg are the same format.

The page reads the CSV with the same parser the table converters use and draws it on a canvas. The picture is saved at JPEG quality 0.92, with no other setting to choose. Several CSV files selected together become one JPG each.

### Other ways to convert CSV to JPG

- **Calc and ImageMagick:** in Calc, choose File > Open for the CSV, then File > Export As > Export as PDF. Turn the first PDF page into an image with `magick 'table.pdf[0]' table.jpg`. ImageMagick relies on Ghostscript to read PDF.
- **Excel and GIMP:** open the CSV in Excel with File > Open, select the cells, and choose Home > Copy arrow > Copy as Picture. In GIMP choose File > Create > From Clipboard, then File > Export As and type a name ending in .jpg.
- **Python and Pillow:** read the rows with `csv.reader`, draw them on an image with `ImageDraw.multiline_text` and save with `image.save("table.jpg", "JPEG")`. You choose the canvas size, fonts and column widths in the script.

### Problems with CSV files

- **Everything lands in one column**: the delimiter does not match what the program expects. Set the separator in the import dialog.
- **Dates or IDs changed**: Excel can reinterpret them on opening. Import with the column formats you want.
- **Rows split in the wrong place**: a parser must honor quoted line breaks rather than treat each physical line as a record.
- **Formatting is gone**: CSV saves the current sheet's data alone.

faqs.question: Can ImageMagick make the JPEG?

faqs.question: Can the JPEG replace the DICOM file?

guide.title: About DCM and JPEG
guide.markdown:
### What is a DCM file?

DCM is the usual ending for DICOM, the standard that defines medical objects such as images, waveforms and reports. The ACR-NEMA predecessor appeared in 1985 and the renamed DICOM standard followed in 1993. The registered media type is application/dicom, and the registration recommends .dcm for disk files other than DICOMDIR, which can index a collection of related files. A Part 10 file begins with a 128-byte preamble followed by the DICM marker. A DCM stores an image together with patient and study metadata, and its pixels can be 16-bit grayscale.

### Programs that open DCM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** 3D Slicer imports DICOM studies into a database and then loads the series you choose. ImageMagick can read DICOM images, and its notes list window center and width tag handling.
- **Windows:** MicroDicom is a viewer, free for noncommercial use, for CT, MRI and other DICOM studies. IrfanView lists DCM, ACR and IMA among its formats, which need its plug-ins.

### DCM and JPEG compared

- **Content**: a DCM holds the image and its attributes. A JPEG holds only a picture.
- **Depth**: DICOM pixels can be 16-bit grayscale, while a JPEG has no transparency and is always lossy.
- **Compression**: DICOM has many compression options.
- **Types**: application/dicom against image/jpeg.

No conversion happens on this page: with no DICOM reader, the file is rejected with "Image decode failed." Do the export in a program that understands the format.

### Other ways to convert DCM to JPEG

- **MicroDicom (Windows):** open the images, or a disc or folder with File > Scan for DICOM files, then choose File > Export > To a picture file or press Shift+P. Pick a destination folder, what to export and JPG as the image format, then click Export. More settings sets the JPEG quality and whether annotations and overlay text are drawn.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick image.dcm image.jpeg`. ImageMagick reads DICOM images and recognizes window center and width tags.
- **IrfanView (Windows):** install the plug-ins IrfanView needs for DCM, open the file, then use File > Save as and choose JPG as the output format.

### Problems with DCM files

- **Only one slice opens**: a series often spans many files. Open the folder in a viewer.
- **Can't tell whose study it is**: file and folder names do not reliably identify the patient, study or series. Use the DICOM attributes.
- **Some objects will not load**: certain information objects need 3D Slicer extensions instead of its core importer.
- **Patient details travel with the study**: DICOM objects can contain demographic information, so sharing an exported image and sharing the source study have different privacy consequences.

guide.title: About DDS files
guide.markdown:
### What is a DDS file?

DirectDraw Surface, abbreviated DDS, is Microsoft's texture container, first made for DirectX and used for cubemaps too. Inside, the data may be plain pixels or compressed texture blocks, and the DXT or BC block formats meant for GPUs are common. Game textures and other GPU-ready assets are its typical uses.

Beside the largest surface a file may carry a chain of mipmaps, and cube maps and volume textures also fit. With Direct3D 10 and 11 came an extra header that adds texture arrays. This DX10 header can name formats the original pixel-format structure cannot express.

### Programs that open DDS files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- GIMP: built-in DDS support arrived in GIMP 2.10.10.
- ImageMagick: reads and writes DDS, including documented DXT compression and mipmap options.

### DDS and JPEG compared

- **Purpose**: a DDS is a texture container for graphics hardware. A JPEG is a photographic image format.
- **Compression**: a DDS commonly uses DXT or BC blocks. A JPEG is lossy with an adjustable quality.
- **Extras**: a DDS can hold mipmaps and cube maps. A JPEG is one image.
- **Alpha**: a DDS can have an alpha channel. A JPEG has none.
- **Support**: JPEG opens everywhere.

The page has ImageMagick read a single picture from the DDS and write it out as a JPEG.

### Other ways to convert DDS to JPEG

- **texconv:** run texconv -ft jpg review-texture.dds. This Microsoft DirectXTex tool takes a DDS as input, and -ft sets the output file type.
- **GIMP:** open the DDS, then choose File > Export As, use a .jpeg ending and click Export. The JPEG dialog offers a quality value from 0 to 100, and JPEG cannot hold transparency or multiple layers.
- **ImageMagick:** run magick review-texture.dds texture-report.jpeg. ImageMagick lists DDS with DXT and mipmap support.

### Problems with DDS files

- **A reader refuses it**: tools that reject the DX10 extension may accept a legacy RGB or DXT1 to DXT5 header instead.
- **The header is truncated**: a plain DDS header takes at least 128 bytes, and 148 with the DX10 extension.
- **The texture looks scrambled**: a wrong pitch value can throw off how a reader interprets scan lines, so compute it for the stored format.

guide.title: About DIVX and MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is a DIVX file?

A .divx file belongs to DivX's video playback and authoring ecosystem. The first DivX releases used MPEG-4 Part 2 video, normally inside AVI files, and H.264 came later. DivX authoring can add menus and chapter points to a movie, and a DivX movie can contain subtitles and more than one audio track. DivX certification profiles describe what each playback device can handle, so the advanced features depend on the device.

DivX is mainly a delivery format. Adobe advises converting it before editing in Premiere.

### Programs that open DIVX files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player decodes DivX video.
- **Windows and Mac:** DivX Player lists the .divx extension and offers soundtrack selection.
- **Linux:** FFplay, FFmpeg's test player, handles DivX streams and subtitle samples.

### DIVX and MP4 compared

- **Container**: MP4 is a nested-box container standardized as ISO/IEC 14496-14. DivX names a codec family and a set of player features.
- **Extras**: menus and chapters belong to DivX authoring; MP4 can hold subtitles and chapters of its own.
- **Playback**: every major browser plays MP4, with the media type video/mp4.

Converting here decodes the DivX video and encodes a new H.264 picture beside AAC sound at 96 kbps. A picture over 1920 px in either direction shrinks to fit, and the rate is held to 30 fps. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced first.

### Other ways to convert DIVX to MP4

- **Prism (Windows):** Prism lists AVI files encoded with DivX as an input. Run `prism.exe -convert "C:\Media\feature.avi" -format .mp4` on the AVI that holds your DivX video. Prism reports nothing when the job ends, so watch its window.

### Problems with DIVX files

- **It plays in DivX Player only**: menus, chapters and extra tracks rely on the player's DivX profile, so a different player may skip them.
- **A device refuses the DIVX**: certification profiles describe each device's limits, so a file can be fine on one player and rejected by another.
- **Editing in Premiere**: Adobe advises converting DivX before editing, because DivX is primarily a delivery format.
- **A decoder is not enough**: having a DivX video decoder does not by itself mean every advanced authoring feature will work.

guide.title: About DNG files
guide.markdown:
### What is a DNG file?

DNG stands for Digital Negative. Adobe published it in September 2004 as one documented format for camera-raw data, in place of the many proprietary raw formats. Its design adds to the TIFF family the tags needed to make sense of raw photographs. A DNG can store mosaic sensor data or a demosaiced linear representation, and it may use lossless JPEG compression for the raw samples. Exif metadata can accompany the image data.

Photographers use DNG to archive raw photos and to move them between raw editors. Some phones and cameras write DNG directly. Adobe offers DNG Converter to translate supported proprietary raw files into DNG.

### Programs that open DNG files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- darktable: imports DNG. Decoding limitations still apply to some files.
- ImageMagick: reads DNG, and the dng: prefix selects the format explicitly.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe Camera Raw: Adobe's raw processing workflow includes DNG support.

### DNG and TIFF compared

- **Content**: a DNG holds unprocessed sensor data or a linear representation. A TIFF holds a finished raster.
- **Structure**: both are tag-based, since DNG extends the TIFF family.
- **Compression**: DNG may compress raw samples losslessly, while TIFF offers many methods, lossless or lossy.
- **Depth**: high bit depth and CMYK are part of what TIFF supports.
- **Support**: Lightroom, Photoshop, darktable and RawTherapee open DNG, and TIFF is read by Preview, Windows Photos, GIMP and Photoshop.

Here ImageMagick develops one picture from the DNG with default settings and writes it as a TIFF.

### Other ways to convert DNG to TIFF

- **darktable:** import the DNG and develop it. Open the export module and choose file on disk for the target storage, then select TIFF as the format and tune bit depth, compression, profile and size before you export.
- **ImageMagick:** run magick dng:negative.dng developed.tiff. The dng: prefix names the format.

### Problems with DNG files

- **Sensor layout is not recognized**: a DNG can be valid and still use a sensor pattern some readers cannot handle, and darktable lists limits for non-Bayer sensors.
- **A linear DNG is different**: its data is already demosaiced, so it cannot stand in for untouched sensor-mosaic samples.

guide.title: About DOT and PNG files
guide.markdown:
### What is a DOT file?

A DOT file is a plain-text graph description from the Graphviz project, also saved as .gv. It lists nodes, edges and their attributes. A graph can be directed or undirected. The file holds relationships rather than a finished picture, so Graphviz tools such as dot decide where each shape and label goes. People use it for dependency and flow diagrams and for diagrams of networks.

### Programs that open DOT files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Graphviz lays out and renders DOT files. Its download page lists Windows installers, Linux packages and, for Mac, MacPorts and Homebrew.

Gephi opens DOT files too. Any text editor shows the source, though an editor does not draw the graph.

### DOT and PNG compared

PNG, a lossless raster format from the mid-1990s, was designed to replace GIF without patent worries; it is an ISO/IEC 15948 standard and a W3C Recommendation. Every browser shows it, so a diagram sent as a PNG needs no Graphviz at the other end. The trade is that the result is pixels. The nodes and edges become pixels, so keep the DOT file for later edits.

Here, Graphviz 16.1.0 compiled to WebAssembly lays out the first graph in your file inside the browser. The picture is drawn on white at twice the graph's size in points, and it is fitted to 4096 px on each side when it would be larger. There is no quality setting. Pictures and shape files the graph names are not loaded.

### Other ways to convert DOT to PNG

- **Graphviz:** run `dot -Tpng input.dot -o diagram.png`.
- **PyGraphviz:** call `g = pgv.AGraph("input.dot")`, then `g.draw("diagram.png", format="png", prog="dot")`. It draws through Graphviz's layout programs, here `dot`.
- **pydot:** call `graphs = pydot.graph_from_dot_file("input.dot")`, then `graphs[0].write_png("diagram.png")`. The example takes the first graph with `graphs[0]`. Graphviz is installed separately.

### Problems with DOT files

A DOT file with a syntax error is not drawn: Graphviz's own error message is shown instead, so test a small graph before adding the whole network. An empty file is refused. A graph with more than 1,000 edges is laid out with Graphviz speed limits unless it sets its own. A very large graph is drawn smaller to fit 4096 px, and its small text can become hard to read.

infoArticle.title: About FanslyLive downloads
infoArticle.markdown:
Fansly live streams are ephemeral by design. Once a broadcast ends, the content often disappears unless the creator explicitly saves a replay. If you missed the window or your connection dropped mid-stream, that content is gone. Fansly Live Downloader captures authorized live broadcasts as they happen, writing standard MP4 files to your local storage so you retain a permanent copy of streams you were entitled to watch.

The workflow is straightforward. Open a Fansly live stream page in your browser while logged in to your subscriber account. The extension detects the active broadcast and presents a record button in the toolbar popup. Press record and the incoming stream data is captured frame by frame and assembled into an MP4 container on your hard drive. Audio and video stay synchronized throughout, even when the streamer switches between camera angles or adjusts their broadcast settings mid-session.

Recording happens entirely within your browser. No data is routed through external relay servers, no temporary copies are staged in the cloud, and no metadata about your viewing habits leaves your machine. The extension communicates with Fansly to receive the stream and with a license server for activation — nothing else.

You can pause and resume recording during a single broadcast if you only want specific segments. Each saved file is automatically named with the creator handle and timestamp, making it easy to organize a growing archive without manual renaming. When the stream ends naturally or you stop recording, the file is finalized and immediately playable in any standard video player.

Compatible with Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, and Opera across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Three free recording sessions are included so you can verify quality and compatibility before purchasing a full license.
