infoArticle.title: About Video Downloader for Mindvalley
infoArticle.markdown:
Mindvalley quests are transformational, but at $499 per year, that subscription is a serious commitment. Cancel and you lose instant access to every lesson, meditation, and masterclass you have been working through. That is a lot of personal growth to leave behind.

This extension gives you a safety net. Open any Mindvalley lesson, press play, click the extension icon, and choose your preferred quality. The video saves as an MP4 straight to a dedicated Mindvalley folder on your computer. It works with all the different video players Mindvalley uses across its pages, so one extension handles everything.

Most generic download tools fail on Mindvalley because the platform uses time-limited video links that expire quickly. This extension was built specifically around that challenge, so it grabs the video reliably where other tools fail. Three free downloads are included after a quick email sign-in, no credit card required. All processing happens right in your browser, and your videos are never uploaded anywhere else.

faqs.question: How do I download a Mindvalley lesson?
faqs.answer: Open the Mindvalley lesson page, press play so the stream becomes active, then click the extension icon and choose the quality you want. The extension detects the active source and saves the finished file as MP4.

faqs.question: What Mindvalley content can it download?
faqs.answer: It is designed for recorded Mindvalley lesson content such as quest videos, masterclasses, and other course pages you can already access in your session.

faqs.question: Why do I need to press play first?
faqs.answer: Mindvalley uses tokenized HLS delivery. The correct stream URLs often appear only after playback starts, so the extension needs the active request before it can build the download.

faqs.question: What video platforms are supported on Mindvalley pages?
faqs.answer: The extension supports Mindvalley native video and can also detect embedded Vimeo, YouTube, Loom, Wistia, and SproutVideo content when those players appear on Mindvalley pages.

faqs.question: What quality options are available?
faqs.answer: Quality depends on the lesson source. For native Mindvalley HLS, the extension can read the master playlist variants. For embedded providers, it shows the renditions exposed by that platform.

faqs.question: Where are files saved?
faqs.answer: Completed downloads are written automatically to a Mindvalley folder inside your browser's default Downloads directory.

faqs.question: Does it support live streams?
faqs.answer: No. The product is built for recorded Mindvalley lesson content, not live-stream capture.

faqs.question: Does it work in the Mindvalley mobile app?
faqs.answer: No. This is a desktop browser extension for Mindvalley.com and compatible desktop browsing sessions.

faqs.question: Which browsers are supported?
faqs.answer: Desktop builds support Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave, Opera, Whale, and Yandex on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Safari and mobile browsers are not supported.

faqs.question: How does the free trial work?
faqs.answer: After secure email OTP sign-in, you get 3 free downloads on the current device. Continued use requires the paid license configured for this product.

faqs.question: Is my data private?
faqs.answer: Yes. Detection, stream processing, and MP4 generation happen locally in the browser. Remote requests are limited to activation, update checks, and the original video sources you are already authorized to access.

infoArticle.title: About XHamsterLive downloads
infoArticle.markdown:
xHamsterLive cam sessions are transient. Performers go live, interact with their audience, and when the session ends the content is typically gone unless a recorded replay surfaces later. This downloader lets you capture live cam sessions in real time, writing the incoming stream directly to an MP4 file on your local device so you maintain a permanent offline copy of broadcasts you were authorized to view.

Open any active xHamsterLive cam room in your browser while logged in to your account. The extension detects the live stream and adds a capture button to the toolbar popup. Click it, and the broadcast is recorded locally as it plays. The extension intercepts the stream data at the browser level and writes it to disk without re-encoding, preserving the original quality and keeping CPU usage low.

If a session runs for hours, the extension handles it gracefully. Automatic segment stitching assembles long recordings into a single continuous file, and a heartbeat monitor watches for stream interruptions. If the feed drops temporarily and resumes, the recorder picks up again without creating a separate file. You end up with one clean MP4 per session.

Every file is named automatically using the performer's handle and the session start time. This convention makes it simple to browse a large collection weeks or months later without trying to remember which file is which. Duplicate detection prevents you from accidentally re-recording a session you have already saved.

The entire process is local. No stream data is uploaded to external servers, no recording logs are transmitted, and no analytics are collected. The extension talks to xHamsterLive for stream access and to a license server for activation. That is the complete list of network destinations. Works on Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, and Opera across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Three free capture sessions are included.

guide.title: Understanding DST to JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is a DST file?

A DST file is a machine embroidery stitch file developed by Tajima. It stores needle positions and commands such as jumps, color stops and trims rather than a picture. Ordinary DST files do not keep a thread palette, though pyembroidery documents an extended-header variant with color information. Making a design bigger only pulls the same stitches farther apart; nothing fills the gaps.

### Programs that open DST files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Ink/Stitch for Inkscape reads and writes DST stitch files.
- **Windows and Mac:** Embrilliance Essentials displays and recolors DST designs.
- **Windows:** Wilcom EmbroideryStudio reads stitch files, and it can try to recover editable embroidery objects from those stitches.
- **Linux:** pyembroidery is a library for Python, not a viewer with a window. Its read_dst function loads DST stitch data when a compatible Python environment is installed.

### DST and JPG compared

JPG is a lossy format for photographs that stores 8 bits per color channel and has no transparency. DST stores instructions for a machine, so making a JPG from one means drawing the stitches onto a canvas, which an embroidery program does and this page does not. Because ordinary DST files keep no thread palette, the colors in such a preview come from the thread list you assign, not from the file.

This page decodes a file with the browser's own image decoder. A DST has no picture inside, so the decode step fails with the message "Image decode failed." and no JPG is produced.

### Other ways to convert DST to JPG

- **Ink/Stitch and GIMP:** in Inkscape with Ink/Stitch installed, open the DST through File > Open. Export it with File > Export PNG Image, then bring the PNG into GIMP and save it as a JPEG.
- **pyembroidery and ImageMagick:** `pyembroidery.read_dst("design.dst")` loads the stitches and `pyembroidery.write_png(pattern, "preview.png")` draws them. Finish with `magick preview.png preview.jpg`.

### Problems with DST files

- Unexpected preview colors can reflect missing palette data, so an external thread list is needed.
- Reducing a design's coordinates squeezes both the spacing and the length of its stitches.
- Reconstructing embroidery objects from stitches cannot restore every original editing property, so keep your source design next to the DST.
- An SVG kept beside the machine output preserves an editable Ink/Stitch source.

guide.title: About DST and PNG files
guide.markdown:
### What is a DST file?

DST is a Tajima machine embroidery stitch file. Instead of a picture, it records stitch coordinates, plus changes in thread and other machine actions, for the machine to carry out. The file says how to sew a design, not how it looks. Ordinary DST files do not preserve a thread palette, though the pyembroidery project documents an extended-header variant that carries colors.

### Programs that open DST files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Ink/Stitch, an extension for Inkscape, reads and writes DST.
- **Windows and Mac:** Embrilliance Essentials displays and recolors DST designs.
- **Windows:** Wilcom EmbroideryStudio opens stitch files and can try to turn them back into embroidery objects.
- **Linux:** pyembroidery is a Python library and not a viewer; scripts call its read_dst function to load the stitch data.
- **Web:** a browser preview of a DST design is offered by Wilcom Library, with an account.

### DST and PNG compared

PNG is a lossless raster format with optional transparency, and every browser shows it. A PNG preview suits a catalog, an email or a last look at a design before sewing, but a machine cannot sew from it. A DST has no pixels at all. To make a PNG, software has to draw each stitch and pick thread colors, because ordinary DST files keep no thread palette.

This page cannot do that. It decodes pictures, and a DST is not one, so every attempt ends with "Image decode failed." For a PNG preview, use one of the programs above.

### Other ways to convert DST to PNG

- **Ink/Stitch and Inkscape:** with Ink/Stitch installed, choose File > Open in Inkscape then select the DST; it loads in Manual Stitch Mode. Then choose File > Export PNG Image, pick the area (Page, Drawing, Selection or Custom) and the size in pixels, and click Export.
- **pyembroidery:** with the library installed, call `pattern = pyembroidery.read("input.dst")`, then `pyembroidery.write(pattern, "preview.png")`.

### Problems with DST files

A design shown in odd colors usually means the palette is missing, since an external thread list is needed. Enlarging a basic DST spreads its existing stitches without adding any, and shrinking the coordinates tightens stitch spacing and stitch length. Objects rebuilt from stitches miss some of the original editing properties, so keep an SVG design beside the machine file as your editable Ink/Stitch source.

guide.title: Understanding DST for SVG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a DST file?

Tajima developed DST as a machine embroidery stitch format. It stores needle positions plus machine commands: jumps, color stops and trims. It is not a picture. A machine must be told when to insert a color change, thread trim, tie off or tie in, and a DST carries those commands. It is used for industrial embroidery machines and digitized designs, and embroidery programs widely support it. A basic DST has no color information.

### Programs that open DST files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - Ink/Stitch: reads and writes DST embroidery files, and you open them as you would an SVG in Inkscape. The design opens in Manual Stitch Mode, where you can edit individual points.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Embrilliance Essentials: reads DST files and lets you change or remove individual colors and save a new file.
- **Web:**
  - Wilcom Library: accepts DST uploads and previews designs at true scale in a browser on Mac, PC and tablets, with a Library user license. You do not need EmbroideryStudio to use it.

### DST and SVG compared

- **Contents**: a DST has stitch coordinates and machine commands. An SVG describes shapes and paths as XML text that scales to any size.
- **Color**: a DST stores no color information, while an SVG is XML that CSS can style.
- **Use**: a DST feeds industrial embroidery machines. An SVG suits logos, illustrations and charts.

This converter cannot read DST files. A DST added here is met with "Image decode failed." Use pyembroidery in Python to write the SVG.

### Other ways to convert DST to SVG

- **pyembroidery:** run `pyembroidery.convert("sample.dst", "sample.svg")` in Python. The library reads DST and writes SVG. Its read_dst function loads a DST's stitch data, and a DST variant called extended adds a color sequence through its headers.

### Problems with DST files

- **Odd preview colors**: a DST stores no color information, so apply a threadlist, as Ink/Stitch allows, to give the design colors.
- **Resizing changes the stitching**: enlarging a basic DST spreads the same stitches apart, while shrinking it tightens the spacing and shortens the stitches.
- **Rebuilding objects**: EmbroideryStudio can try to rebuild objects from stitches, yet it cannot recreate the colors.

guide.title: Understanding DV for MP4 output
guide.markdown:
### What is a DV file?

DV is a family of digital video encodings developed for videocassettes in the early 1990s, from a specification by a ten-company consortium later standardized by IEC. Each picture is compressed on its own with a discrete cosine transform, so DV does not compress from frame to frame the way MPEG-2 does. Raw DV data can be stored as a file with a .dv or .dif extension.

### Programs that open DV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - FFmpeg: a command-line tool that both decodes and encodes DV video.
  - VLC media player: a free and open source player with a DV demuxer registered for the .dv extension.

### DV and MP4 compared

- **Names**: .dv is a tape-based stream format. MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14, a container for video and audio.
- **Compression**: DV compresses each picture alone. MP4 here holds H.264 with AAC audio.
- **Use**: DV is legacy camcorder footage. MP4 plays on nearly every device.

The work is done by a WebAssembly build of FFmpeg inside your browser tab. It re-encodes the video as H.264 with libx264, at the ultrafast preset with constant rate factor 32, and encodes the sound as AAC at 96 kbps. Interlaced frames get deinterlaced. The output stops at 1920 pixels on its longer side and 30 frames per second, and a smaller or slower source is never raised. Rounding costs a frame with odd dimensions one pixel. No upload takes place.

### Other ways to convert DV to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i tape.dv -c:v libx264 -c:a aac viewing.mp4`. FFmpeg lists DV video and MP4 as supported for both decoding and encoding, and the command picks H.264 video and AAC sound.

### Problems with DV files

- **Raw or wrapped**: the same DV data can sit raw in a .dv or .dif file or inside AVI, QuickTime or MXF. This page's picker takes files ending in .dv.
- **Two kinds of DV**: there is a consumer kind and a professional kind, and DVCAM from Sony and DVCPRO from Panasonic are the professional developments.
- **Frame metadata**: DV attaches metadata to every recorded frame. Your original file is left unchanged, so keep it.
- **A long file is slow**: conversion runs on your own device, so time depends on its speed.

guide.title: About FLV and MOV
guide.markdown:
### What is an FLV file?

Macromedia's Flash video delivery gave us FLV, a binary container. The picture is typically Sorenson or On2 VP6, and the sound is MP3, PCM or ADPCM. Through ActionScript, a Flash SWF could point at an outside FLV, which is why many clips sat in separate files.

Adobe stopped supporting Flash Player at the close of 2020, yet the recordings live on in archives, interview downloads and course libraries. The .flv ending names no codec, so a program also needs whichever decoder the stream inside requires.

### Programs that open FLV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player handles FLV, with Sorenson and VP6 decoding on its feature list. FFplay decodes through FFmpeg.
- **Mobile:** On phones, the Android port of VLC shares the desktop player's decoding, and VLC for iOS opens local files in its own player.

### FLV and MOV compared

- **Origin**: FLV is a Flash-era delivery format. MOV is Apple's QuickTime container, built from atoms.
- **Codecs**: a MOV may carry H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG pictures beside AAC or PCM sound.
- **Support**: MOV works best in Apple's own software and many editors; for the web, MP4 travels further.
- **Types**: video/quicktime for MOV.

Here the FLV is decoded and new H.264 video goes into the MOV with AAC sound at 96 kbps. Anything over 1920 px shrinks to fit, 30 fps is the frame-rate ceiling, and frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced first. The result is an access copy for watching or sharing, not an editing master.

### Other ways to convert FLV to MOV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i interview.flv -c:v libx264 -c:a aac interview.mov` makes an H.264 and AAC MOV. FFmpeg lists FLV and MOV for both reading and writing, takes the output format from the .mov extension, and gets H.264 from the external library libx264.

### Problems with FLV files

- **The FLV won't play**: the stream may need a decoder your player lacks. Try VLC rather than hunting for a Flash Player download.
- **The editor refuses the MOV**: a QuickTime file can use codecs that the destination editor lacks. Check which codecs it imports before converting again.
- **Soft picture**: Flash-era video was often small and heavily compressed, and the MOV can't be sharper than the FLV it came from.
- **Several audio tracks**: the one-audio-stream FLV model cannot keep alternative audio tracks, so none are waiting to be recovered.

guide.title: About FLV and WMV
guide.markdown:
### What is an FLV file?

An FLV is a Flash-era recording, a binary layout tied to Macromedia's Flash video delivery. A file can hold just one video stream and one audio stream; Sorenson or On2 VP6 supply the picture, and MP3, PCM or ADPCM the sound. Flash Player is discontinued, so a saved lesson or interview now needs a desktop player.

The extension names no codec, so a program can read the file only if it has the decoder for the stream inside. Reinstalling Flash Player is not an appropriate way to play an old FLV.

### Programs that open FLV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player's feature list names FLV input as well as Sorenson and VP6 decoding. FFplay relies on FFmpeg's decoders.
- **Mobile:** On Android, VLC brings the desktop player's decoding to phones. On iOS, VLC plays local files with its own engine.

### FLV and WMV compared

- **Container**: a .wmv file is Windows Media content inside ASF, a container designed for synchronized media storage and network delivery.
- **Codecs**: Windows Media Video 7, 8 and 9 all fit the extension, so the extension alone doesn't say which one you hold.
- **Types**: video/x-ms-wmv is what the Library of Congress records for WMV, since IANA has no registration.

FFmpeg picks the codecs for the .wmv here: MS-MPEG4 v3 for the picture, which is not Windows Media Video, and WMA v2 for the sound. Its default bitrates stay in place, so fine lettering and busy scenes blur. Deinterlacing comes first, then oversized pictures shrink and a fast source is thinned without being shortened. Several files run one after another with no size or time limit.

### Other ways to convert FLV to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i lesson.flv lesson.wmv`. FFmpeg lists Flash Video and ASF for both reading and writing, and it takes the output format from the .wmv extension, so no codec options are needed.

### Problems with FLV files

- **Player coverage**: In FFmpeg's documentation the Windows Media Video 9 decoder is not marked as completely working, so test the WMV in the player that will use it.
- **Quality**: the WMV ending alone does not establish image quality. It depends on the codec and compression settings.
- **A reader is not a decoder**: a program may read ASF without having every codec inside it, so a WMV can open and still show no picture.
- **Another generation of loss**: start each attempt from the FLV, not from a previous WMV.

faqs.question: Why is my BMP not animated?
faqs.answer: A BMP holds a single picture, so the converter keeps only the first frame of the GIF. The delays between frames and the loop count are left out.

faqs.question: Can I choose a different frame?
faqs.answer: Not on this page. ImageMagick counts frames from 0, so `badge.gif'[2]'` picks the third frame, and a range such as `[1-3]` picks several.

faqs.question: Why is the BMP bigger than the GIF?
faqs.answer: LZW packs a GIF's palette indexes tightly, but a BMP commonly keeps every pixel uncompressed. Uncompressed pixels take room, which is why PNG or JPEG suits sharing better.

faqs.question: Does BMP bring back colors the GIF lost?
faqs.answer: No. Each GIF frame was limited to a small palette of colors, and the BMP is built from that already reduced image. A new format can't restore the original colors.

faqs.question: Is the GIF comment kept?
faqs.answer: No. Metadata, including comments, is dropped, and the picture is decoded to 8-bit RGBA first. Keep the GIF if its comment matters.

faqs.question: What happens to transparent areas?

guide.title: About GIF and BMP
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

CompuServe introduced GIF in 1987. It compresses with LZW, draws each frame from a palette of up to 256 colors, and can do simple animation. Transparency is one-bit: a palette entry is either clear or solid, so soft edges cannot keep partial opacity. Short looping animations are the format's usual job.

Because of the palette, the colors in a GIF are already limited before any conversion happens.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP exports GIF as a single still or as an animation made from layers. ImageMagick reads GIF, but check which formats your install supports.
- **Web browsers:** Firefox and Chrome display GIF.
- **Mobile:** Safari and Chrome display GIF.

### GIF and BMP compared

- **Frames**: a GIF can hold many, a BMP only one.
- **Compression**: GIF is lossless through LZW, while a BMP commonly stores its pixels uncompressed, although lossless compression is available.
- **Color**: Version 5 of BMP arrived with Windows 98 and can record an ICC profile and an alpha channel.
- **Types**: image/gif and image/bmp.

This page decodes the first GIF frame in the browser as 8-bit RGBA, leaves metadata behind, and has ImageMagick write the BMP. The rest of the animation is ignored, and so are its delays and loop count.

### Other ways to convert GIF to BMP

- **ImageMagick:** `magick badge.gif'[0]' badge.bmp` saves the first frame. The page on image indexes says the first image is index 0, the second is 1, and so on, and the output format comes from the .bmp suffix.
- **Pillow:** `from PIL import Image; Image.open("badge.gif").convert("RGB").save("badge.bmp")` converts the picture to RGB, which BMP writing supports, and takes the BMP format from the filename extension.

### Problems with GIF files

- **The BMP is very large**: a BMP with uncompressed pixels can be bulky, which makes PNG or JPEG the more practical choice for handing files around.
- **An older program rejects the file**: software expecting an older bitmap header may need BMP3 or BMP2 output rather than ImageMagick's default BMP version.
- **Jagged transparency**: GIF transparency has no partial opacity, so soft edges were already hard before converting.
- **Gradients look different**: the small palette can change how a gradient is drawn.

- **Linux, Windows and Mac:** GIMP can export GIF stills or multilayer animations, and ImageMagick reads GIF.
- **Mobile and Web:** GIF display is covered by Chrome, Firefox and Safari.

CUR is the Windows cursor format. It is related to ICO but adds a hotspot, the coordinate of the pixel that registers a click. One CUR file can hold several sizes, and every size carries a hotspot of its own, while animated cursors use ANI instead of the ordinary CUR workflow. - **RealWorld Cursor Editor:** its page says it makes cursors from GIF images and has a wizard for quick conversions.

- **IcoFX:** choose File > Open, which imports a GIF as an image, then Image > Create Cursor From Image. Use File > Save As; cursor images are saved as Windows cursor files.

guide.title: Understanding GIF for PSD output
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

CompuServe introduced GIF, the Graphics Interchange Format, in 1987. Images are packed losslessly with LZW, each palette tops out at 256 colors, and simple animation is part of the design: one file can carry many images, spaced by delays measured in hundredths of a second. The July 1990 GIF89a revision added transparency, per-frame delays, comments and application data blocks. Transparency means choosing a single palette color to be invisible, so partial opacity is impossible. License fees for LZW from Unisys began in 1994, and the patents expired in 2003 and 2004. You see GIF in reaction images, stickers, icons and short looping clips.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - GIMP: can export a still picture or a layered animation.
  - ImageMagick: handles GIF input.
- **Web:**
  - Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox: display GIF.
- **Mobile:**
  - Safari and Chrome: display GIF on a phone.

### GIF and PSD compared

- **Names and types**: .gif is image/gif. .psd is Photoshop's native document, image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.
- **Color**: a GIF frame is capped at 256 palette entries. A PSD header lists one, eight, 16 and 32 bits as possible sample depths.
- **Structure**: a PSD keeps layers, masks and image resources in separate sections. A GIF holds frames.
- **Compression**: a PSD stores pixel data raw or encoded with RLE or ZIP, while GIF uses LZW.
- **Limit**: a PSD side can be no longer than 30,000 pixels, and PSB removes that cap.

Your browser decodes the GIF, and only its first frame is kept, so an animated GIF gives one still picture. The pixels pass through 8-bit RGBA, and ImageMagick writes the PSD. The page builds no layers and no animation frames.

### Other ways to convert GIF to PSD

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick sticker.gif sticker.psd` in a terminal. ImageMagick lists GIF and PSD as readable and writable.

### Problems with GIF files

- **Comments can drop out**: GIMP leaves out a GIF comment that uses characters beyond plain seven-bit text.
- **Soft edges look hard**: a GIF cannot retain partial opacity.
- **Banding**: a GIF holds at most 256 colors, so gradients can shift, and the PSD cannot restore the missing shades.
- **Later frames look partial**: frame disposal changes how later images cover earlier ones.

### What is a GIF file?

GIF dates to 1987 and CompuServe. Its GIF89a revision of July 1990 introduced transparency, animation timing, comments and application blocks. Compression is lossless LZW, but every image has a palette of 256 colors at most. Many images in one file, separated by delays in hundredths of a second, make a GIF animate. The media type is image/gif, and every major browser displays it.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - GIMP: writes still pictures or multilayer animations as GIF.
  - ImageMagick: supports reading GIF.
- **Web:**
  - Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox: show GIF in a tab.
- **Mobile:**
  - Safari and Chrome: handle GIF on a phone.

### GIF and SWF compared

- **Names and types**: .gif is image/gif. SWF has the media type application/vnd.adobe.flash.movie.
- **Color**: GIF frames use palettes capped at 256 colors, while the SWF here carries video.
- **Sound**: a GIF is silent. SWF can carry audio, but the file made here has none.
- **Animation**: GIF repeats a stack of images. A SWF is a timeline-based legacy format that can also hold vector graphics and bitmap video.

Shockwave Flash started at Macromedia, which Adobe acquired in 2005, and carried Flash animations, games and interactive content with ActionScript behind them. Adobe Flash Player reached end of life on 31 December 2020. This page makes a video SWF, so no ActionScript is added.

In your browser, FFmpeg runs as WebAssembly and chooses the video codec itself: its default for SWF is Sorenson Spark (FLV1) video at 200 kbit/s. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced, and the picture is capped at 1920 pixels and 30 frames per second, with each side trimmed to an even value.

### Other ways to convert GIF to SWF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i badge.gif -an -c:v flv badge.swf`. The `-an` option skips audio, and `-c:v` selects the video encoder. FFmpeg lists GIF and SWF as both readable and writable.
- **SWFTools gif2swf:** run `gif2swf -o badge.swf badge.gif`. The `-o` option sets the name of the SWF output file, and the GIF is the input file.

### Problems with GIF files

- **Banding in gradients**: a GIF is limited to 256 colors, which changes smooth gradients.
- **Frames overlay wrongly**: disposal settings decide how later images sit over earlier ones.
- **Comments can drop out**: an export from GIMP skips a GIF comment holding characters outside the seven-bit range.
- **Large GIFs**: a long, large GIF becomes many video frames, so conversion takes longer on a slow device.

The page decodes the GIF in your browser and ImageMagick writes the TGA. Only the first frame of an animated GIF is converted, so open the TGA in an image viewer afterwards to confirm it shows the frame you wanted.

- **Soft edges turn hard**: partial opacity is impossible in a GIF, so transparent edges are clear or opaque before the page reads them.

- **Frames cover each other wrongly**: each frame carries a disposal setting that controls what happens to the previous image, so a wrong setting smears the animation.
- **A comment is missing**: GIMP leaves out a GIF comment that has characters outside seven-bit ASCII.

guide.title: About GIF and TIFF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

GIF came from CompuServe in 1987. LZW compression, at most 256 palette colors per frame and basic animation define it. Transparency is all or nothing, since a color is either clear or solid. Looping clips, simple graphics, reaction images and stickers are typical jobs.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Mac, Windows and Linux:** GIMP exports stills or multilayer animations as GIF, and ImageMagick reads GIF.
- **Web and Mobile:** Chrome and Firefox display GIFs on the web, and Chrome and Safari do on mobile.

### GIF and TIFF compared

Aldus first published TIFF in 1986, and Adobe maintains it today. It stores one or more images in a tag-based structure, with lossless or lossy compression, high bit depth and even CMYK. It serves scanning and archiving, print and professional photography, and fax or document imaging. Because a TIFF can contain several images, scanned document sequences fit well, and preservation masters are another established use. Either .tif or .tiff marks a TIFF file.

Here your browser decodes the GIF and keeps its first frame as 8-bit RGBA, then ImageMagick writes an uncompressed TIFF with an alpha channel. A transparent GIF pixel stays transparent. Expect a file larger than the GIF and no animation. EXIF, XMP and color profiles are dropped. The result opens in Preview on a Mac, in Windows Photos, in GIMP and in Photoshop.

### Other ways to convert GIF to TIFF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick "input.gif[0]" still.tiff`. Index 0 is the first image in the file, and `[1]` would pick the second.
- **Pillow:** call `Image.open("input.gif").save("still.tiff")`; save picks the format from the extension. Call `seek` first to move to a later frame.
- **GIMP:** use File > Open on the GIF, then File > Export As and choose TIFF. The TIFF export dialog offers None, LZW, Pack Bits, Deflate and JPEG compression.

### Problems with GIF files

Partial opacity at soft edges is lost in a GIF. A GIF exported from GIMP is held to 256 colors, which can change gradients. How later images cover earlier ones depends on the disposal setting, so one frame pulled out alone can look incomplete. GIMP also omits a GIF comment with characters outside the seven-bit ASCII range.

guide.title: About GIF and WMV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

From CompuServe in 1987 comes GIF, a raster image format. Each frame uses LZW compression and a palette limited to 256 colors at most, and simple animation is supported. Short looping animations, reaction images and stickers are common uses.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Linux and Mac:** GIMP exports GIF as stills or multilayer animations, and ImageMagick reads GIF files.
- **Web and Mobile:** Chrome, Firefox and Safari handle GIF display.

### GIF and WMV compared

WMV, short for Windows Media Video, is a family of Microsoft video codecs usually kept in the ASF container. It was widely used for Windows video and streaming, and today it is a lossy legacy format. A WMV may hold Windows Media Video 7, 8 or 9 content, and ASF itself was designed for storing synchronized media and sending it across networks. Windows Media Player and VLC media player open WMV, which people mostly meet in older Windows video, screen recordings and Windows Media streaming.

In this converter FFmpeg, built for WebAssembly, re-encodes the GIF inside your browser. A GIF side beyond 1920 px shrinks to fit, a smaller GIF stays at its own size, and a rate above 30 fps sheds frames without shortening the clip. Because both sides are made even, an odd one loses a pixel. A GIF has no audio, so the WMV has none either. FFmpeg's defaults write MS-MPEG4 v3 video at 200 kbit/s, and the page offers no codec, bitrate or quality setting. Several GIFs convert as a batch, but each yields a separate video and they are not joined.

### Other ways to convert GIF to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i input.gif -an output.wmv` on your computer. The output format is guessed from the extension, and `-an` leaves audio out.

### Problems with GIF files

A GIF cannot keep partial opacity along soft transparent edges, and a GIMP export caps its palette at 256 colors, which can change gradients. Frame disposal decides how later images cover earlier ones, so a lone frame can look incomplete. GIMP drops a GIF comment holding characters beyond seven-bit ASCII.

guide.title: About GSM and MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is a GSM file?

GSM here means GSM 06.10, a lossy speech codec specified by ETSI for mobile telephony. Its RPE-LTP algorithm squeezes telephone speech into 13 kbit/s at an 8 kHz sample rate, packing each 160-sample block into a 264-bit frame. It turns up in voice recordings, telephony systems and voicemail, and it is a legacy format. The toast utility from libgsm writes compressed speech with the .gsm ending.

### Programs that open GSM files

- **Windows:** FFmpeg reads raw .gsm frames and exposes them as mono speech.
- **Mac:** Audacity opens GSM audio.
- **Linux:** toast and untoast, the libgsm command-line tools that encode and decode raw GSM speech.

FFmpeg is listed for Mac and Linux too, and VLC media player and SoX are also listed as programs that open GSM.

### GSM and MP3 compared

- **Purpose**: GSM is built for narrow telephone speech. MP3 is a general-purpose lossy audio format from MPEG, and it grew into the standard way to distribute downloadable music.
- **Packaging**: raw .gsm files and Microsoft's WAV GSM packing use different framing.
- **Tags**: MP3 keeps tags such as the title in ID3 data inside the file.
- **Playback**: MP3 plays on nearly every device, browsers included. GSM needs a program that knows the codec.

Here FFmpeg works in your browser, asking libmp3lame for 192 kbit/s and leaving out any video. MP3 cannot reach that rate at GSM's 8 kHz, so the file comes out at about 64 kbit/s. Selected files are processed in sequence, and each MP3 downloads on its own.

### Other ways to convert GSM to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i message.gsm -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k message.mp3`. The -b:a option sets the bitrate for the libmp3lame encoder.
- **FFmpeg, variable bitrate:** `ffmpeg -i message.gsm -q:a N -c:a libmp3lame message.mp3`, where N is a quality number. The libmp3lame q option sets a constant quality for variable bitrate instead of a fixed bitrate.
- **SoX:** `sox message.gsm message.mp3`. SoX lists GSM 06.10 and MP3 as optional formats, and MP3 writing needs SoX built with the LAME library.

### Problems with GSM files

- **Chirping or thin sound**: repeated GSM compression removes more information and can create audible chirping, so work from the first recording.
- **The file will not open**: raw .gsm and WAV format 49 are not interchangeable byte layouts.
- **A cut-off recording**: FFmpeg's raw reader expects complete 33-byte blocks, and a truncated last block is invalid to it. FFmpeg logs an error, and this page still writes the MP3 from what it could read, so download the file again if the end matters.

guide.title: About HDR and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is an HDR file?

HDR here is Radiance RGBE, a high-dynamic-range image format created by Greg Ward for the Radiance lighting simulation software. Each pixel is stored as red, green and blue bytes plus a shared exponent, four bytes in all, which allows a wider brightness range than ordinary 24-bit RGB. Files use run-length encoding and the extension .hdr or .pic; the registered media type is image/vnd.radiance. Radiance lighting simulations use RGBE images to represent calculated brightness, and the files also serve as environment maps for 3D rendering.

### Programs that open HDR files

- **Windows:** ImageMagick has an HDR coder for Radiance files in both directions.
- **Mac:** Adobe Photoshop is named in the format's registration among the users of the Radiance media type.
- **Linux:** Radiance, the original rendering system, which ships RGBE reading and writing code.

ImageMagick is listed on Mac and Linux as well, and Photoshop on Windows. Blender, GIMP and Luminance HDR are also listed as programs that open HDR.

### HDR and JPG compared

- **Range**: HDR keeps a wide brightness range. JPG is lossy and designed for photographs.
- **Pixels**: HDR bytes are not ordinary packed RGB, so software has to interpret the exponent.
- **Transparency**: JPG has no alpha channel.
- **Storage**: HDR uses four bytes per pixel rather than three single-precision floating-point channels.
- **Support**: JPG is widely supported. HDR opens in the programs listed above.

This page uses ImageMagick compiled to WebAssembly on the main thread. It reads a single image and passes no quality or mapping option, so you cannot steer the highlights. Each value above white is clamped to white, and the linear light is encoded to sRGB.

### Other ways to convert HDR to JPG

- **Radiance and ImageMagick:** run `pcond scene.hdr mapped.hdr` to condition the HDR for viewing, `ra_ppm mapped.hdr mapped.ppm` to write a PPM, then `magick mapped.ppm preview.jpg` to make the JPG.
- **ImageMagick:** `magick scene.hdr -colorspace sRGB preview.jpg` on your own machine.

### Problems with HDR files

- **Washed-out or blown highlights**: clipping bright values to the ordinary eight-bit range can discard highlight information. Choose an appropriate rendering instead of truncating samples.
- **Wrong colors in another program**: an HDR image needs software that interprets the shared exponent, because its bytes are not ordinary packed RGB pixels.
- **A file that will not read**: the extension alone does not identify the contents, and the registered Radiance description advises checking the complete header.

guide.title: About HEIC files
guide.markdown:
### What is a HEIC file?

A HEIC file is a photo stored in HEIF, the High Efficiency Image File Format, with its pictures compressed by HEVC, the H.265 video codec. HEIF is a container standard from MPEG, ISO/IEC 23008-12, first published in 2017. Apple made it the iPhone's photo format with iOS 11 and macOS High Sierra, and the iPhone 7 and later capture in it. Apple's reason was size: HEIF compresses photos better than JPEG.

One HEIF file can hold more than one picture. It may carry several images or an image sequence, a depth map, an alpha plane stored as an extra image, more than 8 bits per color channel, and Exif or XMP metadata.

Most HEIC files come from an iPhone or iPad: shared to another device, attached to a message, or copied to a computer. A Live Photo is a HEIC still paired with a short MOV video, so its HEIC file holds only the still picture. Some Android phones can save HEIF too, from Android 10 where the hardware supports it.

### Programs that open HEIC files

**Windows**

- Photos: opens HEIC after you add two Microsoft Store apps, the free HEIF Image Extension and the paid HEVC Video Extensions.
- Adobe Photoshop: reads HEIC on Windows only once both of those codecs are installed.

**Mac**

- Photos and Preview: open HEIC from macOS High Sierra 10.13, and both export JPEG copies.
- Adobe Photoshop: opens HEIC on macOS 10.13 or later.

**Linux**

- GIMP: imports HEIC when built with libheif, the open-source decoder this page also runs.
- ImageMagick: converts HEIC on the command line when compiled with libheif.

**Web**

- Safari: displays HEIC images from version 17.
- This page: decodes HEIC with libheif inside the page, so it works in Chrome, Edge and Firefox as well.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: Photos and Files open HEIC without any setup.
- Android: decodes HEIF from Android 9.

### HEIC and JPG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .heic or .heif, with image/heic and image/heif; .jpg or .jpeg, with image/jpeg.
- **Compression**: HEIC codes each picture as an HEVC still frame. JPEG uses the older 8x8 discrete cosine transform.
- **What one file holds**: a HEIF can bundle several images, depth data and an alpha plane. A JPG holds one picture.
- **Color depth**: HEIF allows more than 8 bits per channel; JPEG stores 8. This page decodes to 8-bit RGB.
- **Transparency**: a JPG has no alpha channel at all.
- **Metadata**: both carry Exif. The JPG made here doesn't get the HEIC's Exif or ICC profile.
- **Where it opens**: JPG opens almost anywhere. HEIC needs the support listed above.

The trade is reach for size. The JPG opens on any device and uploads to any site. It is lossy at quality 0.85, often larger than the HEIC, and carries none of the date, camera or location tags. A burst or multi-image HEIC gives only its primary picture.

### Other ways to convert HEIC to JPG

- **Finder (Mac)**: Control-click the photo, choose Quick Actions > Convert Image, then pick JPEG and a size. On some macOS versions the command sits under Quick Actions > More.
- **Preview (Mac)**: open the photo, choose File > Export, set Format to JPEG and click Save.
- **Photos (Mac)**: select the photos, choose File > Export > Export Photos, and set Photo Kind to JPEG.
- **Preview (iPhone, iOS 26)**: open the file, tap the actions button beside its name, tap Export, then choose JPEG.
- **iPhone camera setting**: Settings > Camera > Formats > Most Compatible makes new photos JPEG. Photos you already took stay HEIC.

### Problems with HEIC files

- **Windows says it can't open the file**: add the HEIF Image Extension and the HEVC Video Extensions, or skip them and convert here.
- **A website won't accept it**: many upload forms want JPG or PNG. Convert first, or use the [HEIC to PNG converter](/heic-to-png/) for a lossless copy.
- **"No images in HEIF"**: the file has no picture to decode. Copy the photo off the phone again and retry.
- **HEIC on one computer, JPG on another**: an iPhone may turn photos into JPEG when they're copied over USB. Choose Keep Originals in the iPhone's Photos settings to get the HEIC files.
- **A whole album to convert**: choose all the photos at once. Each JPG downloads as soon as it's ready.

guide.title: HEIC background and SVG conversion
guide.markdown:
### What is a HEIC file?

The High Efficiency Image File Format (HEIF) is MPEG-H Part 12 (ISO/IEC 23008-12), and its first edition appeared in 2017. It is a container rather than a codec, and HEIC is the variant whose images are coded with HEVC (H.265). One HEIF file may carry multiple pictures, sequences, depth beyond 8 bits, an alpha layer stored as a second image, and Exif or XMP metadata. Apple's photo apps started saving HEIF in iOS 11 and macOS High Sierra, and every iPhone since the iPhone 7 can shoot it. The Camera settings, under Formats, let you pick High Efficiency (HEIF) or Most Compatible (JPEG). The registered media types are image/heic and image/heif.

### Programs that open HEIC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP can import HEIC files; ImageMagick can read them through libheif.
- **Windows:** Windows Photos needs Microsoft's HEIF and HEVC extensions before it will open HEIC.
- **Windows and Mac:** Photoshop handles HEIC on macOS from 10.13, and on Windows after both Microsoft codecs are added.
- **Mac:** Preview on a Mac can open a HEIF file and export JPEG or PNG copies.
- **Mac and Mobile:** Photos from Apple opens HEIF and exports another format.
- **Web and Mobile:** Safari displays HEIC from version 17.0, and the OneDrive website previews uploaded HEIF photos.

### HEIC and SVG compared

HEIC stores a photograph with lossy HEVC compression. SVG is an XML format that describes shapes, text and embedded images, so it usually scales without losing sharpness. The SVG contains one `<image>` element that carries the picture as base64-encoded PNG data at the picture's own pixel width and height. Pixel images inside an SVG keep their original resolution when enlarged, so the result scales like a photo, not like a drawing. libheif decodes the HEIC's primary image to 8-bit RGB, and EXIF and ICC data are dropped.

### Other ways to convert HEIC to SVG

- **libheif and Inkscape:** run `heif-dec input.heic intermediate.png`. The heif-dec tool writes JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP or Y4M output from a HEIF input. Then, in Inkscape, choose File > Import for the decoded PNG and Path > Trace Bitmap. Tracing builds vector paths from the bitmap.

### Problems with HEIC files

- **Windows won't open it**: Windows needs Microsoft's HEIF Image Extension plus the HEVC Video Extensions. The HEIF extensions are free in the Microsoft Store, and the HEVC Video Extensions cost $0.99.
- **iPhone photos arrive as JPEG**: a USB copy can convert them to JPEG unless Photos is set to Keep Originals.
- **Error "No images in HEIF"**: the file holds no image, so fetch a fresh copy of it.

faqs.question: Is the MP4 the same quality as the HEVC video?

faqs.question: How long does a conversion take?
faqs.answer: The page sets no size limit and no timeout. FFmpeg runs on your device, single-threaded, so a long video takes as long as your device needs.

guide.title: About HTML and WebP files
guide.markdown:
### What is an HTML file?

Web pages and applications are written in HTML, a markup language. The WHATWG now keeps it as a Living Standard; its early revisions date from 1990 to 1995 and were worked on at CERN, then at the IETF. Elements and attributes mark up a page's structure, while stylesheets set its look and scripts add behavior. The media type is text/html. Links can point to separate resources, so a file need not hold every asset itself.

### Programs that open HTML files

- **Mac, Linux and Windows:** Visual Studio Code is an editor with HTML highlighting, completion and formatting, and Firefox renders local HTML documents; it opens a file with Ctrl+O, or Command+O on a Mac.

### HTML and WebP compared

WebP is an image format from Google, first released in 2010, whose lossy mode builds on the VP8 video codec. It also supports lossless compression, transparency and animation. Every current major browser displays it. An HTML file stays editable and searchable, while a WebP is a fixed picture of how the page looked.

Here the file is parsed without running anything, then laid out 1280 px wide in an off-screen sandbox and drawn as an image. Scripts, links and frames are removed, and only data: images and fonts in the file are used. Height follows the page with a ceiling of 4096 px, and there is no quality setting.

### Other ways to convert HTML to WebP

- **Playwright and Pillow:** with a Playwright page showing your document, call `page.screenshot(path="page.png", full_page=True)`, then `Image.open("page.png").save("page.webp")` in Pillow. Pillow picks the format from the extension.
- **Chrome DevTools and GIMP:** in DevTools, open the Device Toolbar, choose More options, then Capture full size screenshot. Open the screenshot in GIMP, choose File > Export As, pick WebP, and tick Lossless if you want no quality loss.
- **Chrome DevTools and cwebp:** take the same full size screenshot, then run `cwebp screenshot.png -o page.webp`. cwebp accepts PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP or raw Y'CbCr input.

### Problems with HTML files

Missing linked files can leave an offline HTML document without its pictures or styling, and an incorrect character encoding can make its text render incorrectly. Content that a script would build is not drawn here, because nothing is run. Embed what the page needs inside the file before converting.

guide.title: About images and PDF
guide.markdown:
### What is an image file?

Image files come in two kinds. Raster formats such as JPEG, PNG, HEIC and WebP store a grid of pixels. Vector formats such as SVG store shapes and redraw them at any size. A PDF is a third thing: it describes pages, and a picture is one thing a page can hold. People turn images into a PDF when a form or an office wants a document, when a stack of receipts or scans should travel as one file, or when pages must print the same way on every machine.

This page reads almost any image a phone, camera or computer makes:

- **Web and everyday formats**: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, AVIF, ICO and SVG.
- **Apple photos**: HEIC and HEIF.
- **Editing and print formats**: TIFF, PSD, TGA, JPEG XL and JPEG 2000.
- **Camera RAW**: DNG, Canon CR2, CR3 and CRW, Nikon NEF, Sony ARW, Fujifilm RAF, Olympus ORF and Panasonic RW2.

PDF itself comes from Adobe. John Warnock's Camelot project, begun in 1991, had become PDF by 1992, and it has been an ISO standard since 2008.

### Programs that open the PDF you make

The images above open in many programs; what matters next is where the PDF opens.

**Windows**

- Microsoft Edge: Windows' built-in PDF reader, with tools to highlight and draw.
- Adobe Acrobat Reader: Adobe's free reader, which also fills in forms and adds signatures.

**Mac**

- Preview: opens the PDF, rearranges its pages by dragging thumbnails and adds notes.

**Linux**

- Okular and GNOME's Document Viewer: the usual desktop readers.

**Web**

- Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari: show a PDF in a tab with no extra software.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: the Files and Books apps.
- Android: Google Drive's viewer or the Acrobat Reader app.

### Images and PDF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: each image format has its own, such as .jpg with image/jpeg or .heic with image/heic. A PDF is .pdf with application/pdf.
- **What the file holds**: an image file holds one picture, or the frames of one animation. A PDF holds pages that can mix text, vector shapes and pictures.
- **Compression inside the PDF**: PDF stores pictures with lossless Flate or with JPEG. Here a JPEG keeps its own data. An opaque photo in another photo format (HEIC, AVIF, lossy WebP, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000 or RAW) is stored as a JPEG at quality 92. Everything else, a transparent photo or an SVG included, is stored losslessly as pixels.
- **Transparency**: see-through pixels become a soft mask, so they stay see-through on the page.
- **Page size**: one point per pixel. A 3,000 x 2,000 photo makes a page about 41.7 x 27.8 inches; viewers zoom to fit it on screen.
- **Metadata**: a JPEG's orientation tag turns its page, and its ICC profile is kept. The rest of its Exif, GPS location included, and its XMP are left out.
- **Animation**: an animated GIF or WebP gives its first frame.

### Other ways to put images in a PDF

- **Finder (Mac)**: select the images, Control-click them and choose Quick Actions > Create PDF. Pages follow the order you selected the files in.
- **Preview (Mac)**: open an image, choose File > Export, pick PDF from the Format menu and click Save.
- **Preview (iPhone, iOS 26)**: open the image, tap the actions button next to its name, tap Export and choose PDF.
- **Adobe Acrobat (Windows, Mac)**: choose File > Create > PDF from File, select the image and click Open. Acrobat accepts BMP, JPEG, GIF, TIFF, PNG, PCX, RLE and DIB images.

### Problems with images in a PDF

- **More than 100 images**: one PDF made here stops at 100. Split the set and make two PDFs.
- **Over 250 MB**: the page tells you how many images fit. Remove some, or make two PDFs.
- **An image over 50 megapixels**: the page names the file. Scale it down in an editor first; a 48-megapixel phone photo fits.
- **Pages in the wrong order**: use Move up and Move down before making the PDF. Afterwards, Preview on a Mac can drag pages into place.
- **Pages print huge or tiny**: page sizes follow the pixels, so choose your print dialog's option to fit or scale to the paper.
- **Text in a scan can't be searched**: run text recognition in a PDF editor such as Adobe Acrobat.

Image to PDF turns your images into one PDF document in your browser, without uploading them. One image makes a one-page PDF; several make one PDF with a page for each image, in the order you set.

Each page is the size of its image, so a photo isn't cropped and a screenshot isn't stretched. A JPG is placed in the PDF as it is, and other photos are stored as high-quality JPEG, so a PDF of phone photos stays about the size of the photos. Screenshots, scans and drawings keep every pixel.

- Transparent areas show the white of the page.

guide.title: JFIF background and ICO conversion
guide.markdown:
### What is a JFIF file?

JFIF is the JPEG File Interchange Format, a thin wrapper that lets JPEG data move between programs. Eric Hamilton at C-Cube Microsystems wrote it first, and version 1.02 dates from 1992. ITU-T T.871 and ISO/IEC 10918-5 later standardized it. JFIF adds an APP0 segment labeled JFIF right after the JPEG start-of-image marker, and that segment may hold a small thumbnail. Most files called JPEGs are JFIF files. The pixels inside are lossy JPEG data at 8 bits per color channel, with no alpha channel. A .jfif file has the media type image/jpeg, and JFIF files may also use .jpg, .jpeg, .jpe, .jfi or .jif.

### Programs that open JFIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick's JPEG reader handles JFIF, and Mozilla Firefox displays JPEG/JFIF data.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays JFIF, and so does Safari on mobile.

### JFIF and ICO compared

ICO is Microsoft's image format for interface icons. A file can hold more than one image, it uses little-endian byte order, and its media type is image/vnd.microsoft.icon. Most people know ICO as the favicon format.

Here the browser decodes the JFIF and ImageMagick writes the ICO. This ICO contains a single image rather than several sizes. Anything larger than 256 px on its long side is scaled down to fit a 256 by 256 box, proportions intact; smaller pictures are left at their size. The image sits inside the ICO as PNG. Open the finished ICO in an image viewer to confirm the whole picture is there and nothing was cropped. Pixels go through 8-bit RGBA, and EXIF, ICC and XMP metadata is not kept.

### Other ways to convert JFIF to ICO

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick portrait.jfif -resize '256x256>' portrait-icon.ico`. In the geometry, the `>` means a picture shrinks only when it is larger than the box.

### Problems with JFIF files

- **No see-through areas**: a JFIF stores no alpha channel, so the icon starts out fully opaque.
- **A reader rejects the JFIF**: some JPEG extensions outgrow a particular JFIF reader, so try a baseline-compatible export.
- **Unsure what the file holds**: the .jfif suffix can contain ordinary JPEG data, so identify its encoding before re-encoding.

faqs.question: How do I change a JFIF to JPG without converting?

faqs.question: Is a JFIF file the same as a JPG?

faqs.question: Why do images I save from the web end in .jfif?
faqs.answer: Some Windows PCs pick .jfif when saving JPEG pictures from a browser. The picture is a normal JPEG; only the ending is unusual.

faqs.question: Does converting JFIF to JPG lower the quality?

faqs.question: Should I rename or convert my JFIF files?

faqs.question: Will the JPG look the same as the JFIF?

faqs.question: Can I open a JFIF file on a Mac?

guide.title: About JFIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a JFIF file?

JFIF stands for JPEG File Interchange Format. The JPEG standard says how to compress a photo but leaves out details that programs need to swap files reliably, such as the color model and the pixel shape. JFIF fills that gap with a minimal wrapper, which is why most files people call JPEGs are really JFIF files.

The wrapper is small. A JFIF file opens with JPEG's start-of-image marker, followed at once by an APP0 segment labeled JFIF. That segment gives a version number, the resolution in dots per inch or per centimeter, and room for an optional small thumbnail. The compressed picture follows. Eric Hamilton of C-Cube Microsystems wrote the first versions, with 1.02 dating from 1992, and the format was later standardized as ITU-T T.871 and ISO/IEC 10918-5.

JFIF files may end in .jfif, .jfi, .jif, .jpe, .jpeg or .jpg, and all of them are image/jpeg. You see the .jfif ending mostly on Windows, where some PCs save pictures downloaded from a browser that way. The file is fine; the ending is what trips up other apps and upload forms.

### Programs that open JFIF files

**Windows**

- Photos: opens .jfif files as ordinary pictures.
- Paint: opens .jfif pictures for quick edits.
- Browsers: show a .jfif dragged into a tab.

**Mac**

- Preview: opens the file and exports a JPEG copy.
- Adobe Photoshop: opens the file and exports a JPG.

**Linux**

- GIMP: opens the JPEG data inside and exports a .jpg.
- ImageMagick: `magick photo.jfif photo.jpg` writes a re-encoded JPG copy.

**Web**

- Every major browser shows JFIF files, since they are served as image/jpeg.

**Mobile**

- Phone browsers display a .jfif image from a web page like any JPEG.

### JFIF and JPG compared

- **Image data**: the same JPEG compression, with 8x8 blocks, a discrete cosine transform and Huffman coding.
- **Extensions and media type**: .jfif is one of several JFIF endings, next to .jpg and .jpeg. All share image/jpeg.
- **Header**: a JFIF file starts with an APP0 segment. Many camera JPGs carry an Exif segment instead, or as well, with shooting details.
- **Extras**: JFIF can hold a tiny thumbnail and a resolution; Exif adds camera settings, dates and location.
- **Color**: 8 bits per channel and no transparency, in both.
- **What this page does**: decodes the picture, then writes a fresh JPEG at quality 0.85 from its pixels, without the thumbnail, EXIF, ICC profile or XMP.

Renaming is the lossless option: change .jfif to .jpg and every byte stays the same. Convert instead when you want a fresh file or many files at once without renaming each.

### Other ways to convert JFIF to JPG

- **Rename on Windows**: in File Explorer, turn on endings with View > Show > File name extensions in Windows 11, or the File name extensions box on the View tab in Windows 10. Then rename the file and replace .jfif with .jpg.
- **Rename on a Mac**: select the file, open Get Info, and change the ending in Name & Extension. To see endings everywhere, turn on Show all filename extensions in Finder > Settings > Advanced.
- **Preview (Mac)**: open the file, choose File > Export, pick JPEG from the Format pop-up menu and click Save. A JFIF is already JPEG data, so exporting compresses it again.
- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: open the .jfif, then use File > Export > Export As with JPG as the format and click Export.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: open the .jfif, choose File > Export As, change the ending of the name to .jpg and click Export.

### Problems with JFIF files

- **An upload form says the type isn't allowed**: it checks the ending. Convert the file here or rename it to .jpg.
- **Saved images keep arriving as .jfif**: some Windows PCs choose that ending for JPEG downloads. Rename them after saving, or convert a batch here.
- **An app won't open the file**: it may not know the .jfif ending. Rename it to .jpg and try again.
- **You can't see a .jfif ending at all**: Windows and macOS hide many endings by default. Turn them on as described above, or check the file's type in its properties or Get Info window.
- **You need transparency or lossless edits**: JPEG has neither. Use the [JFIF to PNG converter](/jfif-to-png/).

guide.title: About JFIF and SVG
guide.markdown:
### What is a JFIF file?

JFIF, the JPEG File Interchange Format, is a container convention for JPEG-compressed pictures that fixes the color space and pixel aspect ratio. Files ending in .jfif contain ordinary JPEG image data. Some browsers and Windows tools save pictures this way, and photographs are often exchanged in it. The compression is lossy and there is no alpha transparency. Because a JFIF can be read as a regular JPEG, any program that opens JPEG pictures opens it too.

### Programs that open JFIF files

- **Windows:** Windows Photos opens it, and ImageMagick reads it with its JPEG reader.
- **Web and Mobile:** Google Chrome displays JFIF.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays JFIF.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays JFIF.

GIMP is also listed as a program that opens it.

### JFIF and SVG compared

- **Kind**: JFIF is a pixel format. SVG is an XML-based W3C vector format that describes shapes, paths and text mathematically.
- **Scaling**: true SVG vectors stay sharp at any size. A photo placed inside an SVG keeps its original resolution.
- **Use**: SVG suits logos, icons and diagrams. JFIF suits photographs.

On this page your browser decodes the picture and a canvas builds the SVG. The resulting SVG contains one image element, with the picture stored as a base64 PNG sized to its own pixel dimensions. Nothing is resized, and the pixels pass through 8-bit RGBA.

### Other ways to convert JFIF to SVG

- **Inkscape, embedding:** File > Import, choose Embed rather than Link so the picture is stored inside the file, then File > Save As and pick Inkscape SVG.
- **Inkscape, tracing:** File > Import, select the picture, run Path > Trace Bitmap, then save as SVG. This produces paths, but the manual says a trace suits dark silhouettes against a bright background and will disappoint if you expect a faithful copy.
- **Photopea:** File > Open, then File > Export As > SVG.

### Problems with JFIF files

- **A .jfif file may simply hold ordinary JPEG data**: identify its encoding before deciding to re-encode.
- **A reader rejects the file**: some JPEG extensions exceed a particular JFIF reader's capabilities, so try a baseline-compatible export.
- **No transparency to keep**: a JFIF carries JPEG data, so transparency is not something it can store.

guide.title: Understanding JFIF to WEBP
guide.markdown:
### What is a JFIF file?

Short for JPEG File Interchange Format, JFIF lets JPEG data travel between programs and platforms. Eric Hamilton wrote it at C-Cube Microsystems, with version 1.02 dating from 1992, and it later became ITU-T T.871 and ISO/IEC 10918-5. The media type is image/jpeg, and the name may end in .jpg, .jpeg, .jpe, .jfi, .jfif or .jif. Most pictures sold or shared as JPEGs turn out to be JFIF files, and a small embedded thumbnail can ride along inside one.

### Programs that open JFIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick's JPEG reader handles JFIF, and Firefox displays it.
- **Web and Mobile:** Chrome displays JFIF directly on both, and Safari does on mobile.

### JFIF and WebP compared

WebP is an open-source image format developed by Google and announced on 30 September 2010. The lossy mode reuses intra-frame coding from the VP8 video codec on still pictures, and lossless WebP uses a separate method. WebP files are RIFF containers. RFC 9649 describes the format and is where the image/webp media type is registered. The format also supports lossless compression, transparency, animation, ICC profiles and Exif or XMP metadata. JFIF holds plain JPEG data, so it has no alpha channel and no animation, while WebP can have both.

The browser decodes your JFIF and encodes the pixels as WebP through 8-bit RGBA. Metadata is dropped on the way, and the page offers no quality control. Quality already lost to JPEG compression stays lost, so the point of this conversion is the format that your site or app wants, and not a better picture.

### Other ways to convert JFIF to WebP

- **ImageMagick:** `magick picture.jfif picture.webp` converts by extension. ImageMagick's format list marks both JPEG and WebP as readable and writable. Reading or writing WebP needs ImageMagick's WebP delegate library.

### Problems with JFIF files

Behind a .jfif suffix sits ordinary JPEG data, so identify the file before deciding to re-encode it. Some JPEG files exceed what a particular JFIF reader handles, and a baseline-compatible export may solve that. Because JPEG cannot store transparency, a cut-out logo saved as JFIF has a solid background, and no converter can bring the transparency back.

guide.title: About JIF and JPEG files
guide.markdown:
### What is a JIF file?

JIF stands for JPEG Interchange Format. It is the original file layout described in the JPEG standard for storing JPEG-compressed images, and JFIF and Exif largely replaced it, so .jif files are rare now. The pictures use ordinary lossy JPEG compression and carry no alpha transparency. The later JFIF convention allows .jif among its extensions, yet a .jif is far less common than the .jpg that most JFIF files carry. JFIF can carry a small embedded thumbnail, and it was standardized as ITU-T T.871 in May 2011.

### Programs that open JIF files

- **Linux, Windows and Mac:** GIMP, which imports JPEG for editing, is listed among the programs that open JIF files, and ImageMagick reads JPG.
- **Mobile and Web:** Chrome, Firefox and Safari can display JPEG.

XnView and IrfanView are listed as openers for JIF as well.

### JIF and JPEG compared

JPEG is named for the committee behind it, the Joint Photographic Experts Group. ISO/IEC 10918-1 defines it, and it is the usual format for digital camera output. The .jpg and .jpeg extensions mean one and the same format. Editors scale quality from 0 to 100, and the same number in two editors need not give the same compression or appearance. Baseline JPEG compresses 8x8 pixel blocks, using a discrete cosine transform plus Huffman coding, and stores 8 bits per color channel. Because JPEG is lossy, keep the JIF if you may want the first pass later.

Here your browser decodes the JIF to 8-bit pixels and saves a JPEG at quality 0.85, so the lossy step runs a second time.

### Other ways to convert JIF to JPEG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick input.jif compatible.jpeg`; its command-line page shows this `magick in out` form for changing formats.
- **Pillow:** call `Image.open("input.jif").save("compatible.jpeg")`. Pillow reads and writes JPEG, and its quality option defaults to 75.
- **GIMP:** choose File > Open on the JIF, then File > Export As, give the file a .jpeg name and click Export. The JPEG export dialog has a Quality setting.

### Problems with JIF files

A picture that needs transparency has to start in another format, because a JIF has no alpha channel.

guide.title: Understanding JP2 for JPEG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a JP2 file?

JP2 wraps a JPEG 2000 codestream in the Part 1 file format, developed by the Joint Photographic Experts Group. JPEG 2000 compression can be lossy or lossless, and the codestream inside decides which, not the wrapper. The wrapper can store color profiles, opacity information and other metadata. A JP2 reader ignores wrapper extensions it does not understand. Its standard extension is .jp2 and its registered media type is image/jp2. The Library of Congress serves digitized maps and newspapers as lossy JP2 images.

### Programs that open JP2 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - ImageMagick: lists read and write support for JP2.
  - OpenJPEG: an open-source JPEG 2000 codec written in C.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Adobe Photoshop: opens a JP2 file when you select it in the latest version.

### JP2 and JPEG compared

- **Names**: .jp2 is image/jp2; JPEG uses .jpg or .jpeg.
- **Compression**: JPEG 2000 allows lossy or lossless coding, while JPEG is lossy.
- **Opacity**: a JP2 may store opacity, which JPEG cannot hold because it has no alpha transparency.
- **Metadata**: the JP2 wrapper can carry color profiles and other metadata alongside the picture.
- **Use**: JP2 suits archives and service images, while JPEG is used for web photographs, camera output and email attachments.
- **After converting**: open the JPEG and compare it with the JP2, since a lossy JPEG cannot return to the original and the JP2 should be kept.

The JP2 is opened as a single picture by ImageMagick running inside your browser tab, and the page sets no JPEG quality. The page refuses a file larger than about 537 megapixels.

- **Few cameras write it**: most cameras do not encode JPEG 2000, so a JP2 is rarely straight out of a camera.

guide.title: JPEG background and JPEG conversion
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPEG file?

The format's committee, the Joint Photographic Experts Group, started in 1986. ITU-T T.81 from 1992 and ISO/IEC 10918-1 from 1994 specify the core. Baseline JPEG discards information: the picture is split into blocks eight pixels square, every block is run through a discrete cosine transform, and the result is Huffman-coded. Each color channel gets 8 bits, and with no alpha channel there is no transparency or layers. A progressive variant exists too, which shows a rough picture first and refines it while the rest downloads. Cameras and scanners have JPEG built in, and its media type is image/jpeg. Both .jpg and .jpeg are used for one and the same format.

### Programs that open JPEG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP opens JPEG for editing, and ImageMagick can read it.
- **Web:** Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox display JPEG.
- **Mobile:** Safari and Google Chrome display it too.

### JPEG and JPEG compared

Both sides of this conversion are the same format, so the only change is a new encode. The page decodes your JPEG in the browser and writes another one at quality 0.85. That number is an encoder setting, and the same value can mean different quality in different programs; GIMP, for example, defaults to 85. EXIF, ICC and XMP data don't come along, and the pixels pass through 8-bit RGBA. Convert once from the original, because each lossy encode starts from what the last one left behind.

### Other ways to convert JPEG to JPEG

- **GIMP:** open the JPEG, choose File > Export As, enter a new name and pick JPEG under Select File Type. In the JPEG options, set the quality level from 0 to 100. GIMP also lets you choose which metadata to keep.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick original.jpeg -quality 90 rewritten.jpeg`. ImageMagick's JPEG writer scales quality by its own rules.
- **Preview:** on a Mac, open the JPEG and choose File > Export. In the Format pop-up menu select JPEG, set the quality, give the copy a new name and click Save.

### Problems with JPEG files

- **Transparency is lost**: JPEG stores no alpha channel, so choose another format if you need clear areas.
- **An old photo frame shows nothing**: it may not read progressive JPEG, so export with progressive turned off.
- **Quality numbers don't match**: the same number in two editors does not guarantee the same compression or appearance.
- **Layers are flattened**: only one merged image is stored, so keep your layered project file.

guide.title: JPEG and JPG: one format, two endings
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPEG file?

JPEG is one image format with several file endings. The name comes from the Joint Photographic Experts Group, and the standard was published as ITU-T T.81 in 1992 and ISO/IEC 10918-1 in 1994. Most digital cameras and scanners write it, and it remains the web's usual format for photos.

The endings differ because of history, not format. MS-DOS and early Windows file names allowed three characters after the dot, so .jpg became standard on PCs, while Macs and Unix systems used .jpeg. Both stuck. JFIF, the wrapper most JPEG files use, allows .jpg, .jpeg, .jpe, .jfi, .jfif and .jif, and every one is served as image/jpeg.

JFIF was first written by Eric Hamilton at C-Cube Microsystems, with version 1.02 dated 1992. It was later standardized as ITU-T T.871, approved in May 2011, and as ISO/IEC 10918-5. A JFIF file can carry a small thumbnail of the picture, and camera photos usually carry an Exif block with shooting details as well.

### Programs that open JPEG files

Every image program reads both endings. These matter for this job:

**Windows**

- File Explorer: renames a .jpeg to .jpg once file name extensions are shown.
- Photos: opens either ending the same way.

**Mac**

- Finder: renames the file and asks you to confirm the new ending.
- Preview: exports a fresh JPEG when you want a new file rather than a new name.

**Linux**

- Any file manager: renames the file.
- GIMP and ImageMagick: write a new JPEG when you need one.

**Web**

- Every browser shows both endings.

**Mobile**

- Phone photo apps treat .jpg and .jpeg alike.

### JPEG and JPG compared

- **Format**: identical. The same compression, the same data and the same media type, image/jpeg.
- **Extension**: four letters or three. Programs treat both alike.
- **Compression**: lossy, in 8x8 blocks with a discrete cosine transform and Huffman coding, with an optional progressive mode that loads a coarse picture first.
- **Color**: 8 bits per channel, with no alpha channel and no layers.
- **Metadata**: Exif, the ICC profile and XMP stay when you rename the file and are dropped when you convert it here.
- **What this page changes**: it decodes the image and encodes it again at quality 0.85. You get a new file, not a renamed one.

### Other ways to turn a .jpeg into a .jpg

- **Rename it on Windows**: in File Explorer, turn on View > Show > File name extensions (on Windows 10, the File name extensions box on the View tab), then rename the file.
- **Rename it on a Mac**: select the file, choose File > Get Info, edit Name & Extension, then confirm Use .jpg.
- **Preview (Mac)**: choose File > Export, pick JPEG from the Format pop-up menu and click Save. Re-exporting re-compresses the image.
- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: choose File > Export > Export As, pick JPG and click Export.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: choose File > Export As, give the file a .jpg name and click Export. Every JPEG save re-compresses the image.

### Problems with JPEG files

- **An upload form wants .jpg**: some forms check only the ending. Rename the file, or convert it here.
- **Downloads arrive as .jfif**: some Windows PCs save web images with a .jfif ending. Rename them to .jpg.
- **The date and location disappeared**: converting drops Exif. Rename instead when you need to keep them.
- **Quality slips after repeated saves**: every encode loses a little, so don't convert the same file again and again.

guide.title: About JPEG files
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPEG file?

JPEG takes its name from the Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee that began work on it in 1986. The standard was published as ITU-T T.81 in 1992 and as ISO/IEC 10918-1 in 1994, and its US patents ran out on 27 October 2006. It was built for photographs, and most digital cameras and scanners still write it.

Most files called JPEG are JFIF files: a small wrapper, first written by Eric Hamilton at C-Cube Microsystems, that lets the compressed picture move between programs and platforms. Camera photos usually add an Exif block with the date, exposure and sometimes the location.

A JPEG becomes a PDF when someone wants a document rather than a picture: a photographed receipt for an expense claim, a signed page, a scan for a school or office portal.

### Programs that open JPEG files

**Windows**

- Photos: views and prints JPEGs. Printing to Microsoft Print to PDF also saves a PDF.
- Paint: crops or resizes a photo before you convert it.

**Mac**

- Preview: opens JPEGs and exports them as PDF.
- Photos: keeps the library your camera and phone photos land in.

**Linux**

- GIMP: edits and re-exports JPEGs.
- Gwenview and GNOME's Image Viewer: quick desktop viewers.

**Web**

- Every major browser displays JPEG, and printing an opened photo from the print dialog can save it as a PDF too.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: Photos and Files.
- Android: Google Photos and the phone's gallery app.

### JPEG and PDF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .jpg or .jpeg, sometimes .jpe or .jfif, with image/jpeg; .pdf with application/pdf.
- **Compression**: JPEG discards fine detail in 8x8 blocks, which usually shrinks a photo to between a tenth and a twentieth of its raw size. A PDF can carry JPEG data as it is or store pixels with lossless Flate. This converter does the second: it decodes the photo and embeds it as PNG data. No further detail is lost, but the PDF is usually larger than the JPEG.
- **Color**: JPEG stores 8 bits per channel and has no alpha channel, so there is no transparency to carry.
- **Layout**: a JPEG has pixels but no page. The PDF page takes the photo's size, one point per pixel, with no margin.
- **Text**: a PDF can hold real, searchable text, but one made from a photo holds only the picture.
- **Metadata**: Exif, the ICC profile and XMP stay in the JPEG; the PDF gets none of them.

### Other ways to convert JPEG to PDF

- **Finder (Mac)**: select the photos in the order you want, Control-click them and choose Quick Actions > Create PDF. You get one PDF with a page per photo.
- **Preview (Mac)**: open the JPEG, choose File > Export, pick PDF from the Format pop-up menu and click Save.
- **Preview (iPhone, iOS 26)**: open the photo, tap the actions button next to its name, choose Export and then PDF.
- **Adobe Acrobat (Windows, Mac)**: choose File > Create > PDF from File, select the JPEG and click Open.

### Problems with JPEG files

- **The photo is sideways**: phones often record rotation as an Exif tag instead of turning the pixels, and programs that ignore the tag show the photo sideways. [Image to PDF](/image-to-pdf/) reads that tag and turns the page to match.
- **The PDF is too big to email**: this page stores the photo losslessly. Image to PDF embeds a JPEG's own data instead, so its PDF stays close to the photo's size.
- **A .jfif file**: it's a JPEG with another ending. Rename it to .jpg if a program refuses it.
- **"Image decode failed."**: the JPEG is damaged, for example by a download that didn't finish. Get a fresh copy.
- **Blocky edges or smeared text**: that's JPEG compression in the original, and the PDF shows it as it is. Start from the sharpest copy you have.
- **A scanned page is tilted or has dark edges**: the PDF shows the photo exactly as taken. Crop and straighten it in your photo app first.
