guide.title: About JPEG and TGA
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPEG file?

The committee behind JPEG, short for Joint Photographic Experts Group, issued its core specification first as ITU-T T.81 (1992) and then as ISO/IEC 10918-1 (1994). Pixels are grouped in 8x8 blocks, passed through a cosine transform and Huffman coded, which discards detail for good. Every color channel is limited to 8 bits in a JPEG, which also has no transparency and no layers. Both the .jpg and .jpeg endings name this format, whose media type is image/jpeg, and cameras and scanners write it by default.

### Programs that open JPEG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP opens a JPEG as an editable image, and ImageMagick can read it.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox show a JPEG directly in a tab.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays JPEG on a phone.

### JPEG and TGA compared

- **Compression**: JPEG is lossy and typically makes an image ten to twenty times smaller than its raw pixels. TGA keeps the pixels as they are, and can add run-length encoding.
- **Transparency**: a 32-bit TGA adds an 8-bit alpha channel to RGB, which a JPEG never has.
- **Color depth**: a 24-bit TGA keeps 8 bits in each color component.
- **Uses**: TGA turns up in video editing and game development, while JPEG is built into cameras and scanners.

The decoding step belongs to your browser; ImageMagick then takes the pixels and produces the Targa file. Everything passes through 8-bit RGBA, which is why the metadata does not follow. Photographs contain few repeated runs for run-length coding to exploit, so expect a file larger than the JPEG.

- **GIMP:** Load the JPEG in GIMP, pick File > Export As and export it as TGA. The TGA dialog has a Use RLE compression checkbox and an Origin choice of Bottom left or Top left.
- **ImageMagick:** `magick photograph.jpeg texture_copy.tga` writes the Targa file. ImageMagick reads and writes both JPEG and TGA.
- **Tacent View:** `tacentview -c photograph.jpeg --out tga` runs in command-line mode, so no window opens. Its JPEG load option exifo=true applies the photo's EXIF orientation.

### Problems with JPEG files

- **Cutouts are missing**: the JPEG stores no transparency, so any mask has to be drawn in an editor afterwards.
- **Layers are gone**: a JPEG flattens the picture, so an editable stack of layers survives only in your project file.
- **Legacy displays balk**: certain old picture frames cannot show a progressive JPEG, and a baseline copy avoids that.
- **Quality settings are not portable**: one quality figure gives different results from one editor to the next.

guide.title: About JPEG and TIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPEG file?

The format is named for the Joint Photographic Experts Group, which started work on it in 1986 and saw the core specification appear as ITU-T T.81 in 1992. Baseline JPEG works lossily, applying a discrete cosine transform to 8x8 pixel blocks and then Huffman coding. Its progressive mode first shows a coarse picture, then refines it while more data arrives. Each channel holds 8 bits and there is no alpha. GIMP's default quality is 85 on the usual 0 to 100 scale. The registered media type is image/jpeg.

### Programs that open JPEG files

- **Linux, Mac and Windows:** GIMP imports JPEG so you can edit it, and ImageMagick reads JPG files.
- **Web and Mobile:** Chrome renders JPG on both, with Firefox on the web and Safari on mobile.

### JPEG and TIF compared

Aldus and Microsoft developed TIFF as a tag-based raster wrapper. Revision 6.0 dates from 1992, and Adobe now holds the specification. A file can use various compression methods and color representations and can hold several images. Archival master copies and high-bit-depth work are well-established uses. The names .tif and .tiff both mean TIFF, whose media type is image/tiff.

Here your browser decodes the JPEG to 8-bit RGBA and ImageMagick writes the .tif without any compression. The result is larger than the JPEG and holds no more detail. Camera EXIF, XMP and the ICC profile stay behind.

### Other ways to convert JPEG to TIF

- **Preview on a Mac:** open the JPEG, choose File > Export, pick TIFF in the Format pop-up menu, and click Save.
- **GIMP:** open the photograph, choose File > Export As, export it as a TIFF image, and pick the Compression in the TIFF dialog. JPEG is the one lossy choice there.
- **Pillow:** call `Image.open("input.jpeg").save("delivery.tif", compression="tiff_lzw")`. Without libtiff, Pillow writes only uncompressed TIFF files.

### Problems with JPEG files

- A JPEG holds no transparent pixels, so artwork that needs them has to start in another format.
- JPEG has no layer stack; keep the project file if you may edit the artwork again.
- Quality numbers differ between editors, so equal settings do not promise equal compression or appearance.

guide.markdown:
### What is a JPG file?

The committee behind JPEG, the Joint Photographic Experts Group, began its work in 1986, and the standard came out twice: T.81 from the ITU in 1992, then ISO/IEC 10918-1 in 1994. Baseline JPEG is lossy: it divides the image into 8x8 pixel tiles, applies a DCT to every tile and finishes with Huffman coding. A JPG has 8 bits per color channel, no alpha channel and no layers. The .jpg and .jpeg extensions are interchangeable names for it, and image/jpeg is its media type.

### Programs that open JPG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP imports JPEG for editing, and ImageMagick reads JPG.
- **Web and Mobile:** Chrome shows JPG.
- **Web:** Firefox shows JPG.
- **Mobile:** Safari shows it as well.

Windows Photos and Preview on macOS also open it.

### JPG and CUR compared

- **Purpose**: JPG stores photographs. CUR is the Windows cursor format, related to ICO but with coordinates for the active pointer location.
- **Hotspot**: the pixel that does the clicking is called the hotspot. One CUR can hold images at several dimensions, each with hotspot information of its own.
- **Transparency**: CUR supports alpha. JPG does not, so the converted image is opaque.
- **Compression**: JPG is lossy, so the picture's quality is already settled before it becomes a cursor image.

The browser decodes the JPG first, and then ImageMagick writes the CUR with a single image in it. A larger JPG is scaled down, with its proportions intact, until both sides are 256 px or less. The page has no hotspot setting.

### Other ways to convert JPG to CUR

- **GIMP:** open the JPG and choose File > Export As, type a name ending in .cur and click Export. Hot spot X and Hot spot Y in the dialog place the pointer's click point.

### Problems with JPG files

- **Transparency is lost**: a JPEG export cannot keep transparent pixels, so a pointer with a shaped outline needs a format that has alpha.
- **Progressive JPEG**: some older photo frames reject it, so try an export with progressive mode turned off.
- **Quality numbers**: editors scale quality differently, so equal numbers can compress differently.
- **Layers**: no layer stack survives inside a JPG, so keep your project file.

guide.title: About JPG and JFIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPG file?

Began in 1986, JPEG was the work of the Joint Photographic Experts Group committee. ISO/IEC 10918-1 followed in 1994, after ITU-T T.81 in 1992. Each color channel takes 8 bits, and no alpha channel exists. The .jpg and .jpeg extensions name one and the same format, and digital cameras and scanners build it in. Inside, baseline JPEG splits the picture into 8x8 pixel blocks and compresses them lossily.

### Programs that open JPG files

- **Windows, Linux and Mac:** GIMP imports JPEG for editing, while ImageMagick can read JPG.
- **Web and Mobile:** Chrome is a JPG viewer on both web and mobile; Firefox covers the web and Safari covers mobile.

### JPG and JFIF compared

JFIF (JPEG File Interchange Format) is a minimal wrapper that lets JPEG data move between programs and platforms, and it pins down the color space and pixel aspect ratio. JFIF began with C-Cube Microsystems' Eric Hamilton; version 1.02 is from 1992, and it was approved as ITU-T T.871 in May 2011. A JFIF file begins with the JPEG start-of-image marker and then an APP0 segment labeled JFIF. Most files people call JPEGs are JFIF files, so anything that opens a regular JPEG reads one.

The extensions .jpg, .jpeg, .jpe, .jfi, .jfif and .jif are all allowed for JFIF files, sharing the media type image/jpeg. Some browsers and Windows tools save pictures under the .jfif name.

Your browser decodes the JPG into 8-bit pixels and saves a new JPEG named .jfif, at quality 0.85. This is a second lossy pass, and camera tags, XMP and the color profile are not kept.

### Other ways to convert JPG to JFIF

- **Pillow:** call `Image.open("input.jpg").save("output.jfif", format="JPEG")`. Pillow writes standard and progressive JFIF files.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick input.jpg output.jfif`. Its JPEG format, listed as read and write, is described as the JFIF format.
- **libjpeg-turbo:** run `djpeg -outfile pixels.ppm input.jpg`, then `cjpeg -outfile output.jfif pixels.ppm`.

### Problems with JPG files

- Progressive JPEG is refused by some older photo frames, so export without it for such a target.
- Editors do not map one quality number to the same compression or appearance.
- Transparency cannot survive JPEG export; pick a format with alpha instead.
- Any editable layer stack is gone in a JPEG, so retain the project file.

guide.title: About JPG and JPEG XL files
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPG file?

JPG, or JPEG, is the lossy photo format from the Joint Photographic Experts Group; work started in 1986, and its US patents lapsed on 27 October 2006. The baseline method, covered by ITU-T T.81 (1992) and ISO/IEC 10918-1 (1994), cuts the image into 8x8 pixel blocks and applies a discrete cosine transform and Huffman coding to each. A typical setting leaves 1/10 to 1/20 of the uncompressed size. Each channel holds 8 bits, there is no alpha, and .jpg and .jpeg mean the same thing. Cameras and scanners write it widely, and its media type is image/jpeg.

### Programs that open JPG files

- **Mac, Windows and Linux:** GIMP can import JPEG for editing, and ImageMagick opens JPG.
- **Mobile and Web:** Chrome displays JPG on web and mobile, Safari does so on mobile, and Firefox on the web.

### JPG and JXL compared

JPEG XL comes from the JPEG committee as ISO/IEC 18181. It handles lossy and lossless coding, alpha channels, animation and progressive decoding, along with high bit depth, wide color gamuts and HDR. Existing JPEG files can be recompressed by it without any loss. A .jxl file is either a bare codestream or a box-based container, and its media type is image/jxl.

This page does not recompress losslessly. Your browser decodes the JPG to 8-bit RGBA pixels and ImageMagick encodes them as a lossy JXL with default settings. Pixel values change, and there is no quality control. Metadata is dropped.

### Other ways to convert JPG to JXL

- **cjxl:** run `cjxl input.jpg output.jxl`; by default it recompresses the JPEG losslessly.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick input.jpg converted.jxl`, which needs the JPEG XL delegate library.
- **GIMP:** open the JPG, pick File > Export As, and save the result as a JPEG XL file. GIMP 2.10.34 added export, limited to 8-bit lossless.

### Problems with JPG files

- JPEG offers no alpha channel, so transparent pixels cannot survive an export to it.
- An editable layer stack is not preserved in JPEG, so hold on to the project file.
- Older photo frames may reject progressive JPEG; turn progressive mode off when you export for one.

guide.title: About JPG files
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPG file?

A JPG is a JPEG image, the lossy photo format standardized by the Joint Photographic Experts Group in the early 1990s. The three-letter .jpg ending comes from MS-DOS and early Windows, which allowed only three characters after the dot. A .jpg and a .jpeg file are the same format.

JPEG splits a picture into 8x8 pixel blocks, converts each block into frequencies with a discrete cosine transform, and rounds away the fine detail the eye is least likely to miss. A quality number, usually 0 to 100, decides how much goes. GIMP starts at 85, and the same number can mean different things in different programs. Every time a JPEG is edited and saved, it is compressed again and loses a little more. A progressive JPEG stores the picture in passes, so a browser can show a coarse version first and sharpen it as the rest arrives.

JPG is everywhere: cameras and scanners write it, and almost every website and app reads it. People turn one into a PNG to edit it without adding more loss, or because a site, template or app asks for PNG.

### Programs that open JPG files

**Windows**

- Photos: the default viewer for JPG, with crop and rotate tools.
- Paint: opens a JPG and saves a copy as PNG.
- Adobe Photoshop: edits JPGs and exports them in other formats.

**Mac**

- Preview: opens a JPG and exports it as PNG.
- Finder: Quick Actions convert a JPG without opening it.

**Linux**

- GIMP: edits a JPG and exports it as PNG.
- ImageMagick: converts JPGs in bulk from the command line.

**Web**

- Every browser displays JPG.

**Mobile**

- Every phone's photo app opens JPG, on iPhone, iPad and Android alike.
- iPhone: the camera saves JPG instead of HEIC when Settings > Camera > Formats is set to Most Compatible.

### JPG and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .jpg or .jpeg with image/jpeg; .png with image/png.
- **Compression**: JPEG is lossy, with a discrete cosine transform and Huffman coding. PNG is lossless DEFLATE: every pixel comes back exactly as stored.
- **Color depth**: JPEG stores 8 bits per channel. PNG allows 1 to 16 bits per sample, in grayscale, indexed or truecolor.
- **Transparency**: PNG has an optional alpha channel. JPEG has none.
- **Animation**: PNG can animate as APNG. JPEG is always a still.
- **Metadata**: JPEG commonly carries Exif and an ICC profile. PNG can hold an ICC profile, and its third edition adds an eXIf chunk for Exif. This converter carries none of it across.
- **Typical use**: JPEG for photos; PNG for screenshots, text and graphics with hard edges.

Converting changes the container, not the picture. The PNG holds exactly the pixels the JPG decodes to: no lost detail returns, no blockiness goes away, and nothing becomes transparent.

### Other ways to convert JPG to PNG

- **Preview (Mac)**: open the JPG, choose File > Export, pick PNG from the Format pop-up menu and click Save.
- **Finder (Mac)**: Control-click the file, choose Quick Actions > Convert Image, then PNG and a size. On some macOS versions it is under Quick Actions > More.
- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: choose File > Export > Export As, pick PNG and click Export.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: choose File > Export As, give the file a .png name and click Export.
- **Paint (Windows)**: open the JPG and save a copy with PNG as the file type.

### Problems with JPG files

- **Blocky patches or halos around text**: those are compression artifacts, and a PNG keeps them. Start from the original photo or a higher-quality export.
- **You need a transparent background**: converting won't remove the background. Erase it in an editor, then save as PNG.
- **Quality drops after repeated edits**: each JPEG save compresses again. Convert once to PNG, edit the PNG, and export a JPG only at the end.
- **The PNG is too large to send**: that's normal for photos. Share the JPG and keep the PNG for editing.
- **Camera details have gone**: EXIF isn't carried into the PNG, so keep the original if you need the date or location.
- **"Image decode failed."**: your browser couldn't read the JPG, most often because a download or copy was cut short. Fetch the file again.

guide.title: Understanding JPG to PPM
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPG file?

Its name honors the Joint Photographic Experts Group, a committee that started in 1986. ITU-T T.81 (1992) holds the core specification, and ISO/IEC 10918-1 followed in 1994. Baseline JPEG is lossy. It transforms 8x8 pixel blocks with a discrete cosine transform, then packs the result with Huffman coding. Color channels get 8 bits each, and there is no alpha channel or layer support. Quality usually runs on a 0 to 100 scale, yet one number can mean different results in different programs. Both .jpg and .jpeg name this format. US patents on it lapsed in October 2006.

### Programs that open JPG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads JPG from the command line, and GIMP imports it for editing.
- **Web and Mobile:** Chrome displays JPG on both, Firefox on the web and Safari on phones.

### JPG and PPM compared

PPM is the color member of the Netpbm family. Each pixel carries red, green and blue samples, in a binary form that starts with P6 or a plain-text form that starts with P3. The maximum sample value can run from 1 to 65535, and PPM has no alpha channel. The media type image/x-portable-pixmap is conventional but not registered with IANA, and a raw PPM can hold a sequence of images with no separators.

The browser decodes your JPG and the page writes the pixels out with ImageMagick. Compression is gone, so the file balloons. Metadata is dropped, and quality lost to JPEG stays lost.

### Other ways to convert JPG to PPM

- **Netpbm:** `jpegtopnm photo.jpg > photo.ppm` handles color input. A grayscale JPG yields PGM, not PPM.
- **GIMP:** load the JPG, use File > Export As with a .ppm name, and select ASCII or raw data formatting.
- **ImageMagick:** `magick photo.jpg photo.ppm` converts by extension and writes color PPM.

### Problems with JPG files

JPEG export cannot keep transparent pixels, so for transparency use a format that has alpha. Some older photo frames reject progressive JPEG, and an export with progressive mode disabled fixes that. Equal quality values in two editors need not give equal compression or equal looks. Layers do not survive in a JPEG, so keep your project file for later edits.

guide.title: About JPG and RGB
guide.markdown:
### What is a JPG file?

JPG is the everyday name for JPEG, the format of the Joint Photographic Experts Group. Its specification appeared as ITU-T T.81 (1992), then as ISO/IEC 10918-1 (1994). A JPG compresses a picture with a discrete cosine transform followed by Huffman coding, then adds a header that records its width and height. Every color channel gets 8 bits and nothing is kept for transparency. Both endings, .jpg and .jpeg, mean the same thing, and the registered media type is image/jpeg. Cameras and scanners write it by default.

### Programs that open JPG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** a JPG opens for editing in GIMP, and ImageMagick can read it.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox display a JPG without extra software.
- **Mobile:** Safari displays a JPG on a phone.

### JPG and RGB compared

- **Header**: a JPG records its size and settings inside the file, whereas raw RGB records none.
- **Compression**: JPG is lossy, and raw samples are uncompressed.
- **Samples**: the raw output is red, green and blue values with no alpha, one byte each.
- **Name clash**: an .rgb ending may also mean an SGI image, which is laid out differently.

A raw RGB file is nothing but red, green and blue samples in a row. With no header, nothing in it tells a program the width, height or bit depth. The browser decodes the JPG and passes the pixels to ImageMagick, which writes them as raw samples. They pass through 8-bit RGBA first, so the metadata is left behind. You must tell any reader the width, height and format yourself.

### Other ways to convert JPG to RGB

- **ImageMagick:** `magick photo.jpg -depth 8 RGB:samples.rgb` writes raw red, green and blue samples. The `-depth` option sets the depth of raw formats such as RGB, whose depth the file does not record.
- **Pillow:** `from PIL import Image; pixels=Image.open('photo.jpg').convert('RGB'); open('samples.rgb','wb').write(pixels.tobytes())` saves the pixels as raw bytes. Pillow reads JPEG files, and `tobytes()` returns the unprocessed pixel data.

### Problems with JPG files

- **Blocky or smudged areas**: raw RGB shows the flaws exactly as decoded and can't repair them.
- **No transparency**: a JPG has no alpha channel, so the samples have nothing to hold.
- **Some old players stall**: progressive JPGs can be rejected by aging photo frames, and re-saving without progressive scans fixes it.
- **The quality scale varies**: one editor's quality value is not another's, so identical settings can give different files.

guide.markdown:
### What is a JPS file?

JPS is a stereoscopic 3D image format that stores the left and right views side by side in one JPEG file. A typical JPS arranges the two eye views for crossed-eye viewing. The VRex proposal described the stereo layout in a JPEG APP3 marker, and a JPS can carry an embedded preview thumbnail. It is used for stereoscopic 3D photos and for 3D viewers and VR headsets, with JPEG compression and lossy quality.

### Programs that open JPS files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** sView reads JPS stereo markers and treats .jps as a crossed-eye image pair.
- **Windows:** StereoPhoto Maker opens JPS directly and lets you pick the stereo arrangement, and Stereoscopic Player documents JPS descriptor support.
- **Mac:** Pro for Mac is the vendor's Wine-based package of StereoPhoto Maker.
- **Mobile:** On a phone, sView for Android.

XnView MP and IrfanView are also listed as programs that open JPS.

### JPS and PDF compared

- **Content**: a JPS is one picture holding two views. A PDF keeps a fixed page layout.
- **Stereo data**: a PDF page here is a flat picture, so the viewer cannot rearrange the eyes.
- **Layout choices**: StereoPhoto Maker supports side-by-side, above/below and interlaced layouts, and treats the file type separately from the stereo layout.
- **Pages**: a PDF can hold many pages, while a JPS is a single picture.
- **Support**: PDF opens in Adobe Acrobat Reader, Preview on macOS and any web browser.

The browser decodes each file and a separate PDF is written for it. The PDF has one page the size of the image, and the picture is embedded losslessly as a PNG. Metadata is not carried over.

### Other ways to convert JPS to PDF

- **Pillow (Python):** call Image.open on the JPS, then save it under a .pdf name.
- **ImageMagick:** `magick stereo.jps stereo.pdf`.

### Problems with JPS files

- **The views look swapped or stretched**: selecting the wrong stereo arrangement displays the eye views incorrectly.
- **A reader will not infer the layout**: a .jps extension does not guarantee that every reader knows it, and StereoPhoto Maker asks you to specify it.
- **Quality drops after editing**: re-saving a JPS through JPEG output applies the selected compression quality again, so keep the source.

guide.title: About KTX and PNG
guide.markdown:
### What is a KTX file?

Khronos Texture version 1, KTX, is a container for OpenGL and OpenGL ES textures. A file records the texture dimensions and the GL format that its loader needs. It can hold cubemap faces and texture arrays, stores mipmap levels from largest to smallest, and may carry named metadata such as texture orientation. KTX2 is a separate container whose structure is incompatible with the first.

### Programs that open KTX files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** KTX Software with its libktx library reads KTX 1 and 2, though it is a developer library and not a photo viewer. FFmpeg reads KTX 1.0 files that use ASTC formats, and kram is a command-line utility that decodes supported KTX and KTX2 textures.
- **Windows and Linux:** PVRTexTool is a texture GUI and command-line tool that lists KTX and KTX2 among its inputs.
- **Mac:** kramv is a viewer for supported KTX and KTX2 textures on Apple Silicon Macs.

### KTX and PNG compared

- **Purpose**: KTX feeds a GPU, while PNG is a lossless picture meant for people.
- **Contents**: KTX can hold mipmaps, cubemap faces and arrays. A PNG holds one picture.
- **Compression**: a KTX may use a GPU compression format, but a PNG is always lossless.

This page reads only the original KTX format, and only when the texture is uncompressed 8-bit RGB or RGBA. It takes the first image in the file and writes its pixels as a PNG. A compressed or non-8-bit texture is refused with a message, and nothing is saved. An RGBA texture keeps its transparency, and an RGB texture has none to keep.

### Other ways to convert KTX to PNG

- **PVRTexToolCLI:** `PVRTexToolCLI -i texture.ktx -d extracted.png -noout` decodes the texture and writes a PNG. The -i option accepts KTX and KTX2 files, -d saves a decompressed file with the extension you give it, and -noout stops the .pvr file from being written.
- **Tacent View:** `tacentview -c texture.ktx --out png` converts from the command line without opening the GUI. Tacent View loads KTX and KTX2 and saves PNG, on Windows and Linux.

### Problems with KTX files

- **The picture is upside down**: a texture may look upside down when its coordinate origin differs from the viewer, so inspect KTXorientation and flip the PNG in an editor.
- **The suffix was changed**: renaming a KTX2 file to .ktx does not convert it.
- **Unsupported internal format**: a KTX texture does not guarantee that every OpenGL implementation supports its internal image format.
- **Compressed texture**: decode it first in a tool such as PVRTexTool, which can save a decompressed copy.

faqs.question: Is M2V the same as MPEG-2?

faqs.question: Can I convert more than one M2V in one go?

faqs.question: What happens to a damaged M2V?

guide.title: About M2V and MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is an M2V file?

A file ending in .m2v is an MPEG-2 video elementary stream: the picture data of MPEG-2 (ITU-T H.262, also called MPEG-2 Part 2) with nothing else attached. Sound lives elsewhere. A program stream bundles one video with its audio, and a transport stream can multiplex several channels, so an M2V on its own naturally gives a silent result. These streams mostly come out of DVD authoring tools and MPEG-2 encoders.

### Programs that open M2V files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg and ffplay decode MPEG-2 video and name .m2v for raw MPEG-2 output. VLC media player reads this kind of stream through its MPEG-I/II elementary-video demuxer.
- **Windows and Mac:** Telestream Switch documents M2V input.

### M2V and MP4 compared

- **Contents**: an M2V stream holds video only, whereas an MP4 can hold video, audio, subtitles and metadata.
- **Codec**: MPEG-2 (H.262) goes in and H.264 comes out.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4.

Encoding is done by libx264 (ultrafast preset, CRF 32, zerolatency tune). Width and height are limited to 1920 pixels and the frame rate to a ceiling of 30. A smaller picture is never enlarged, so a standard-definition stream keeps its size apart from rounding an odd side down to even. The source never had audio, so the MP4 has none.

### Other ways to convert M2V to MP4

- **FFmpeg video only:** `ffmpeg -i pictures.m2v -c:v libx264 -an viewing.mp4` writes H.264 video and requests no audio, which suits a source that has none.
- **FFmpeg separate audio:** `ffmpeg -i pictures.m2v -i soundtrack.wav -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -shortest complete.mp4` brings in a separate audio file as a second input, and -shortest ends the output with the shorter input. Check that the start and end line up before you share the result.

### Problems with M2V files

- **The MP4 is silent**: the M2V had no audio to begin with. Add the soundtrack separately, as the second method above shows.
- **A stream looks wrong in a player**: program and transport streams are built differently from an elementary stream, so choose the stream type your player expects.
- **The file is cut off or damaged**: FFmpeg usually still converts what it can read, so the MP4 can come out shorter than you expect.

guide.title: About M4A files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

M4A is the ending for MPEG-4 files that carry sound and no picture. The container is the same one MP4 video uses; the A just tells software to expect audio. Apple adopted the ending for unprotected music, and its media type is audio/mp4.

Inside, most M4A files hold AAC, the Advanced Audio Coding defined in MPEG-4 Part 3. AAC was designed to sound better than MP3 at the same bitrate, and it handles sample rates from 8 to 96 kHz and bitrates up to 512 kbps. Some M4A files hold Apple Lossless instead, which keeps the sound exactly but is much larger.

You meet M4A files in several places. Songs sold through iTunes used AAC. The iPhone's Voice Memos app saves its recordings as M4A, and audio ripped or imported with Apple's apps often ends up in the format too. Protected purchases use a sister ending, .m4p, and can't be played outside Apple's own software.

### Programs that open M4A files

**Windows**

- Media Player: Windows 11's built-in player handles M4A.
- iTunes: plays M4A and can make MP3 copies.
- VLC: plays it with its own decoders.

**Mac**

- Music: Apple's player and library, which can convert songs to MP3.
- QuickTime Player: plays a single file.

**Linux**

- VLC: plays M4A out of the box.
- Audacity: imports M4A for editing once its FFmpeg library is installed.

**Web**

- Every major browser plays AAC in an MP4 container, so an M4A plays when dragged into a tab.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: Music, Files and Voice Memos.
- Android: plays AAC in .m4a files on every version.

### M4A and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .m4a with audio/mp4; .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Codec**: M4A usually holds AAC and sometimes Apple Lossless. MP3 is one codec, MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, standardized as ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993 and extended by ISO/IEC 13818-3 in 1995.
- **Compression**: both AAC and MP3 are lossy and rely on a model of hearing to drop sounds listeners are unlikely to notice. AAC does more with fewer bits.
- **Range**: MP3 runs from 32 to 320 kbps at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz. At 128 kbps an MP3 is about an eleventh the size of the same music on a CD.
- **Tags**: an M4A keeps titles and artwork in MPEG-4 metadata; an MP3 keeps them in ID3 blocks. This page leaves out cover art and doesn't promise that other tags come across, so check them after converting.
- **Support**: MP3 plays almost everywhere, from browsers to old car stereos. M4A plays in browsers and on phones but trips up some older hardware and software.
- **History**: MP3 was developed at Fraunhofer IIS from the late 1980s with partners in the MPEG audio group. Its patent licensing program ended on 23 April 2017.

What this page writes: an MP3 encoded with LAME at a constant 192 kbps. A minute of audio comes to about 1.4 MB, whatever the bitrate of the M4A you start from.

### Other ways to convert M4A to MP3

- **Apple Music (Mac)**: in Music > Settings > Files > Import Settings, set Import Using to MP3 Encoder, select the songs, then choose File > Convert > Create MP3 Version. Protected purchases can't be converted, and going from one lossy format to another costs some quality.
- **iTunes (Windows)**: choose Edit > Preferences, click General, then Import Settings, and set Import Using to MP3 Encoder. Select the songs and choose File > Convert > Create MP3 Version. Store purchases convert only if they are iTunes Plus songs.
- **VLC (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: open Media > Convert/Save, add the M4A with the Add button, pick an MP3 audio profile under Profile, choose where to save it as the Destination file, then press Start.
- **FFmpeg (command line)**: `ffmpeg -i input.m4a -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3`. MP3 encoding needs an FFmpeg build that includes the LAME library.

### Problems with M4A files

- **A car stereo or old player ignores the file**: it may not know AAC in MP4. An MP3 copy plays on nearly everything.
- **The file ends in .m4p**: it may be copy-protected, and a protected file can't be converted. An unprotected one converts with the [M4P to MP3 converter](/m4p-to-mp3/).
- **The MP3 is larger than the M4A**: the original used a low bitrate, which is common for voice recordings. That is normal, since this page always writes 192 kbps.
- **The artwork is missing**: cover art isn't carried into the MP3. Add it back in your player, for example with Get Info in Apple Music.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: the audio couldn't be decoded, perhaps because the file is cut short or isn't really an M4A. Play it first to check.
- **You plan to edit the audio**: every lossy save costs a little. The [M4A to WAV converter](/m4a-to-wav/) makes an uncompressed copy to work on, with no second lossy step.

guide.title: Understanding M4A to WMA
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

Files ending in .m4a are audio-only MPEG-4, a form Apple took up for unprotected music. AAC, defined in MPEG-4 Part 3, is what most of them hold, though some carry lossless Apple Lossless (ALAC). AAC is a lossy design meant to beat MP3 at a given bitrate, with support for sample rates between 8 and 96 kHz and bitrates reaching 512 kbps. iTunes songs were sold as AAC. All the major browsers play AAC inside MP4, Android plays .m4a on every release, and the media type is audio/mp4.

### Programs that open M4A files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity needs its optional FFmpeg library before it opens M4A, and protected files are excluded. ffplay, the player that comes with FFmpeg, opens it from the command line, using FFmpeg's decoders.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox play AAC in MP4, though Firefox can depend on system codecs.
- **Mobile:** VLC and mpv for Android handle it, depending on the media inside.

### M4A and WMA compared

Microsoft developed WMA as a family of audio codecs kept in the ASF container. Its standard version is lossy, a Lossless variant also exists, and the format is proprietary. It served Windows media libraries and older portable music players, and Windows Media Player, VLC media player and foobar2000 open it.

This page decodes the M4A and writes WMA with the wmav2 encoder at 192 kbps. The video stream is dropped, and the rest of the choices are left to FFmpeg's defaults. AAC to WMA is a lossy-to-lossy step, so there is no quality gain.

### Other ways to convert M4A to WMA

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i song.m4a -vn song.wma` drops any video stream and writes a WMA.
- **WavePad for Windows:** open the M4A, choose File > Save As and select WMA. WMA saving is offered only in the Windows version.

### Problems with M4A files

The FFmpeg library route cannot import DRM-protected recordings. If you import several recordings into one project window, the last file's tags replace the project tags. M4A import in that program depends on the optional library being installed, and a file that library cannot decode will not open.

guide.title: Understanding M4R to WAV
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4R file?

M4R is the file extension for iPhone ringtones. It is MPEG-4 audio with AAC sound, renamed to .m4r so that iTunes and the iPhone use it as a ringtone. An MPEG-4 file keeps its container structure apart from the encodings of its tracks, and it can store track metadata next to the encoded samples. Apple's GarageBand export limits a ringtone to 30 seconds.

### Programs that open M4R files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** MediaInfo inspects the container and stream properties, though it does not play audio, and its format registry includes .m4r.
- **Windows and Mac:** Switch accepts M4R input, and copy-protected files are excluded.
- **Windows:** WavePad lists .m4r as readable and writable here but not on Mac.
- **Mobile:** GarageBand for iPhone can make a custom ringtone from eligible audio and install it. Switch lists Android M4R input support.

Audacity's AAC export accepts .m4r as an MP4 ringtone filename.

### M4R and WAV compared

WAV is an audio container developed by Microsoft and IBM and based on RIFF. It usually holds uncompressed PCM, so files are large but exact, and it has a 4 GB file size limit. It suits recording, editing and professional sound production, and it often serves as a source format before compression. You can open it in Audacity, VLC, Windows Media Player or a web browser.

The page decodes the M4R and writes pcm_s16le, 16-bit little-endian PCM, with no video stream. Nothing is trimmed, so the WAV runs as long as the ringtone does. AAC detail that was lost stays lost.

### Other ways to convert M4R to WAV

- **WavePad for Windows:** open the M4R, choose File > Save As, select WAV and review the encoding.
- **Switch:** add the M4R, pick WAV as the Output Format, look over Encoder Options and press Convert.
- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i tone.m4r -vn tone.wav` writes a WAV and skips any video stream.

### Problems with M4R files

WavePad does not decode copy-protected input, so its M4R support does not cover protected tones. In GarageBand, a dimmed song is one not yet downloaded to the iPhone. When a ringtone runs over the limit, GarageBand proposes a shorter cut before it finishes the export.

guide.title: Understanding M4V to AVI
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4V file?

M4V is Apple's video format, a close sibling of MP4 used for videos in iTunes and the Apple TV app and for phone and tablet video. It typically carries H.264 video with AAC audio in an MPEG-4 container. HandBrake treats its .m4v and .mp4 outputs as the same MPEG-4 container. Apple's iTunes Store sold some files with FairPlay DRM protection. FFmpeg's MOV/MP4 demuxer lists .m4v among the extensions it handles. The MPEG-4 family stores timed audio and video tracks and metadata in boxes, and playback depends on the encodings inside.

### Programs that open M4V files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC handles MPEG-4 containers with the usual MPEG-4 video and AAC audio codecs. FFmpeg lists M4V input explicitly, though processing also needs the relevant decoders.
- **Mac:** On Apple devices, QuickTime Player and the Apple TV app play M4V.

### M4V and AVI compared

AVI is a container introduced by Microsoft in 1992, based on RIFF. It interleaves video and audio and can hold many codecs, so the extension alone says nothing about quality. Modern features are poorly supported, which makes it a legacy format, yet you will still meet it in old Windows video, capture files and archives. VLC media player, Windows Media Player and QuickTime Player open AVI.

The page writes MPEG-4 Part 2 video, tagged xvid and without B-frames, plus MP3 sound at 96 kbps. Output is deinterlaced where needed. A frame over 1920 pixels on its long side is scaled down, a rate over 30 fps is thinned, and both sides are rounded to even numbers. Nothing is scaled up.

### Other ways to convert M4V to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i recording.m4v recording.avi` writes an AVI from the command line.
- **Prism for Windows:** add the M4V, set the Output Format to AVI, review Encoder Options and press Convert.

### Problems with M4V files

An unsupported codec can stop playback even when a player recognizes the container. Renaming the suffix cannot fix a damaged file or an unsupported encoding. A recording whose writing ended before the required metadata was finished may not open at all. If you need a different file than M4V provides, convert a copy and keep the original.

guide.title: About MAC and PNG
guide.markdown:
### What is a MAC file?

A .mac file can hold an image in the legacy MacPaint format, the picture format of the drawing program released with the original Apple Macintosh in 1984. MacPaint pictures are black and white on a fixed canvas of 576 by 720 pixels, and the data is normally run-length encoded, although a file with the compression turned off can still conform to the format. The data fork alone does not carry all the classic Mac file identification information, so a copy without a MacBinary or BinHex wrapper may not be recognized as a picture. Today the format turns up in legacy Macintosh graphics and retro computing archives.

### Programs that open MAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Deark is a free extractor whose raster formats include MacPaint, and Netpbm's macptopbm is a command-line reader that writes PBM.
- **Mac:** GraphicConverter lists MacPaint import and export in its vendor manual.

### MAC and PNG compared

- **Colors**: MacPaint is black and white. A PNG can hold full color but here carries the same two tones.
- **Canvas**: MacPaint has a fixed canvas, and its writers crop oversized input.
- **Compression**: both formats are lossless.

The page runs ImageMagick compiled to WebAssembly on the main thread and reads the file as one image. Nothing is uploaded. The result is a PNG of the monochrome bitmap, written at the full size of the canvas, so there are no colors to lose.

### Other ways to convert MAC to PNG

- **Netpbm:** `macptopbm old_drawing.mac > drawing.pbm; pnmtopng drawing.pbm > drawing.png` converts in two steps through PBM. If the picture comes out shifted, the file may have a 128-byte prefix, and macptopbm has an `-extraskip` option for it.
- **Deark:** `deark -m macpaint old_drawing.mac` selects the MacPaint module, which is needed because not every MacPaint file can be autodetected. Deark converts pictures to formats such as PNG.

### Problems with MAC files

- **The picture is shifted**: a 128-byte Finder prefix was probably added in transfer. Try macptopbm with `-extraskip`.
- **The file will not open on classic Mac OS**: the data fork needs a MacBinary or BinHex wrapper to be identified.
- **Oversized art is cropped**: the fixed canvas cannot hold a larger picture.

guide.title: About MJPEG and MP4
guide.markdown:
### What is an MJPEG file?

Motion JPEG is a way of coding video: each frame is compressed as an ordinary JPEG picture and the frames follow one another, with no prediction between them. It is therefore an encoding and not a container. AVI files carry it under the MJPG FourCC, following a profile that OpenDML documented in 1996 and 1997, and QuickTime can hold it as well. Cameras and capture hardware commonly record it, and editors sometimes work in it before exporting something lighter for delivery.

### Programs that open MJPEG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player lists MJPEG A/B decoding, and FFmpeg reads raw MJPEG.

### MJPEG and MP4 compared

- **Compression**: MJPEG compresses every frame on its own, so size follows the encoded images. H.264 also exploits similarity between frames.
- **Container**: MJPEG is an encoding that sits in AVI, QuickTime or a raw stream, and MP4 is a container.
- **Editing**: because every frame stands alone, editors can cut at any frame, while H.264 is made for delivery.
- **Reach**: every major browser plays MP4.

Conversion happens in your browser with FFmpeg, and nothing is uploaded. libx264 does the work, set to ultrafast with CRF 32 and the zerolatency tune. A picture above 1920 pixels on either side is scaled down, and 30 frames a second is the ceiling. Interlaced frames are cleaned up on the way, and audio, if there is any, becomes AAC at 96 kbps. After converting, play the MP4 and check its length and speed against the original recording, since the page does not preview the result for you.

### Other ways to convert MJPEG to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i camera.mjpeg -c:v libx264 -an camera_view.mp4` encodes H.264 and drops audio from the command.
- **FFmpeg with a chosen pixel format:** `ffmpeg -i clip.mjpeg -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:v libx264 clip_player.mp4` also sets the pixel format to yuv420p.

### Problems with MJPEG files

- **The file will not parse**: raw MJPEG and multipart JPEG are different formats, and a wrong assumption can stop FFmpeg.
- **A saved frame is not a valid JPEG**: an extracted frame can lack a Huffman table that a standalone decoder needs.
- **The result has no sound**: a raw MJPEG stream normally carries none.

guide.title: About MKV and WMV
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

The Matroska container is written in EBML, a binary relative of XML, and traces back to the MCF project. Several video, audio and subtitle streams fit in one file, next to chapter markers and tags. It leaves the codec and the quality up to whoever made the file, and its registered media type is video/matroska. Films, fan releases and screen recordings are common sources of MKV files.

### Programs that open MKV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv lets you switch between the audio and subtitle streams while an MKV plays, and ffplay opens the file too.
- **Mobile:** on a phone, MKV plays in VLC for Android or VLC for iOS, depending on the streams inside.

### MKV and WMV compared

- **Container**: MKV is Matroska, built on EBML, and a WMV is an ASF container.
- **Streams**: an MKV can carry many audio and subtitle streams, while an ASF holds audio, video and other streams.
- **Codecs**: Windows Media Video versions 7, 8 and 9 appear in a WMV, whereas an MKV can wrap any codec.

FFmpeg works inside your browser tab, and the .wmv ending makes FFmpeg choose MS-MPEG4 version 3 video at about 200 kbit/s and Windows Media Audio version 2. The page also limits pictures to 1920 pixels on the long side and the rate to 30 frames a second, and it deinterlaces flagged frames. Without a track picker, FFmpeg decides which audio lands in the file. Play the WMV afterwards and check the language, the length and the picture.

### Other ways to convert MKV to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i film.mkv film.wmv` takes the Windows Media codecs from the .wmv ending.
- **FFmpeg with chosen streams:** `ffmpeg -i multilingual.mkv -map 0:0 -map 0:1 delivery.wmv` uses `-map` to name the video and audio streams that go into the WMV. Change the second index to pick another audio track when the MKV has several.
- **Prism for Windows:** add the MKV through Add File(s), set the Output Format to WMV, then click Convert. Prism lists MKV as an input when the Matroska DirectShow filter is installed.

### Problems with MKV files

- **Wrong language**: the page has no track picker, so choose the track with `-map` in FFmpeg.
- **Seeking is slow in the MKV**: missing or damaged cues make seeking harder, and they are stored apart from the media.
- **A stream cannot be decoded**: recognizing the Matroska container does not ensure that a player or converter can decode every codec inside it.

guide.title: Understanding MOV to FLV
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

Apple's QuickTime movie format, MOV, appeared in 1991 and reached Windows in 1994. QuickTime files are made of atoms, and programs may skip any atom they do not recognize. Inside, video may be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG, and audio AAC or uncompressed PCM. QuickTime was the starting point for the MPEG-4 file format, though the two are not interchangeable. Mac screen recordings are saved as MOV, and its media type is video/quicktime. Few browsers handle it well, and Apple now favors MP4 in its own tools.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay handles MOV through FFmpeg's demuxer, and mpv plays it on the desktop.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MOV when the necessary decoder is available.
- **Mobile:** Phones can use VLC, on Android or iOS, though decoding depends on the media inside.

### MOV and FLV compared

Macromedia, and Adobe afterwards, built FLV to serve video through Flash Player. Streaming was the aim, and the typical contents are H.263 or H.264 picture with MP3 or AAC sound. With Flash at end of life it is now a legacy format for older web video and archived Flash content. VLC media player, mpv and Adobe Media Encoder can open it.

This page encodes H.264 with a fast preset and AAC at 96 kbps, wrapped as FLV. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced. Any side beyond 1920 pixels gets scaled down, and a rate beyond 30 fps is thinned by dropping frames, which leaves the length unchanged. Smaller or lower-rate video is left alone.

### Other ways to convert MOV to FLV

- **Prism for Windows:** add the MOV, set FLV as the Output Format, glance at the Encoder Options and click Convert.
- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i take.mov -c:a aac -f flv -c:v libx264 take.flv` writes H.264 and AAC into FLV.

### Problems with MOV files

Codecs inside a QuickTime container may be missing from the editor you are moving to. A rename does not transcode the video or add the absent decoder, so a file that will not open under another extension still needs a real conversion.

guide.title: Understanding MOV and HEVC
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

Apple's QuickTime format stores media as tracks inside one container. A MOV can hold several kinds of compressed picture and sound, so two files that both end in .mov may need different decoders. A camera recording and an editing export are examples.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** to inspect the source clip first, mpv gives a choice of audio and subtitle streams, and ffplay opens MOV.
- **Windows and Mac:** Premiere imports a MOV once it has the decoder for the clip's codec.
- **Mobile:** MOV opens in VLC for Android and VLC for iOS once their decoders cover the codec inside.

### MOV and HEVC compared

MOV is a wrapper; HEVC, also called H.265, is a video codec. A MOV can already hold HEVC. The .hevc output holds pictures alone: no audio track, no container.

Here the video is always re-encoded. FFmpeg decodes the first video stream of the MOV, shrinks a picture whose long side tops 1920 pixels and holds the rate to 30 fps. Your browser's HEVC encoder produces the new pictures, and FFmpeg writes them as an Annex B stream. A new encode can lose detail. Copying an existing HEVC track avoids that, and the FFmpeg extraction method below does it.

### Other ways to convert MOV to HEVC

- **FFmpeg encoding:** `ffmpeg -i camera.mov -an -c:v libx265 encoded.hevc` creates new HEVC pictures: `-an` leaves out the audio and `-c:v libx265` selects the x265 encoder. The result is a new lossy encode.
- **FFmpeg extraction:** if the MOV already contains HEVC, `ffmpeg -i camera.mov -c:v copy -an extracted.hevc` copies the video stream without re-encoding it, which works only when that stream is already HEVC. `-an` again leaves out the audio.

### Problems with MOV files

**A decoder is missing:** a MOV may hold a codec that the destination editor lacks, so check the codec inside rather than the ending.

**Renaming is not converting:** a new filename ending leaves the video as it was and installs no decoder.

**A broken save:** a MOV whose write was cut off can be unusable, although fragmented output recovers in a different way.

guide.title: Understanding MOV and M4V
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

A MOV packages media using Apple's QuickTime structure. It can hold video, sound and other tracks, with different codecs permitted inside. A professional camera export and a small shared clip need not have similar sizes or decoding requirements just because both end in .mov.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows and Mac:** Premiere Pro can import MOV when it has the decoder the clip needs.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, with the right decoders built in, and mpv both play MOV.
- **Mobile:** On Android and iOS, the VLC apps handle MOV, depending on the media it contains.

### MOV and M4V compared

M4V is an extension for MPEG-4 container files. HandBrake's documentation says an M4V and an MP4 differ only in the extension. FFmpeg also has a separate raw MPEG-4 video muxer named m4v, which is not what this page makes.

The page runs one FFmpeg command: x264 at CRF 30 with the ultrafast preset, AAC at 96 kbps, and faststart. Both the video and the audio are encoded again, and nothing is copied from the MOV. A larger or faster clip comes out with a smaller frame or fewer frames per second than it went in, so keep the MOV when you need the full frame for editing.

A frame already under the cap is left unchanged. A test run showed the file written with the ipod muxer and an M4V brand.

### Other ways to convert MOV to M4V

- **FFmpeg explicit MP4:** `ffmpeg -i edit.mov -f mp4 -c:a aac -c:v libx264 movie.m4v` names the MP4 wrapper outright and encodes H.264 and AAC.
- **FFmpeg repackaging:** `ffmpeg -i edit.mov -c copy -f mp4 repacked.m4v` copies the streams without re-encoding, which works when the MP4 muxer accepts their codecs.

### Problems with MOV files

**No decoder in the editor:** QuickTime containers can use codecs that a destination editor does not have, and an M4V ending does not change that.

**A new ending is not a conversion:** swapping .mov for .m4v changes the name only.

**A cut-off save:** a regular MOV that stopped mid-write may not play at all, whereas fragmented output recovers in its own way.

guide.title: MOV background and MKV conversion
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

QuickTime, Apple's media technology, launched in 1991 and came to Windows in 1994. MOV is its file format. Inside, a QuickTime file is a series of objects called atoms, and a program may skip any atom it doesn't know. Video in a MOV may be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG, with AAC or uncompressed PCM audio. macOS saves screen recordings as MOV. Its media type is video/quicktime. iPhone recordings are typical MOV files, and video editing on macOS and professional video workflows use the format too.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay and mpv play MOV.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere Pro imports MOV.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player and Final Cut Pro open MOV.
- **Mobile:** VLC has Android and iOS apps for MOV.

### MOV and MKV compared

Matroska is a container built on EBML. It stores several video and audio streams in one file, along with chapters and tags, and it prescribes no single codec. Typical uses are Blu-ray rips, personal video libraries and files with more than one audio track. A MOV is a QuickTime container with its own atoms.

This page does not rewrap the streams, it re-encodes them. In your browser, FFmpeg encodes the video with x264 (preset ultrafast, CRF 32) and the audio as 96 kbps AAC. It also deinterlaces, caps the long side at 1920 px and the frame rate at 30 per second. Dimensions that are odd lose a pixel when rounded down.

### Other ways to convert MOV to MKV

- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i source.mov -c copy remuxed.mkv`. It rewraps without re-encoding, and works when Matroska accepts the streams.
- **FFmpeg, re-encode:** run `ffmpeg -i source.mov -c:a aac -c:v libx264 encoded.mkv`.

### Problems with MOV files

- **A player shows no picture**: the QuickTime container may use codecs your player lacks, so look at the codec, not the extension.
- **Renaming did not help**: a new ending cannot transcode the video or install its missing decoder.
- **The picture is smaller than the MOV**: the page caps size and frame rate.
- **You want the exact original quality**: the page cannot give it, so use the stream copy command above on your own computer.

A 10-bit HDR clip stays 10-bit, as H.264 High 10, which many players and browsers can't play, so try the MP4 before you share it.

faqs.question: Does the MP4 keep the sound?
faqs.answer: The audio track is re-encoded as AAC at 96 kbps. A MOV with no sound gives an MP4 with no sound.

faqs.question: How long does converting a MOV take?
faqs.answer: It depends on the video's length and your device. FFmpeg runs single-threaded in your browser with no time limit, so an hour of video can take a long while on a phone.

faqs.question: Why won't my MOV play in Chrome or on Windows?
faqs.answer: MOV is Apple's QuickTime format, and support outside Apple software is patchy. An MP4 with H.264 and AAC plays in every major browser and on almost any device.

guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

MOV is the QuickTime File Format. Apple introduced it with QuickTime in 1991 and brought QuickTime to Windows in 1994. Files end in .mov, or occasionally .qt, and are labeled video/quicktime. A MOV is a container: it holds separate tracks for video, sound, text and timecode, packed in building blocks called atoms. Software skips atoms it doesn't recognize, which let the format grow over the years without breaking older players.

The tracks inside can use many codecs. Common ones are H.264 or HEVC for everyday video, Apple ProRes and Motion JPEG for editing, and AAC or uncompressed PCM for sound. That range is why two MOV files can behave very differently: one plays everywhere, another needs special software.

You meet MOV files on Apple devices. The iPhone camera records them, a Mac saves screen recordings as MOV, and editing apps such as Final Cut Pro export them. They arrive by AirDrop, in cloud folders and as email attachments. Outside Apple's world they cause trouble, because browser support for MOV is limited, and Apple itself now generally uses MP4 for sharing.

### Programs that open MOV files

**Windows**

- VLC: plays most MOV files with its own codecs.
- Microsoft Clipchamp: imports a MOV and exports it as MP4.
- Adobe Premiere Pro: edits MOV footage, ProRes included.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player: Apple's built-in player and the format's home.
- Final Cut Pro: Apple's editor, which reads and writes MOV.
- VLC: a fallback for unusual codecs.

**Linux**

- VLC and mpv: free players that read MOV.
- FFmpeg: converts or inspects MOV files from the terminal.

**Web**

- Safari plays MOV. Other browsers are inconsistent, which is the usual reason to convert.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: MOV is the camera's own format, so Photos and Files play it.
- Android: VLC for Android plays most MOV files.

### MOV and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mov or .qt with video/quicktime; .mp4 or .m4v with video/mp4.
- **Origins**: MOV is Apple's own format. MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14, ISO/IEC 14496-14, published in 2003. Its structure, the ISO Base Media File Format, was derived from QuickTime, so MOV's atoms and MP4's boxes are the same idea, yet the two formats aren't interchangeable.
- **Typical codecs**: MOV is a common home for editing codecs such as ProRes. MP4 is the usual home of delivery codecs: H.264 video with AAC sound, and also HEVC, AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus.
- **Playback**: every major browser plays MP4. MOV plays reliably only in Apple software and in players like VLC.
- **File size**: the container hardly matters. The codec and bitrate decide size, so the same H.264 video takes the same room as MOV or MP4.

What this page writes: H.264 video with x264's ultrafast preset at CRF 32, AAC sound at 96 kbps, the picture capped at 1920 px on its longer side and 30 frames a second, interlaced footage deinterlaced, and the index moved to the front of the file so playback can start before it has fully loaded.

### Other ways to convert MOV to MP4

- **VLC (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: choose Media > Convert/Save, click Add and pick the MOV, choose an MP4 profile from the Profile menu, set the Destination file and click Start. VLC's guide doesn't list its profiles by name.
- **FFmpeg (command line)**: `ffmpeg -i input.mov -c copy output.mp4` moves the tracks into an MP4 without re-encoding, so nothing is lost. It fails when the MOV holds a codec MP4 can't carry; leave out `-c copy` to re-encode instead.
- **Microsoft Clipchamp (Windows, web)**: add the MOV to a Clipchamp project, use the Export button in the top-right corner and pick a resolution. The video is re-encoded and saved as MP4.

### Problems with MOV files

- **It won't play in Chrome, Firefox or a Windows app**: convert it to MP4 here, or open it in VLC.
- **An iPhone video shows sound but no picture on Windows**: the video is probably HEVC, which Windows needs Microsoft's HEVC Video Extensions to play. The H.264 MP4 made here doesn't.
- **A website or form refuses the upload**: many accept MP4 but not MOV. Upload the converted file.
- **The MP4 looks softer than the MOV**: this page favors speed and size. Keep the MOV as your master copy.
- **It takes a long time**: a big MOV is decoded and encoded on your own device. Plug a laptop in and leave the tab open.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: the MOV couldn't be decoded, which usually means a damaged or half-copied file. Copy or download it again.
- **You need a GIF or just the sound**: use the [MOV to GIF converter](/mov-to-gif/) or the [MOV to MP3 converter](/mov-to-mp3/).

faqs.question: Why does MP3 to AMR fail on this page?
faqs.answer: The page asks FFmpeg for the AMR-NB encoder libopencore_amrnb, and the FFmpeg build here does not include it. FFmpeg reports "Unknown encoder". A desktop FFmpeg built with that encoder can do the job.

faqs.question: What settings does an AMR voice file use?
faqs.answer: Narrowband AMR is a speech codec with eight bitrate modes. The page's command asks for 8,000 Hz, mono and 12.2 kbps, the top mode.

faqs.question: Will my music still sound like music as AMR?
faqs.answer: AMR is optimized for voice and compresses to very small files, so it suits voice messages and phone recordings, not songs.

faqs.question: Is AMR the same as AMR-WB?
faqs.answer: No. AMR-WB is its own codec, sampled at 16 kHz. A narrowband file cannot supply the wider range of a wideband source, and the storage signatures differ.

faqs.question: Can I just rename the MP3 to .amr?
faqs.answer: No. AMR and AMR-WB storage signatures differ, so changing an extension cannot change the encoded speech codec. The file must be encoded.

faqs.question: Which commands work on my own computer?
faqs.answer: On a desktop FFmpeg that has the encoder, the first method below sets the encoder, bitrate, sample rate and channel count. SoX can write AMR-NB when it has the optional AMR encoder. Both are shown below.

faqs.question: What does -C 7 mean in the SoX command?
faqs.answer: It selects AMR-NB mode 7, which is 12.2 kbit/s, the same top rate the page's command asks of FFmpeg. AMR-NB uses a fixed 8 kHz sample rate.

faqs.question: Will I lose quality going from MP3 to AMR?
faqs.answer: Yes. MP3 is already lossy, and AMR adds a second lossy stage at a far lower bitrate. Convert from your original recording if you still have it.

guide.title: About MP3 and AMR
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file

Short for MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III, MP3 is a lossy format that MPEG standardized under ISO/IEC 11172-3 with substantial help from the Fraunhofer Society, and it became the normal choice for music downloads, podcasts and portable players. It can be encoded at a constant or a variable bitrate, keeps song titles and other tags in ID3 structures, and has the media type audio/mpeg.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows and Mac:** Audacity edits it as an imported project.
- **Windows:** Windows Media Player for listening.
- **Linux:** ffplay, the FFmpeg player.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play it straight from a page.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and the Android port of mpv.

Apple Music and VLC media player also play MP3.

### MP3 and AMR compared

- **Purpose**: MP3 carries music. AMR is a speech codec standardized by 3GPP for mobile phone networks, optimized for voice.
- **Rate**: AMR narrowband spans 4.75 to 12.2 kbps at 8 kHz in 20-millisecond frames.
- **Origin**: AMR expands to Adaptive Multi-Rate and was standardized by ETSI for GSM speech, and 3GPP adopted it for third-generation cellular systems.
- **Storage**: RFC 4867 defines storage files as well as RTP transport, and the media type for narrowband AMR is audio/AMR.
- **Use**: AMR is used for voice recordings and voice messages on phones.

On this page the command asks FFmpeg for the libopencore_amrnb encoder at 8,000 Hz, mono, 12.2 kbps. That encoder is missing from this page's FFmpeg build, so no AMR file is written. Use the methods below on your own machine.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to AMR

- **FFmpeg with an external AMR-NB encoder:** `ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -codec:a libopencore_amrnb -b:a 12.2k -ar 8000 -ac 1 voice.amr`.
- **SoX with AMR-NB writing support:** `sox song.mp3 -t amr-nb -C 7 -c 1 -r 8000 voice.amr`.
- **Switch Sound File Converter:** use the Add button or File > Add to load the MP3, choose AMR in the Output Format field and click Convert.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **Import errors**: Audacity can refuse a malformed MP3 that another player still plays.
- **Tags replaced**: when you combine imports in a single Audacity project, tags from the latest file can replace earlier metadata.
- **Two lossy stages**: exporting another lossy file after editing an MP3 compresses the audio a second time, so keep the original.

faqs.question: How do I convert MP3 to CAF?

faqs.question: What is inside the CAF?

faqs.question: Will the CAF sound better than the MP3?

faqs.question: Why is the CAF bigger than the MP3?

faqs.question: Why would I use a CAF instead of the MP3?

faqs.question: Does a mono MP3 stay mono?
faqs.answer: No. The page always writes two channels, so a mono MP3 comes out as stereo.

faqs.question: Who opens a CAF?
faqs.answer: macOS handles it through Core Audio, and FFmpeg and ffplay read it on any system. Opening the container still leaves the audio codec to be decoded, which a given system might not support.

faqs.question: Is my file uploaded?
faqs.answer: No. FFmpeg runs in your browser, so the MP3 stays on your device.

guide.title: About MP3 and CAF
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3, formally MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, came out of Fraunhofer IIS and was standardized as ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993. It saves space by discarding what a hearing model says most listeners would not notice. Sampling can happen at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz, with the bitrate set between 32 and 320 kbps; tags such as titles live in separate ID3 blocks. Every major browser plays MP3, which makes it the usual way to share a recording and a poor one to edit.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** an MP3 imported into Audacity becomes a project you can edit, and ffplay plays one.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP3 directly, so nothing needs installing just to listen.
- **Mobile:** the Android port of mpv and VLC for Android handle MP3.

### MP3 and CAF compared

- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy, and a CAF written here holds uncompressed PCM.
- **Container**: CAF uses 64-bit offsets, so it can hold recordings larger than older containers allow.
- **Metadata**: MP3 keeps titles in separate ID3 blocks, while CAF has its own information chunks for descriptive text.
- **Channels**: CAF supports multiple channels with optional layout information.

Everything runs locally with FFmpeg and nothing is uploaded. FFmpeg decodes the MP3 and writes 16-bit little-endian stereo PCM at 44.1 kHz into the CAF. Those settings are fixed, so a mono or 48 kHz MP3 still comes out as two channels at 44.1 kHz. Decoding cannot restore sound the MP3 already discarded; the CAF only stops any further loss while you edit. Open the CAF in your editor afterwards and listen to the start and the end.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to CAF

- **FFmpeg PCM:** `ffmpeg -i listening.mp3 -c:a pcm_s16le -ar 44100 -ac 2 -f caf editing.caf` names the PCM encoder, the sample rate, the channel count and the CAF container, the same recipe this page runs.
- **Apple afconvert:** `afconvert -f caff -d LEI16@44100 -c 2 listening.mp3 editing.caf` is the tool built into macOS. The `-f caff` option selects CAF and `-d LEI16@44100` selects 16-bit little-endian samples at 44.1 kHz.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **Re-exporting as MP3 costs quality**: every export is another lossy pass, so keep the CAF as the working copy.
- **A damaged file will not import**: Audacity may refuse a broken MP3 that another player still handles.
- **Tags can be overwritten**: bring several files into one Audacity project and the newest file's tags may replace the earlier ones.

guide.title: About MP3 and CDDA
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, defined in ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993. It omits sound that listeners are unlikely to hear, and its bitrates run from 32 to 320 kbps. ID3 tags carry the title and artist inside the same file, and it is the usual way to share a recording on the web.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** an imported MP3 becomes an editable project in Audacity, while ffplay handles playback.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP3 directly.
- **Mobile:** a phone can play MP3 with either VLC for Android or the mpv port.

### MP3 and CDDA compared

- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy, while the result here is raw samples.
- **Header**: MP3 has frames and ID3 tags. The raw file has no header, so nothing in it states the rate or channel count.
- **Apple's .cdda**: on macOS the ending names AIFF-C audio, and a suffix alone cannot prove what is inside a file.

Nothing leaves your device, because FFmpeg runs inside the tab. The MP3 is decoded and the signed samples are written as a raw stream, always as two channels. The rate and sample format are fixed, so any player must be told them, and the output is not the AIFF-C file Apple software expects. Nothing is compressed, which is why the file is larger than the MP3. Open it as raw audio in an editor and listen before you rely on it.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to CDDA

- **FFmpeg raw PCM:** `ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -ar 44100 -ac 2 -c:a pcm_s16le -f s16le samples.cdda` writes headerless samples, the same layout this page writes.
- **FFmpeg WAV and Python wave extraction:** Convert to WAV with FFmpeg first (`ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -ac 2 -ar 44100 -c:a pcm_s16le prepared.wav`), then use Python's `wave` module to read the frames with `readframes` and write them out with no header. A short script can check the channels, sample width and rate with `getnchannels`, `getsampwidth` and `getframerate` before writing.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **A broken MP3 is rejected**: a malformed file can trigger an import error in Audacity even when other players cope.
- **Metadata follows the last import**: when several MP3s share one Audacity project, the latest file's tags can displace the earlier ones.
- **Going back to MP3 loses more**: encoding the raw samples again as MP3 is a new lossy step.

guide.title: About MP3 and MP2
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 comes out of Fraunhofer IIS, whose engineers worked with the wider MPEG audio group on it during the late 1980s. Two ISO standards cover it: 11172-3 from 1993 and 13818-3 from 1995. The allowed bitrate runs from 32 kbps at the low end to 320 kbps at the top, and the sampling rate is 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz. Music libraries, podcasts and portable players rely on it, and browsers all play it.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Linux:** Audacity brings MP3 audio into an editable project.
- **Mac:** ffplay, the FFmpeg player.
- **Windows:** Windows Media Player, or ffplay from the FFmpeg tools.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome decode MP3 inside the browser.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android and mpv for Android.

Audacity runs on Windows and Mac too. Apple Music and VLC media player also open MP3.

### MP3 and MP2 compared

- **Family**: both are MPEG audio. MP2 is Layer II of MPEG-1 Audio, finalized in 1992, and is specified by ISO/IEC 11172-3. It is the predecessor of MP3 Layer III.
- **Where used**: MP2 appears in digital radio and television broadcasting, DVD-Video soundtracks and Video CD production.
- **Media type**: the Library of Congress lists audio/mpeg for MP2 files.
- **Complexity**: MP2 has low decoding complexity.
- **Loss**: MP2 uses perceptual lossy coding, so decoding cannot recover the sound information it omitted. ISO/IEC 13818-3 later extended Layer II for MPEG-2.
- **Programs**: VLC media player, Audacity and foobar2000 open MP2, and FFmpeg's audio codec list includes MP2 decoding and encoding.

Here FFmpeg uses its mp2 encoder in your browser at 192 kbps, without video. The page passes no sample rate, channel count, stream mapping or tag option.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to MP2

- **FFmpeg, native encoder:** `ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -c:a mp2 -b:a 192k track.mp2`.
- **FFmpeg with libtwolame:** `ffmpeg -i track.mp3 -c:a libtwolame -b:a 192k track.mp2`. The libtwolame encoder is a TwoLAME wrapper, a separate implementation of MP2.
- **Audacity:** open the MP3, then pick File > Export Audio and select MP2 as the Format, set a bit rate from 16 to 384 kbps (the default is 160) and press Export.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **A failed import**: a damaged MP3 can make Audacity complain even when another player still opens it.
- **Overwritten metadata**: tags from the most recently imported file may replace earlier tags in a shared Audacity project.
- **Generation loss**: editing an MP3 and exporting a second lossy file adds another lossy encoding stage, so hold on to the original.

guide.title: Understanding MP3 and OGA
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3 uses MPEG Audio Layer III perceptual coding. It is common in downloaded music and spoken recordings because its lossy compression reduces storage. Earlier encoding losses remain part of the decoded sound; putting it into another file cannot reconstruct the original samples. Its metadata is stored separately from the sound, so tags travel as their own data.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity brings an MP3 into an editable project, and ffplay plays one.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome can play MP3 straight from a page, though the codec inside the file still counts.
- **Mobile:** MP3 opens in VLC for Android and in mpv for Android.

### MP3 and OGA compared

OGA names general audio in the Ogg container, not one codec. RFC 5334 keeps .ogg for Vorbis-only Ogg and gives .oga to the broader case, so a receiving application still has to decode whatever audio is inside. The same RFC gives .oga as the default extension for the audio/ogg media type.

This page runs FFmpeg with libvorbis at quality 5 and writes Ogg. The title and artist tags are copied as Vorbis comments, and any embedded cover picture is left behind. The result is a second lossy encoding with a quality-based variable bitrate, not a promised file size. The page never uses FLAC, though Ogg can carry that codec.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to OGA

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -c:a libvorbis -q:a 5 -f ogg song.oga` explicitly requests Ogg and Vorbis.
- **Audacity:** import the MP3 into a project and choose Ogg Vorbis as the Format in the File > Export Audio dialog. Its quality slider runs from 0 to 10.

### Problems with MP3 files

**The import errors out:** Audacity may refuse a damaged MP3 file even when a different player handles it.

**Tags get overwritten:** if you load more than one file into a single project, Audacity can replace the earlier tags with those of the newest file.

**A second lossy pass:** editing an MP3 and then saving another MP3 puts the sound through a second lossy encode, so keep the original.

guide.title: MP4 background and AIFF conversion
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is specified by Part 14 of MPEG-4, also numbered ISO/IEC 14496-14, and the first edition appeared in 2003. It is built on the ISO Base Media File Format, which grew out of Apple's QuickTime, and it is made of nested boxes. MP4 is a container: it commonly holds H.264 video with AAC audio, and it can also carry AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus. Video usually carries .mp4 or .m4v, while MPEG-4 files with sound alone commonly end in .m4a. Registered media types for it are video/mp4 and audio/mp4, and the big browsers can play it.

A screen recording, a phone clip or a downloaded video usually arrives as MP4. People convert it to AIFF to pull the sound out for an audio editor or a Mac workflow that wants uncompressed audio.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay can play MP4, and mpv plays it on desktop systems.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere takes MP4 in as an import when a suitable decoder exists.
- **Web:** Firefox plays MP4 media it supports, and Chrome handles supported MP4 audio and video pairings.
- **Mobile:** VLC apps for Android and iOS play MP4 on a phone.

### MP4 and AIFF compared

MP4 is a container for timed media, not a single audio codec, so its sound may be AAC or something else. The Audio Interchange File Format is an Apple audio wrapper descended from Electronic Arts' IFF family. It often carries uncompressed linear PCM samples, and AIFF-C extends it to compressed audio. Named chunks can hold author, copyright and annotations. Professional audio users choose AIFF for masters, and Audacity and Adobe Audition open it. Apple published version 1.3 of the AIFF specification on 4 January 1989, and the usual media types are audio/aiff and audio/x-aiff.

The page runs FFmpeg in your browser with `-acodec pcm_s16be -vn`: the video is dropped and the sound is written as signed 16-bit big-endian PCM. Decoding the sound to PCM doesn't restore detail removed when the MP4 was made.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to AIFF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mp4 -vn interview.aiff`. As an output option, `-vn` turns off video, so only the sound is written to the AIFF.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No sound to extract**: if the MP4 holds only picture, there is nothing to write into the AIFF.
- **A cut-off file will not play**: an interrupted MP4 recording can be unplayable because its packet index is kept as a single block.
- **No decoder for the contents**: understanding the MP4 wrapper is not enough if the player has no decoder for the codec used inside.
