guide.title: About SWF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an SWF file?

Flash animations, games and interactive pages were delivered as SWF files, a format that began at Macromedia. Adobe acquired Macromedia in 2005. The Library of Congress also records the expansion Small Web Format. A file can combine vector graphics, animation and bitmap video. Interactive content uses ActionScript alongside a timeline.

An SWF may refer to external media instead of holding every resource. Flash Player was discontinued by Adobe on 31 December 2020, which leaves SWF mostly as a format for old archived web content.

### Programs that open SWF files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- Ruffle: emulates Flash, and how well a file plays depends on the ActionScript features it uses.

**Windows and Linux**

- Lightspark: a Flash implementation that is only partial.

**Mac**

- Adobe Audition: imports SWF to extract audio from a video file if DLMS support is enabled; it does not run interactive Flash.

**Web**

- Ruffle's web player: runs Flash in a browser through WebAssembly, and some APIs are still missing.

### SWF and AVI compared

- **Purpose**: an SWF is a Flash container for vector animation, ActionScript and embedded media. An AVI holds interleaved video and audio.
- **Interaction**: an SWF can respond to clicks through ActionScript. An AVI plays from start to finish.
- **Container**: an AVI is RIFF-based and can hold many codecs. Microsoft introduced it in 1992.
- **Players**: AVI plays in QuickTime Player, in Windows Media Player and in VLC.

Here FFmpeg takes the media streams out of the SWF, encodes the video as MPEG-4 and the sound as MP3, and wraps them in an AVI.

### Other ways to convert SWF to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** run ffmpeg -i clip.swf -c:v mpeg4 -c:a libmp3lame decoded.avi. FFmpeg's SWF reader decodes audio and video tags and skips the rest, so ActionScript does not run.
- **JPEXS Free Flash Decompiler with FFmpeg:** on Linux, run ffdec -export movie extracted presentation.swf. The movie export defaults to FLV without sound. Then run ffmpeg -i extracted-movie.flv -c:v mpeg4 extracted-movie.avi, using the file name the export wrote.
- **Ruffle with OBS Studio and FFmpeg:** play the SWF in Ruffle, then in OBS add a Window Capture or Display Capture source, review the audio settings and begin recording. Then run ffmpeg on the recording file, for example ffmpeg -i your-recording -c:v mpeg4 -c:a libmp3lame performance.avi. This captures a game as it plays.

### Problems with SWF files

- **Nothing runs**: Adobe Flash Player no longer runs Flash content after its end-of-life block. Open the file in Ruffle.
- **A game acts differently**: some Flash APIs are missing from Ruffle, so visuals or behavior can change.
- **Parts are missing**: an SWF that refers to external media may not behave as intended when those files are absent.

faqs.answer: FFmpeg reads only the media embedded in an SWF, meaning video frames, sound and bitmaps, and not its vector shapes. An SWF can also point to media outside its own file, and a conversion cannot add what the file does not hold.

faqs.answer: Yes. It is the richer source for artwork and behavior. For playing it, Ruffle emulates Flash in a browser or on the desktop.

faqs.answer: No. The page never edits your file. It builds a new FLV in your browser and you download that copy, so the SWF stays as it was.

guide.title: Understanding SWF and FLV
guide.markdown:
### What is a SWF file?

SWF is the legacy Flash multimedia format associated with Macromedia and Adobe. It can combine vectors, bitmap media, timelines, and ActionScript-driven interaction. An animation, a video wrapper, and an interactive game can therefore share the extension while requiring different ways to interpret their contents.

### Programs that open SWF files

- **Web:** the Ruffle web player emulates Flash inside a browser with WebAssembly, leaving some APIs incomplete.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** to watch the SWF before converting, Ruffle emulates Flash, with results that depend on the ActionScript in use.
- **Windows and Linux:** Lightspark implements Flash only in part.
- **Mac:** Adobe Audition can pull the audio out of an SWF, though it is no interactive Flash runtime.

### SWF and FLV compared

FLV is a container from the Flash delivery ecosystem, usually holding H.263 or H.264 video with MP3 or AAC audio. An SWF can be an interactive program, and its ActionScript can even point to an external FLV.

This page runs FFmpeg to re-encode the SWF as H.264 video and AAC sound. Frames wider than 1920 pixels shrink, 30 fps is the ceiling for the rate, and odd edges lose a pixel.

### Other ways to convert SWF to FLV

- **FFmpeg direct encode:** `ffmpeg -i media.swf -c:v libx264 -crf 27 -f flv -c:a aac direct.flv` re-encodes the embedded media with CRF 27 where this page uses CRF 32, and with no size or rate cap.
- **FFmpeg compatible copy:** `ffmpeg -i media.swf -c copy -f flv copied.flv` skips the new encode when the extracted streams fit FLV.
- **FFmpeg lossless intermediate:** decode with `ffmpeg -i media.swf -c:v ffv1 -c:a pcm_s16le intermediate.mkv`, check that file, then encode it to FLV. The review stage costs disk space but no extra loss before the final encode.

### Problems with SWF files

**Flash Player is retired:** Adobe's end-of-life block stopped Flash Player from running Flash content.

**Ruffle differs:** Ruffle leaves some Flash APIs unimplemented, so an SWF may look or act differently.

**Assets are absent:** an intact SWF can misbehave when the external assets it needs are missing.

**Interaction cannot stay:** ActionScript controls do not survive conversion to video.

guide.title: SWF background and MOV conversion
guide.markdown:
### What is an SWF file?

SWF belongs to the Flash ecosystem. Macromedia created the format for Flash animations, games and interactive web content, and Adobe stopped supporting Flash Player on 31 December 2020. A file can combine timeline animation, vector shapes, compressed media and ActionScript code. Some SWFs hold a movie stream, while others draw their scenes from vectors and scripts, and a few carry both. That difference decides whether a media converter finds anything to extract.

MOV is a QuickTime movie container for timed media. It holds a linear recording of pictures and sound, so clickable Flash behavior and branching can't survive in it.

### Programs that open SWF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Ruffle, an emulator for Flash, plays SWF files, though some language and API features are still missing, and the JPEXS Free Flash Decompiler opens them too.
- **Windows and Linux:** Lightspark is an incomplete Flash implementation.
- **Web:** a web player from Ruffle emulates Flash in a browser through WebAssembly.

FFmpeg has an SWF demuxer that reads the media embedded in the file.

### SWF and MOV compared

This page does not render Flash. FFmpeg runs in your browser and reads only the audio and video embedded in the SWF. It doesn't run ActionScript or draw the vector animation, so a SWF without embedded video has nothing for it to read.

When there is media to read, the page encodes H.264 video with x264 and AAC audio at 96 kbps into a MOV, with the moov atom moved to the front (`+faststart`). The long side is capped at 1920 px, the frame rate at 30 per second, and sizes become even.

### Other ways to convert SWF to MOV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i archive.swf -c:a aac -c:v libx264 extracted-movie.mov`. Check the result by playing the MOV, since only embedded media can appear in it.

### Problems with SWF files

- **The MOV shows no scene**: the SWF draws its scene with Flash features and holds no video to read.
- **Buttons no longer work**: a movie plays straight through and keeps no interaction.
- **The animation does not look like the SWF**: only the embedded audio and video are read, never the vector drawing.

guide.title: About TIFF and GIF
guide.markdown:
### What is a TIFF file?

TIFF is a tag-based raster format that Aldus and Microsoft developed, with revision 6.0 published in 1992 and the specification now controlled by Adobe. It allows several compression methods and color representations, and one file may hold multiple images, which suits scanned document sequences. High-bit-depth imaging and preservation masters are established uses. The endings .tif and .tiff mean the same thing.

### Programs that open TIFF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** GIMP imports TIFF for editing. ImageMagick reads and writes it, and lets you choose the compression, strip or tile layout and byte order.
- **Mac:** Preview offers TIFF in the File > Export format list.

### TIFF and GIF compared

- **Palette**: a GIF picture is capped at 256 colors, whereas a TIFF can hold far more, so a photograph gets reduced.
- **Transparency**: GIF marks one palette color as transparent, with no partial transparency.
- **Images per file**: both can hold several images. A GIF plays them in sequence with a delay between each, while a TIFF scan keeps them as pages.
- **Compression**: GIF compresses with LZW, which is lossless, once the colors have been cut down.

On this page ImageMagick reads one picture from the TIFF and writes it as a GIF, with no quality setting. Every major browser displays GIF, but the GIF holds only a 256-color version of the scan, so keep the TIFF as your master copy.

### Other ways to convert TIFF to GIF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick 'scan.tiff[0]' cover.gif`. The number in square brackets picks the image from a multi-image file, counting from 0, so `[1]` is the second one.
- **IrfanView (Windows):** open the TIFF in IrfanView, which reads and saves both TIF and GIF, then use File > Save as and choose GIF as the output format.

### Problems with TIFF files

- **Several images in one file**: a TIFF can hold a whole sequence, and a tool that shows only one image hides the rest. Use software that exposes the full sequence.
- **A TIFF over about 4 GB**: classic TIFF uses 32-bit offsets, which limit it to roughly that size; BigTIFF extends the fields.
- **Unusual tags or profiles**: a reader may not understand every private tag, including some color-profile extensions.

guide.title: About TIFF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TIFF file?

TIFF stands for Tagged Image File Format. Aldus first published it in 1986, and the Library of Congress records Microsoft as a co-developer. The 6.0 revision dates from 1992, and Adobe holds the specification today. A file begins with II for little-endian or MM for big-endian byte order, and the specification sets no limit on how many images a file may contain. Tags make TIFF flexible: a single file can mix compression methods and color representations and contain more than one image.

You find TIFF in scanners and archives, in professional photography and print workflows, and in fax and document imaging. High-bit-depth work and preservation master files are established uses. The registered media type is image/tiff, and both .tif and .tiff extensions are in use.

### Programs that open TIFF files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- GIMP: imports a TIFF as an editable image, and each export format carries over only some of a project's properties.
- ImageMagick: reads and writes TIFF, including its compression, strip, tile and byte-order settings.

**Mac**

- Preview: File > Export lists TIFF as one of its formats.

### TIFF and WebP compared

- **Compression**: TIFF supports many methods, lossless or lossy, and WebP has its own lossy and lossless modes.
- **Pages**: a TIFF can hold multiple images. WebP can hold the frames of an animation.
- **Color and depth**: TIFF can store CMYK images and high bit depth.
- **Origin**: Aldus and Microsoft developed TIFF. Google released WebP in 2010, built on the VP8 video codec for lossy images.
- **Reach**: current major browsers support WebP.

This page reads one picture through ImageMagick and writes it as a WebP. It passes no quality setting.

### Other ways to convert TIFF to WebP

- **cwebp:** run cwebp -q 80 scan.tiff -o article.webp. Google's command-line encoder takes TIFF input, and -q sets the quality from 0 to 100.
- **ImageMagick:** run magick scan.tiff scan.webp. ImageMagick needs its WebP delegate library for this.

### Problems with TIFF files

- **Colors differ between programs**: private tags, including some color-profile extensions, are not understood by every reader.
- **A file approaches the limit**: classic TIFF uses 32-bit offsets, capping files at about 4 GB, a limit BigTIFF removes by widening them.

guide.title: Understanding TXT and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

TXT commonly identifies plain text: character data without a page-layout model or rich typographic instructions. The encoding determines how bytes become letters. A text editor supplies the font and display arrangement, so the same document can look different when opened with another editor or window width.

### Programs that open TXT files

- **Mac:** TextEdit creates, opens and saves plain text documents.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** to read the text before drawing it, Visual Studio Code and Vim both open plain text.

### TXT and JPEG compared

TXT records characters without layout, and the font and wrapping come from whatever opens it. JPEG records pixels with lossy compression. Rendering fixes the look of the text, including wrapping and font choice, and does not make it editable.

This page reads the file in the encoding it detects and draws it black on white in DejaVu Sans. It shows a limited number of lines, and a longer file stops with a note on the last line, so check the ending before sharing instructions or a transcript.

### Other ways to convert TXT to JPEG

- **ImageMagick:** `magick -background white -fill black -pointsize 20 -size 800x caption:@notes.txt notes.jpeg` wraps the file's text to 800 pixels. It needs an installed font, and some systems disable the `@file` form through a security policy. A trailing newline in the file adds a blank line.
- **GIMP:** choose Tools > Text, then pick the font from the list of installed fonts, and load the TXT with the folder icon in the Text Editor window and arrange it on the canvas. Export a .jpeg copy with File > Export As.
- **Inkscape plus GIMP:** type the text with the Text tool, set the font in Text > Text and Font, and export with File > Export PNG Image. Then open that PNG in GIMP and export a JPEG with File > Export As.

### Problems with TXT files

**Characters look wrong:** the wrong encoding can turn valid text into incorrect characters.

**Styling is gone:** a styled document loses its formatting once it is saved as TXT.

**No pictures or tables:** plain text cannot hold an image or table the way a word processor does.

faqs.question: Does enlarging the SVG keep it sharp?
faqs.answer: No. The letters are pixels inside the SVG, not paths or text drawn from fonts, so enlarging the SVG does not redraw them any sharper.

faqs.question: How are long lines wrapped?
faqs.answer: Lines break between words once they reach the picture's fixed width. A word too long for a line is broken inside the word.

faqs.question: Is there a limit on how much text fits?
faqs.answer: Yes. Beyond a fixed number of lines the text is cut off, the final line names the line where it stopped, and the page tells you it was cut.

faqs.question: Why do my accented letters look wrong?
faqs.answer: The page reads the file as UTF-8, or as UTF-16 when it starts with a byte order mark, and otherwise as Windows-1252. A file saved in another encoding shows the wrong characters, so save it as UTF-8 and try again.

faqs.question: Which font and colors does the picture use?
faqs.answer: Black letters on white, set in DejaVu Sans with a margin around the text. Scripts that font lacks, such as Chinese or emoji, fall back to your browser's sans-serif font.

faqs.question: Does it handle Hebrew and Arabic?
faqs.answer: Yes. When a line begins with a Hebrew or Arabic letter, it is drawn from right to left, and DejaVu Sans covers both scripts.

faqs.question: What happens to tabs and terminal colors?
faqs.answer: Tabs stop every 4 characters. Other control characters and terminal color codes are dropped, so only the readable text is drawn.

guide.title: TXT files and SVG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

Plain text is what a TXT file holds: characters with no fonts, styles or images. Any text editor opens it, which is why it turns up as notes, logs, readme files and configuration. It has no page layout either, so turning it into a graphic means choosing a font, a width and margins.

The one thing a TXT file does carry is a character encoding such as UTF-8. A receiving program reads the bytes through that encoding, so the same file can show correct text in one program and wrong characters in another.

### Programs that open TXT files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Visual Studio Code opens and edits text files.
- Vim edits plain text.

**Mac:**

- TextEdit works on plain text files. Converting rich text to plain text there removes its styles and formatting.

### TXT and SVG compared

A TXT file is text/plain, with no layout of its own. An SVG is XML with the type image/svg+xml, and it can describe shapes, text and embedded pixel images.

This page uses the embedded picture. It draws your text on a canvas in DejaVu Sans, black on white, at 16 px on 24 px lines with 32 px margins, wrapped at 800 px, and wraps the resulting PNG in an SVG. The SVG holds no text and no paths, so its words cannot be selected or searched.

### Other ways to convert TXT to SVG

- **LibreOffice Draw:** click the page, choose Insert > File, select the TXT and click Insert, then click OK in the Insert Text dialog. Choose File > Export, select SVG as the file type and save. SVG shows no options dialog on export.
- **ImageMagick with Inkscape:** run `magick -size 800x -pointsize 16 caption:@note.txt note.png` to draw the text file as a PNG. Import the PNG into Inkscape with File > Import, choose the embed option and save the result as SVG. This also gives pixels, not text.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Strange characters**: the encoding was guessed wrongly. Save the file as UTF-8.
- **Formatting disappeared**: plain text never held any. A TXT file keeps no formatting from a styled document.
- **An image or table is missing**: a plain text file has no place to hold a picture or a table.

guide.title: About video to GIF
guide.markdown:
### What is a video file?

A video file is a container with tracks inside. The container, such as MP4, MOV, WebM or AVI, decides how the tracks are packed and labeled. The codecs inside decide how the picture and sound are squeezed: H.264, HEVC, VP9 or AV1 for the picture, and AAC, MP3 or Opus for the sound. That is why two .mp4 files can play differently on the same device.

The picture track is a run of still frames, usually 24, 30 or 60 a second. Video codecs save space by storing most frames as changes from the ones before, so a long clip can still be small. A GIF has no such trick. Each frame is a separate picture, so turning video into GIF is really choosing which stills to keep and how to color them.

This page takes MP4, the most common video format, from phones, cameras, screen recorders and editors. Other containers have their own pages: [MOV to GIF](/mov-to-gif/), [WebM to GIF](/webm-to-gif/) and [AVI to GIF](/avi-to-gif/).

### Programs that play and trim video files

**Windows**

- Media Player: the built-in player for MP4 and most common video.
- Microsoft Clipchamp: trims clips and can export short ones as GIF.
- VLC: plays nearly any video, with its own codecs.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player: plays MP4 and MOV, and Edit > Trim cuts a clip down.
- iMovie: Apple's free editor for longer edits.

**Linux**

- VLC and mpv: free players.
- FFmpeg: cuts, scales and converts from the terminal.

**Web**

- Browsers: MP4 with H.264 plays in all the major ones.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: the Photos app trims a video in its editor.
- Android: Google Photos and most gallery apps can trim a clip before you share it.

### Video and GIF compared

- **Frames**: video often runs at 30 or 60 frames a second. This page keeps 15, so a 4-second clip becomes 60 images in the GIF.
- **Size of the picture**: the GIF is at most 480 px on its longer side, with both sides rounded down to an even number. A 1920x1080 clip comes out at 480x270.
- **Color**: a video frame can use millions of colors. A GIF image uses a palette of at most 256, so this page reads the whole clip first, builds one palette that suits it, then maps every frame onto that palette.
- **Compression**: video stores differences between frames. GIF stores each frame with LZW, which is lossless, but it can't predict motion, so a GIF is usually much larger than a video of the same length and size.
- **Sound**: video can carry it; GIF can't.
- **Playback**: a GIF starts by itself and needs no player, which is why chat apps, forums and email accept it where they block video. The GIF made here loops forever.
- **Media types**: video/mp4 for MP4; image/gif for GIF, a format CompuServe introduced in 1987.

### Other ways to convert video to GIF

- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: import the clip with File > Import > Video Frames to Layers, turn the layers into a frame animation in Window > Timeline, then export with File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy) and choose GIF. Photoshop reads MP4, MOV, AVI and MPEG when the right codecs are installed, and may not import a long video in full.
- **Microsoft Clipchamp (Windows, web)**: put the clip on a project timeline, press Export in the top-right corner and pick GIF. Clipchamp offers GIF only for videos up to 15 seconds long.
- **FFmpeg (command line)**: `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.gif` works, but its palette is a general-purpose one that isn't tuned to the clip. For truer color, make a palette from the clip first with the palettegen filter and apply it with paletteuse, the method this page uses. Frame timing in a GIF counts in hundredths of a second, so no delay can be shorter than 0.01 s.

### Problems with video to GIF

- **The page won't take your file**: it accepts MP4 only. Use the converter for your video's format.
- **The GIF is too heavy to post**: shorten the clip before converting. Every second adds 15 frames, so the file grows with the length.
- **Small text is unreadable**: the 480 px limit shrinks screen recordings a lot. Crop to the part that matters, or share the video instead.
- **Shading turns into dots or steps**: 256 colors per frame can't hold a smooth gradient. Clips with flat colors convert best.
- **It takes a long time**: FFmpeg runs on your device in a single thread. Keep the tab open, and on a laptop plug in.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: the video couldn't be read. Make sure it plays in your usual player; if it doesn't, the file is probably damaged or incomplete.
- **You wanted the audio**: a GIF has none. The [MP4 to MP3 converter](/mp4-to-mp3/) saves the sound instead.

guide.title: About VOB files
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

DVD Video Object is what VOB stands for. Producers of DVDs keep a disc's video, sound and menus in VOB streams, which are closely related to MPEG-2 program-stream material. One file can hold up to 1 GB.

A DVD backup commonly places those files in a VIDEO_TS directory. DVD authoring also needs companion IFO and BUP files that tell a player how the pieces fit together. People meet VOB when they rip a DVD into files.

### Programs that open VOB files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- VLC: can open DVD-Video discs and MPEG program-stream files.
- HandBrake: accepts VOB files as well as VIDEO_TS disc folders, so long as nothing on the disc is protected.

### VOB and AVI compared

- **Container**: a VOB is an MPEG-2 program stream. An AVI is RIFF-based, was introduced by Microsoft in 1992 and can hold many codecs.
- **Streams**: a VOB can carry several audio streams. An AVI interleaves video and audio.
- **Position on a disc**: VOB files sit in the VIDEO_TS folder alongside IFO and BUP files. An AVI stands alone.
- **Players**: AVI files open in Windows Media Player, in VLC media player and in QuickTime Player.

The page hands the VOB to FFmpeg, which writes MPEG-4 for the picture and MP3 for the sound inside an AVI container.

### Other ways to convert VOB to AVI

- **Avidemux:** open the VOB with File > Open and let Avidemux index it. Choose MPEG-4 ASP (Xvid) video, MP3 (LAME) audio and the AVI output format, then use File > Save > Save Video. The program's own tutorial recommends two-pass encoding.
- **FFmpeg:** run ffmpeg -i segment.vob -c:a libmp3lame -c:v mpeg4 segment-copy.avi. FFmpeg's format list includes MPEG-PS input, and both streams are encoded afresh.

### Problems with VOB files

- **A protected disc**: a VOB may be encrypted with CSS. HandBrake does not process copy-protected DVD sources.
- **A loose file does not make a disc**: one VOB on its own does not replace the whole DVD structure that authoring needs.
- **A clip from the wrong title**: one disc can hold several titles, so picking the wrong one gives you the wrong footage in the AVI.

guide.title: Understanding VOB to MKV
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

The letters stand for DVD Video Object, the container that holds a disc's video, sound, subtitles and menus. It is closely related to the MPEG-2 program stream, and CSS encryption may be applied. Copies of a disc usually sit in a VIDEO_TS folder next to IFO and BUP companion files, and a lengthy title is divided among VOBs of up to 1 GB each.

### Programs that open VOB files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC can play discs in the DVD Video layout along with MPEG program streams. HandBrake accepts either a single VOB or an entire VIDEO_TS folder, so long as nothing on the source is protected.

### VOB and MKV compared

Matroska is a free, open container with space for as many video, audio, picture and subtitle tracks as you like, plus chapters and metadata. Nearly any codec fits, so the contents decide how it plays. It suits Blu-ray rips and films with many soundtracks, WebM is a subset of it, and a VOB by contrast follows the DVD-Video layout.

Here the MKV holds H.264 picture and AAC sound at 96 kbps, made with a fast preset. Interlaced frames are cleaned up by the yadif filter. A picture over 1920 pixels on the long side is scaled down, motion above 30 frames per second is thinned to 30, and both dimensions end up even. Nothing is scaled up and no rate is raised.

### Other ways to convert VOB to MKV

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i title.vob -c:v libx264 -c:a aac title.mkv` writes H.264 and AAC into Matroska. Add `-map` options when a disc has several soundtracks.
- **HandBrake:** use Open Source to pick the VOB or the whole VIDEO_TS folder, choose a title with the Title control if the source holds several clips, set the container to MKV and encode.
- **Prism for Windows:** add the VOB, choose MKV as the Output Format, review Encoder Options and press Convert.

### Problems with VOB files

- A short result tends to mean one numbered piece was converted, so run all of them.
- A disc often holds several titles, and the wrong choice gives the wrong clip.
- One VOB on its own cannot stand in for the full DVD structure that authoring needs.
- Some MPEG-2 players ignore the subtitle streams of a DVD.
- HandBrake does not defeat copy protection of any kind, so a protected disc has to be handled with other software.

guide.title: VOB files and MOV output
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

VOB is the DVD Video Object. A DVD-Video disc keeps its video, sound, text overlays and menus inside VOB streams, which are based on the MPEG-2 program stream. A disc copy usually puts them in a VIDEO_TS folder next to companion IFO and BUP files, and a loose VOB does not replace that structure. A VOB file on a disc is limited to 1 GB, so a long film is split across several of them. People meet VOB files when ripping DVDs to files, and a disc can hold several titles, so choosing the wrong one gives the wrong clip.

### Programs that open VOB files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player reads DVD-Video media and MPEG program streams.
- HandBrake accepts VOB files as well as complete VIDEO_TS disc folders. Its input must be unprotected.

### VOB and MOV compared

A VOB is a DVD container with several audio and text-overlay streams, and some discs are encrypted with CSS. A MOV is Apple's QuickTime container, registered as video/quicktime, with the extension .mov or .qt. It holds video, audio, text and timecode tracks, and many codecs including H.264 and ProRes. The QuickTime format was the basis for the MPEG-4 file format, but MOV and MP4 are separate formats.

This page decodes the VOB and writes new H.264 video and AAC sound into a MOV, so it is not a copy of the DVD streams. Frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced. The picture may be 1920 px on its longer side at most, and the frame rate may be 30 fps at most.

### Other ways to convert VOB to MOV

- **FFmpeg, H.264 and AAC:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c:a aac -b:a 192k -c:v libx264 -crf 21 scene.mov` to re-encode both streams.
- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c copy scene-copy.mov`. Stream copy passes the packets through without decoding or encoding.
- **FFmpeg, ProRes:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c:v prores_ks scene-edit.mov` to encode the video as ProRes, one of the codecs a MOV can hold.

### Problems with VOB files

- **The clip is too short**: you chose one segment, or the wrong title on a disc with several.
- **No menus**: they are part of the DVD structure, which a loose VOB lacks.
- **Overlays missing**: a player that plays MPEG-2 video can still skip the DVD text overlays, which can be bitmap images rather than text.
- **A protected disc fails**: HandBrake does not process copy-protected DVD sources.

guide.title: Understanding VOB to MP3
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

VOB means DVD Video Object. Discs keep picture, audio, subtitles and menus inside these files, which are tied to MPEG-2 program streams. They are normally found in a VIDEO_TS folder beside IFO and BUP files. CSS may encrypt them, and with a limit of 1 GB per file, a long title runs across several VOBs.

### Programs that open VOB files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Either a lone VOB or a whole VIDEO_TS folder opens in HandBrake when the source has no protection. VLC plays DVD Video media as well as MPEG program streams.

### VOB and MP3 compared

A VOB bundles picture, sound and subtitles, and can carry several audio and subtitle streams. MP3 stores sound alone. Its full name is MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, and the ISO/IEC 11172-3 standard of 1993 grew out of work at Fraunhofer IIS and elsewhere in the MPEG audio group.

MP3 is lossy. A model of human hearing picks out sound that listeners are unlikely to notice, and that sound is thrown away. Song titles and other tags are stored apart, in ID3 structures, and every major browser plays MP3.

This page drops the video and encodes the soundtrack with the LAME encoder, asking for 192 kbps. Audio sampled under 32 kHz falls short of that rate and is written lower.

### Other ways to convert VOB to MP3

- **Switch:** add the VOB, set the Output Format to MP3, adjust Encoder Options if you like and press Convert. Switch lists VOB among its input formats.
- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i chapter.vob -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k chapter.mp3` does the same job as this page. Add `-map` when you need a specific audio track.

### Problems with VOB files

- If the audio ends early, you probably converted a single numbered piece; run the rest too.
- A disc may hold more than one title, so check you chose the right one.
- A lone VOB lacks the wider DVD structure that authoring relies on.
- A player may handle the MPEG-2 video but skip DVD subtitle streams.
- Protected discs need other software, because HandBrake leaves copy protection alone.

guide.title: WAV files and OPUS output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

The Waveform Audio File Format (WAV) wraps sound in RIFF chunks and was documented by Microsoft and IBM in 1991. It usually holds uncompressed linear PCM, so files are large but exact. Compressed encodings can appear inside too. Broadcast WAVE extends it with production metadata, and the Library of Congress also recommends WAV for digital audio collections. People use it for recording, editing and professional sound production.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Audacity brings in most WAV files, all PCM variants included.
- ffplay plays WAV, using the demuxer FFmpeg includes for it.

**Mobile:**

- Firefox for Android lists WAV among its supported audio types.
- VLC for Android is a free mobile media player.
- mpv for Android is the Android port linked by the mpv project.

### WAV and Opus compared

WAV is audio/wav or audio/x-wav and usually lossless, with a 4 GB file size limit. Opus is an open lossy codec from the IETF, defined in RFC 6716, which combines Skype's SILK and Xiph.Org's CELT. Ogg Opus supports descriptive metadata and seeking. Opus bitrates run from 6 to 510 kbit/s, it has low latency and it is royalty-free.

Here FFmpeg in your browser runs libopus on the WAV's sound with a 128 kbps target and compression level 4. Any picture stream is dropped. Nothing in the page lets you change the sample rate, channels or tags.

### Other ways to convert WAV to Opus

- **opusenc:** run `opusenc --bitrate 128 take.wav take.opus` from the opus-tools. It reads Wave input and writes Ogg Opus, with the bitrate in kbit/s.
- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i take.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 128k take.opus`. The libopus encoder is a wrapper that requires --enable-libopus.
- **Audacity:** choose File > Import > Audio and select the WAV. Then choose File > Export Audio, pick Opus as the format, name the file and export.

### Problems with WAV files

- **A recorder's WAV won't import**: it may use proprietary compression. Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library for such files.
- **Very large recordings**: they may need RF64 instead of the original size fields.
- **Tags differ**: INFO chunks and Broadcast WAVE store different information.

guide.title: Understanding WAV for WMA output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAV, or Waveform Audio File Format, is a RIFF-based wrapper for sound that Microsoft and IBM documented in their multimedia specification. Linear PCM is the usual payload, which makes files large but exact, though compressed encodings can appear too. Broadcast WAVE extends it with production metadata. Archives such as the Library of Congress recommend WAVE for collections. The usual media types are audio/wav and audio/x-wav.

### Programs that open WAV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity opens most WAV files, PCM variants among them, and ffplay plays them as well.
- **Web:** Firefox plays WAV directly, and so does Firefox for Android.
- **Mobile:** Phones can use mpv for Android or VLC for Android.

Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library when a recorder used proprietary compression inside the WAV.

### WAV and WMA compared

- **Container**: WAV is RIFF. WMA uses Microsoft's ASF container.
- **Compression**: WAV is usually uncompressed PCM. This page writes lossy WMA version 2.
- **Variants**: WMA has standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice codecs.
- **Size**: a WMA is usually much smaller than the WAV.
- **Media type**: WMA is commonly audio/x-ms-wma.

FFmpeg runs in your browser as WebAssembly and encodes the WAV with wmav2 at 192 kbps. The command sets no sample rate or channel layout.

### Other ways to convert WAV to WMA

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i rehearsal.wav -c:a wmav2 -b:a 192k rehearsal.wma`. This writes lossy WMA version 2.
- **Audacity:** open the WAV, then choose File > Export Audio and select WMA (version 2) Files (FFmpeg) from the format list. The FFmpeg library must be installed.

### Problems with WAV files

- **A very large recording**: past the 4 GB limit of RIFF's size fields it needs RF64, which not every tool reads.
- **A WAV that uses compression**: a recorder may have used proprietary compression inside the file, and Audacity needs its FFmpeg library to import it.
- **Metadata differs between WAVs**: the INFO chunks and the Broadcast WAVE extensions carry unlike information, so check which your file has.
- **The WAV is your only copy**: the WMA discards detail and cannot give the samples back, so keep the WAV.

guide.title: Understanding WebM for MKV output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebM file?

WebM is a royalty-free web video format, defined as a subset of Matroska. A typical file holds VP8, VP9 or AV1 pictures with Vorbis or Opus sound. Because WebM is a restricted flavor of Matroska, the jump to MKV is a change of container rules more than of family. Matroska itself can hold chapters, tags and many video, audio and subtitle streams.

### Programs that open WebM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay plays WebM through FFmpeg's decoders, and VLC reads Matroska-family media too.
- **Web:** Safari on macOS handles WebM that holds VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis sound. Chrome and Firefox play it directly.
- **Mobile:** The VLC apps on Android and iOS open WebM straight from the device.

What actually decides playback is the codec inside, not the file extension.

### WebM and MKV compared

- **Codecs**: WebM allows a short list of video and audio codecs. MKV does not prescribe a codec.
- **Tracks**: MKV holds many audio and subtitle tracks, plus chapters.
- **Media types**: video/webm for WebM, video/matroska for MKV.
- **This page's output**: H.264 pictures with AAC sound at 96 kbps.

FFmpeg running in your browser decodes the WebM and writes fresh H.264 with libx264, using CRF 32 and the ultrafast preset. It deinterlaces, limits the long side to 1920 pixels, holds output to 30 fps and trims odd dimensions to the next even number down.

### Other ways to convert WebM to MKV

- **FFmpeg remux:** run `ffmpeg -i browser.webm -map 0 -c copy wrapped.mkv`. `-map 0` takes every stream from the input and `-c copy` copies them without re-encoding.

### Problems with WebM files

- **A second audio or language track is missing**: no -map option is set, so FFmpeg's defaults choose the streams. Remux with -map 0 to carry every track.
- **A fast clip looks different**: the page limits the frame rate, so a faster source loses frames.
- **A very sharp source softens**: the page re-encodes and may resize, so remux if you need the original streams.
- **Seeking is slow**: if the cue index is missing, the player has less to go on and seeks less efficiently.
- **The WebM has an odd width or height**: H.264 needs even dimensions, so the page trims it.

guide.title: About WebP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP file?

WebP is an image format made by Google, announced in 2010 and released as open source. Its lossy mode borrows the key-frame coding of VP8, a video codec that began at On2 Technologies and that Google released as open source in May 2010. A lossless mode with its own method followed, and both modes can carry transparency and animation. Inside, a WebP is a RIFF container, the same wrapper WAV audio uses. RFC 9649, published in November 2024, documents the format and registers its media type, image/webp.

You mostly meet WebP on the web. Sites serve it because it is compact: Google reports lossy WebP files about 30% smaller than JPEG on average. So a picture saved from a browser often lands as .webp, and then an older editor, a print shop or an upload form that wants JPG won't take it. Animated WebP turns up too: WhatsApp's animated stickers, for example, are WebP files.

### Programs that open WebP files

**Windows**

- Photos and File Explorer: show WebP once Microsoft's WebP Image Extension is installed.
- Adobe Photoshop: opens and saves WebP from version 23.2; older versions need Google's WebPShop plug-in.
- GIMP: free editor that reads and writes WebP from version 2.10.
- XnView MP: viewer and converter, free for private use, that reads and writes WebP.

**Mac**

- Photoshop and GIMP: the same versions as on Windows.

**Linux**

- GIMP: the usual desktop choice for opening and exporting WebP.
- ImageMagick: converts on the command line when built with the WebP delegate library.

**Web**

- Chrome 17+, Edge 18+, Firefox 65+ and Safari 14+ display lossy WebP. Safari needs macOS Big Sur or later.

**Mobile**

- Android: decodes WebP from 4.0, and lossless or transparent WebP from 4.2.1.
- iPhone and iPad: Safari shows WebP from iOS 14.

### WebP and JPG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .webp and image/webp; .jpg or .jpeg and image/jpeg.
- **Compression**: lossy WebP codes the picture as a VP8 key frame, and lossless WebP uses LZ77, prefix codes and a color cache. Baseline JPEG is always lossy: 8x8 blocks, a discrete cosine transform, then Huffman coding.
- **Transparency**: WebP has an alpha channel in both modes. JPG has none.
- **Animation**: WebP can hold timed frames. A JPG is one still picture.
- **Color depth**: both store 8 bits per channel.
- **Largest image**: 16,383 pixels a side for WebP, 65,535 for JPEG.
- **Reach**: almost any program, camera, printer or photo kiosk reads JPEG. WebP needs a recent browser or one of the programs above.
- **Metadata**: both can carry an ICC profile, Exif and XMP.

What changes in this conversion is the move to a format without transparency or animation. The page decodes the WebP to pixels and writes a JPG at quality 0.85. See-through areas can't stay see-through, an animation gives its first frame, and the metadata stays behind in the WebP.

### Other ways to convert WebP to JPG

- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: open the WebP, choose File > Export > Export As, pick JPG and click Export. Version 23.2 or later opens WebP itself; older ones need the WebPShop plug-in.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: open the file in GIMP 2.10 or later, choose File > Export As, type a name ending in .jpg and click Export.
- **ImageMagick (command line)**: run `magick input.webp output.jpg`. The build must include the WebP delegate library.

### Problems with WebP files

- **Double-clicking does nothing on Windows**: install the WebP Image Extension from the Microsoft Store, or drag the file into a browser window.
- **A site or form rejects it**: convert it to JPG here, or to PNG with the [WebP to PNG converter](/webp-to-png/) when transparency must survive.
- **A renamed file still fails**: changing .webp to .jpg leaves WebP data inside, and strict programs check the data. Convert the file instead.
- **Only one frame came out**: a JPG can't animate, so an animated WebP gives its first frame. Keep the WebP if you need the motion.
- **"Image decode failed."**: the browser couldn't read the file, usually because it is damaged. Download it again from where you found it.
- **The JPG looks soft or blotchy**: a lossy WebP has already lost some detail, and the JPG is compressed again on top. Start from the largest, least compressed copy the site offers.

guide.title: WMA files and M4A output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMA file?

Microsoft's Windows Media Audio is a family of codecs, kept in the ASF container. The .wma extension separates audio-only files from other ASF content. Variants include standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice, and WMA 9 supports variable bit rate. The usual media type is audio/x-ms-wma. People use it for delivering music and sometimes for intermediate audio storage.

### Programs that open WMA files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player supports ASF/WMA input and carries multiple Windows Media Audio decoders.
- Audacity can read unprotected WMA, provided the optional FFmpeg library is added.
- FFmpeg's support matrix covers decoding the WMA 1 and WMA 2 codecs, as well as Pro, Voice and Lossless.

**Windows:**

- Adobe Audition imports WMA only with DLMS Format Support switched on.

### WMA and M4A compared

WMA is a codec family, lossy except for the Lossless variant. Apple adopted the M4A extension, used for MPEG-4 files with audio only, for its unprotected music files. Most M4A files contain AAC, a lossy codec defined in MPEG-4 Part 3 that aims for better sound than MP3 at a comparable bitrate. Apple used it for songs sold through iTunes. The media type is audio/mp4. Android plays AAC in .m4a files, and the major browsers play AAC inside MP4.

This page decodes the WMA and encodes AAC at 192 kbps with FFmpeg in your browser. Picture streams are left out.

### Other ways to convert WMA to M4A

- **FFmpeg, AAC:** run `ffmpeg -i library.wma -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k listening.m4a`. The `-vn` flag drops video streams, and the output is encoded afresh with loss.
- **Audacity:** with the optional FFmpeg library installed, open the WMA and use File > Export Audio with the M4A(AAC) Files FFmpeg format.

### Problems with WMA files

- **Audacity can't import it**: the optional FFmpeg library is missing, or the file is protected.
- **One program plays it, another doesn't**: an application may decode one WMA codec yet fail on another, because the .wma name does not reveal the variant inside.
- **A protected file**: Audacity cannot import protected WMA through its FFmpeg library.
- **Check the result**: play the M4A before deleting the WMA, since AAC discards detail from the decoded sound.

guide.title: About WMV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMV file?

WMV stands for Windows Media Video. Microsoft developed the family of codecs behind it, and a .wmv file stores the Windows Media content in the ASF container. WMV files use one of the Windows Media Video codecs, version 7, 8 or 9. It was a common choice for early Windows video, screen captures and Windows Media streams. The Library of Congress calls it often a final delivery format, and lists Windows Media Player and Windows Media Center among the programs that play it.

Microsoft designed ASF to keep media streams synchronized, whether they sit in a file or travel over a network. Audio and video streams fit in one container, which works from a local disk and from an HTTP server alike. The media type video/x-ms-wmv is the one the Library of Congress lists as commonly used, though IANA has not registered it.

### Programs that open WMV files

**Windows, macOS and Linux**

- VLC media player: reads ASF/WMV files and decodes Windows Media Video in versions 1, 2 and 9.
- FFplay: plays WMV with FFmpeg's decoders.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android: includes the desktop player's decoding features.
- VLC for iOS: opens local media in VLC's own player, not the system player.

### WMV and MPG compared

- **Container**: a WMV is an ASF file. An MPG is an MPEG program stream.
- **Video codec**: WMV uses a proprietary Microsoft codec. MPG carries MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 video.
- **Compression**: both are lossy, and both are legacy formats.
- **Background**: MPG served as the standard for VCD and DVD video.
- **Players**: MPG files play in QuickTime Player, VLC media player and Windows Media Player.

Here FFmpeg decodes the WMV and encodes MPEG-2 video with MP2 sound into an MPG.

### Other ways to convert WMV to MPG

- **FFmpeg:** run ffmpeg -i legacy.wmv -c:a mp2 -c:v mpeg2video legacy-review.mpg. FFmpeg's format list includes ASF input, and the video is encoded anew.

### Problems with WMV files

- **Opens, but not fully**: a player may understand the ASF wrapper yet lack a codec for what is inside.
- **Quality is not set by the extension**: how a WMV looks depends on its codec and compression settings.

guide.title: WPG files and JPG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WPG file?

WPG means WordPerfect Graphics, the graphics format of the WordPerfect word processor. It belongs to the WordPerfect graphics family and was used for clip art and legacy office graphics. Its files may hold vector drawing objects, bitmap data or both, and Corel describes a palette of up to 256 selected colors. Corel separates version 1.0, which targets WordPerfect 5.1 and earlier, from version 2.0, which targets WordPerfect 6 and newer.

### Programs that open WPG files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ImageMagick can read WPG images.
- XnView MP reads WPG too, and private or educational use costs nothing.

**Windows:**

- CorelDRAW imports WPG drawings through File > Import.
- Corel PHOTO-PAINT can open a WPG as a new image or bring it into one that is already open.

### WPG and JPG compared

A WPG may be vector or raster. A JPG is a lossy raster format for photographs, defined by ISO/IEC 10918-1, with no alpha channel, and .jpg and .jpeg are the same format. Any vector structure is lost in the move to JPG.

Here ImageMagick, running in your browser, reads one image from the WPG and writes the JPG. Only the bitmap records are drawn, and vector records are skipped. The page passes no quality setting. Beyond roughly 537 megapixels the picture is declined as too big. A batch gives one JPG per WPG.

### Other ways to convert WPG to JPG

- **CorelDRAW:** choose File > Import, select the WPG file type, click Import and click the page to place it. Then choose File > Export, pick JPG in the Save as type list and click Export. Corel lists limitations for WPG import.
- **LibreOffice Draw:** open the WPG, which Draw lists among its graphics formats, then choose File > Export and pick JPEG.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick illustration.wpg illustration.jpg`. ImageMagick lists WPG as a format it reads.

### Problems with WPG files

- **Elements missing after import**: CorelDRAW keeps embedded WMF and EMF graphics but can discard other embedded elements, and it documents that Graphics Text Type 2 is not supported.
- **Wrong version**: WPG 2.0 is not suitable when the destination needs WordPerfect 5.1 compatibility.
- **This page can't convert the drawing**: it was made only of vector objects, which the reader here skips. Export from CorelDRAW or LibreOffice Draw instead.

guide.title: XCF files and SVG output
guide.markdown:
### What is an XCF file?

GIMP, the GNU Image Manipulation Program, saves its working images as XCF. It keeps layers, channels, paths and selections so an image can be edited again, and it retains transparency rather than only a flattened picture. The undo history is not saved. GIMP's Save writes XCF, while other formats go through Export, and GIMP does not position XCF as an interchange format.

### Programs that open XCF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- GIMP is the native project editor and preserves the working image when saved as XCF.
- ImageMagick reads XCF, though you should not assume third-party rendering reproduces every GIMP feature.

### XCF and SVG compared

An XCF is a layered, lossless working file. An SVG is an XML vector format with the type image/svg+xml, though it can also embed pixel images.

This page reads one picture from the XCF with ImageMagick and embeds it in an SVG as a PNG, so no paths are created and nothing in the SVG can be edited as a shape. Layers are not written out one by one. The page turns away anything above about 537 megapixels. A batch of XCF files is processed in turn, one SVG per file.

### Other ways to convert XCF to SVG

- **GIMP path export:** open the XCF in GIMP, choose Windows > Dockable Dialogs > Paths, right-click the path you want and pick Export Paths, then save the file. GIMP saves the path in SVG format.
- **GIMP and Inkscape wrapper:** in GIMP choose File > Export As and export a PNG. Open Inkscape, bring the PNG in through File > Import with embed selected, and save it as SVG. The result keeps pixels instead of vector shapes.
- **GIMP and Inkscape tracing:** export the picture as PNG in GIMP and import it into Inkscape. With the Selector tool on the image, open Path > Trace Bitmap, adjust the options, preview with Update and accept with Ok. Expect the trace to differ from the original.

### Problems with XCF files

- **A viewer can't open it**: most ordinary image viewers cannot read XCF, so export a display copy from GIMP.
- **Flattened exports lose layers**: a flattened export cannot carry every project property, so the XCF is the file to edit later.
- **A save warning after export**: an export leaves the XCF itself unsaved, so GIMP may still ask about saving on close.
- **Rendering differs from GIMP**: another program that reads XCF may not reproduce every GIMP feature.

guide.title: Understanding XLSX for PNG output
guide.markdown:
### What is an XLSX workbook?

Microsoft Excel saves workbooks as XLSX. Inside the file is a ZIP archive of Open Packaging Conventions parts, many written in XML, and the registered media type is application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet. It cannot store VBA code, so macro workbooks use a different format. A PNG, by contrast, freezes a view into pixels you can paste into a slide or an email.

### Programs that open XLSX files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** LibreOffice Calc opens XLSX.
- **Windows and Mac:** Microsoft Excel opens it as well.
- **Mac:** Apple Numbers imports .xlsx spreadsheets for editing.
- **Linux:** Gnumeric reads it as well.
- **Web:** Google Sheets and Excel for the web open it in a browser.
- **Mobile:** Numbers for iPhone and Excel for Android and iOS cover phones.

### XLSX and PNG compared

- **Content**: XLSX holds cells, formulas and charts. PNG holds only pixels.
- **Editing**: you can sort and recalculate a workbook. You cannot edit a PNG cell.
- **Here**: the PNG is a table drawn from values, with Excel's number, date and percentage formatting applied.
- **Left out**: charts, pictures, comments and colors.

The workbook is read in your browser, and each visible sheet becomes an image on a canvas of up to 4096 pixels per side. At most 100 sheets are drawn, and only the first 500 rows with values are kept. Nothing is uploaded.

### Other ways to convert XLSX to PNG

- **LibreOffice Calc:** open the workbook in Calc and use ScriptForge's Calc service, whose `ExportRangeToFile` accepts png as the image type. For example: `doc.ExportRangeToFile("Sheet1.A1:F20", "/tmp/range.png", "png")`. Hidden rows and columns are not exported.
- **Numbers and Preview:** open the workbook in Numbers, choose File > Export To > PDF, open the PDF in Preview, then use File > Export and pick PNG from the Format pop-up.

### Problems with XLSX files

- **A number looks different**: the image shows the cell's format, such as a percentage or date, not the raw stored value.
- **Rows are missing**: the note on the image says how many rows were shown.
- **A sheet is absent**: it was hidden or held no values.
- **An old or protected file is refused**: save it as an unprotected .xlsx first.

faqs.question: Can you convert XML to PDF?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a listing. The PDF shows your XML's content, one line a node, with each level of nesting indented two columns further, up to 20 levels. It is not the file styled by a stylesheet.

faqs.question: How do I convert XML to PDF?
faqs.answer: Choose one or more XML files above. Each is read in your browser and saved as a PDF named after the file, and each PDF downloads on its own.

faqs.question: What size are the PDF pages?
faqs.answer: A4 portrait with 3/4 inch margins, in 10 pt type: 61 lines a page and 81 characters a line in Courier. A longer line wraps. No header, footer or page numbers are added.

faqs.question: Why does it say my XML isn't well-formed?
faqs.answer: The file broke XML's rules, for example an unclosed tag, an unquoted attribute value or a second root element. The message gives what the parser found and the line and column where it stopped, so you can fix the file and convert it again.

faqs.question: What happens to entities and the DOCTYPE?
faqs.answer: XML's five built-in entities and character references are shown as the characters they stand for. Any other entity is shown as written, never expanded or fetched, so a file that refers to other files converts like any other and loads nothing.

faqs.question: Which characters can it show?
faqs.answer: Text that is all Windows-1252 characters is set in Courier. Anything else is set in DejaVu Sans, embedded in the PDF, which covers scripts such as Arabic and Hebrew. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Indic and Thai characters and emoji are refused, with the characters named, rather than saved as blank boxes.

faqs.question: Can it turn an e-invoice or an XSL-FO file into a formatted document?
faqs.answer: No. It lists any XML file's content, but it doesn't apply an invoice's layout or an XSL-FO or XSLT stylesheet.

faqs.question: How large a file can I convert?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 MB, making up to 2,000 pages. A larger file is refused with a message saying which limit it passed.

infoArticle.title: About YouTube transcription
infoArticle.markdown:
YouTube to Transcript transcribes speech from audio or video files. Uploaded files are processed in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser for transcription. YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud, and other webpage links are not supported right now. The speech model downloads on first use and runs locally.

This tool is best for interviews, meetings, lectures, and voice notes. Larger files take longer to process and may use more memory.

**Why use this tool**

- Handles uploads or direct links to audio and video files.
- Creates a plain text transcript you can edit or share.
- Works with common audio and video formats.

faqs.question: Do my files get uploaded?
faqs.answer: Uploads are processed locally in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser. The model files are downloaded when needed.

faqs.question: Which file types are supported?
faqs.answer: Common audio and video formats like MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, and M4V.

faqs.question: Can I use YouTube or SoundCloud links?
faqs.answer: Not right now. YouTube, SoundCloud, TikTok, and other webpage links are not supported. Upload the audio or video file, or paste a direct link to one.

faqs.question: Why is the first run slower?
faqs.answer: The speech model downloads the first time you run the tool. After that it is cached for faster use.

faqs.question: What does the output look like?
faqs.answer: You get a plain text transcript (.txt) that you can download or copy.
